About the former, Acts 8: Peter and John prayed for the believers in Samaria that they might receive the Holy Spirit. For the Spirit had not yet fallen on any of them, but they had only been baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus. Then they laid their hands on them, and they received the Holy Spirit. A similar passage is found in Acts 19. About the latter is that in 1 Timothy 4: "Do not neglect the gift that is in you, which was given to you through prophecy, with the laying on of hands by the authority of the priesthood," that is, of the elders. 2 Timothy 1: "I remind you to stir up the gift of God which is in you through the laying on of my hands."

units.la: Ex quibus locis animaduertere licet, qui mos olim fuerit ordinandi aliquos ad publicum ministerium. Conuocata multitudine, aliqui e primoribus seu publicis ministris iubebant circumspici a multitudine, num quos viros scirent spectatae probitatis, plenos spiritu Sancto & sapientia (sic enim habemus Actorum cap.6.) quibus ministerium publicum delegari posset. Vbi qui tales erant a multitudine designati, inquirebatur diligenter de vita & doctrina, & breuiter, num eiusmodi in illis virtutes eminerent, quales in episcopis seu diaconis requiri praescribit Apostolus secunda epistola ad Timothei capite tertio, & ad Titum primo. Cuius rei tam habebatur olim diligens ratio, (vtreferente id Ælio Lampridio in vita Alexandri Seueri) publice figeretur charta, qua monebantur, si qui possent proferre in medium, quod eum, qui designatus esset a multitudine, impediret ab ordinatione & promotione. Deinde vero reperti idonei publice coram ecclesia statuebantur, coram senioribus seu toto sacerdotio, & oratione facta, (sicut dicitur Actorum 6.) imponebantur illis per seniores manus: qua re declarabantur publice idonei, & legitimam potestatem exercendi munus illud accipiebant, omnesque eos pro legitimis ministris agnoscebat. Haec prima, simplicissima, atque optima ordinandi ministros ecclesiarum ratio. Quae postea addita obseruata, fuerint, licet ex patrum scriptis colligere. Quae postremis temporibus excogitata sunt, ab illis puto excogitata, quibus animus magis versabatur circa ceremonias Iudaicas, quam circa euangelicam simplicitatem. Caeterum valde necessarium est, rudes instituí ac doceri de hac ordinatione ecclesiastica. Oportet enim sciant, legitimos esse ministros, a quibus instituuntur, & sacramenta suscipiunt: oportet in honore habeant & ministerium & ipsos ministros.
units.tr: From these passages we may observe what custom there once was for ordaining certain men to the public ministry. The multitude being called together, some of the leading men or public ministers ordered the people to look round and say whether they knew any men of proven integrity, full of the Holy Spirit and wisdom (for so we have it in Acts chapter 6), to whom the public ministry could be committed. Where such men had been designated by the multitude, they were carefully examined as to their life and teaching, and briefly as to whether such virtues stood out in them as the Apostle prescribes to be required in bishops or deacons, in his second letter to Timothy chapter 3 and in Titus chapter 1. So careful was this matter once considered (as Aelius Lampridius reports in the life of Alexander Severus) that a notice was publicly posted inviting anyone who could bring forward something that would hinder the man designated by the multitude from being ordained and promoted. Then, when men found fit were publicly set before the congregation, before the elders or the whole priesthood, and prayer having been made (as is said in Acts 6), hands were laid on them by the elders. By this act they were publicly declared fit and received lawful authority to exercise that office, and everyone acknowledged them as lawful ministers. This was the first, simplest and best method of ordaining ministers of the churches. What was later added and observed may be gathered from the writings of the Fathers. What was devised in later times, I think, was devised by those whose minds were more occupied with Jewish ceremonies than with evangelical simplicity. Yet it is very necessary that the untaught be instructed and taught about this ecclesiastical ordination. For they ought to know that those who instruct them and administer the sacraments to them are lawful ministers; they ought to hold both the ministry and the ministers themselves in honour.

units.la: Quando non potest fieri, vt in religione proficiant, qui legitimos ministros, vel ipsum ministerium quoquo modo contemnunt. Sicut in discendis bonis artibus, primus gradus est amare & bene sentire de eo, quem audis, profiteri: ita primus gradus ad proficiendum in sana doctrina est, publicos doctores ecclesiae iusto honore prosequi. Reuera autem quod ritus ille apostolicus ordinandi ministros sit omissus, & in quibusdam locis inanes, & nihil doctrinae aut grauitatis habentes suffectae ceremoniae: in quibusdam vero nullo ecclesiae expectato iudicio, vnius tantum potentis requiritur sufragium, qui, quem placet, etiam idoneum praeficit, puto in causa esse, quod ministerium publicum passim contemnatur. Quod si simplex & apostolica ordinandi ratio reduceretur, credo rediret & ministris suus honos & autoritas.
units.tr: It cannot happen that those who despise lawful ministers, or the ministry itself in any way, make progress in religion. As in learning the liberal arts the first step is to love and think well of the one whom you hear, and to profess it, so the first step toward progress in sound doctrine is to honour the public teachers of the Church with due respect. Indeed, that this apostolic rite of ordaining ministers has been dropped, and in some places ceremonies have been substituted that are empty and have no teaching or dignity, while in other places, without any judgment of the Church, the vote of one powerful man alone is required, who appoints whomever he pleases, even if he is unfit, I think is the cause of the public ministry being despised everywhere. If the simple and apostolic method of ordination were restored, I believe the ministers would regain their honour and authority.

units.la: Certum est, hac ratione doctrina ipsa haberetur maiori in precio, omnes paratires redderentur ad obediendum: denique vniuersa doctrina euangelica conseruari posset. Nam ad hunc locum de impositione manuum pertinet simul doctrina de potestate ecclesiae, de ligando ac soluendo, de excommunicatione, item de ceremonijs ac ritibus, qui ad bonum ordinem conseruandum in ecclesia instituuntur. De quibus omnibus conuenit, eos, qui iam sacramentis atque doctrina sunt imbuti, rectius edoceri, iuxta Scripturas & mandata Christi, quae de his extant. Deligando quidem & soluendo, deque excommunicatione Matthaei capite decimooctauo, prima epistola ad Corinthios capite quinto. Ephesiorum quinto, prima Timothei quinto, ad Titum tertio, ista vero tradita esse olim rudibus in primitiua ecclesia, liquet ex epistolis ad Corinthios, item ex Actis, &c. Grauem censuram exercebant Apostoli, ita vt omnes eorum potestatem formidarent & reuererentur.
units.tr: It is certain that by this method doctrine itself would be held in greater esteem, all would be made readier to obey, and in the end the whole evangelical doctrine could be preserved. For to this place about the laying on of hands pertain at the same time the doctrine of the power of the Church, of binding and loosing, of excommunication, and likewise of the ceremonies and rites that are instituted to preserve good order in the Church. Concerning all these things it is agreed that those who are already imbued with the sacraments and doctrine should be taught more correctly, according to the Scriptures and the commands of Christ that exist concerning them. On binding and loosing, and on excommunication, see Matthew chapter 18, 1 Corinthians chapter 5, Ephesians chapter 5, 1 Timothy chapter 5, Titus chapter 3. That these things were once handed down to the untaught in the primitive Church is clear from the letters to the Corinthians, and likewise from the Acts, etc. The Apostles exercised a grave censure, so that all feared and revered their authority.

units.la: Et resurrectionem mortuorum) Sextum Fundamentum, euangelicae doctrinae proprium, quod patres ab initio mundi, & prophetae, quotquot spiritu Dei afflati fuerunt, confessi sunt: eoque maiori diligentia tradendum rudibus, quo videtur ab omni humana philosophia alienius, & prae caeteris religionis nostrae articulis hostilius ab aduersarijs impugnatum. Nam apud Iudaeos habentes legem & prophetas, Saducaei ausi sunt negare resurrectionem, &c. Item Epicuraei, postea Valentinus. Sed praeterea, cùm ad consolatione conscientiarum in aduersis, maximè in metu mortis, item in ferenda morte amicorum: item ad confirmationem nostram de salute & gloria per Christum nobis parta, nihil certius proponi queat, quàm quòd Christus, sicut mortuus est propter peccata nostra, ita quoque resurrexerit propter iustificationem nostri: quodque exemplo & virtute resurrectionis illius nos itidem debeamus aliquando resurgere: merito hoc fundamentum, ut multò saluberrimum rudibus in Christo statim proponitur. Vt non dicamus, quòd haec doctrina de resurrectione nos ad contemptum rerum terrenarum adducere, à perpetratione malorum auocare queat. A Deo autem ordinata est haec resurrectio, ut totus homo, hoc est, anima cum corpore aeternam gloriam accipiat.
units.tr: And the resurrection of the dead. The sixth foundation, proper to evangelical doctrine, which the Fathers from the beginning of the world, and the prophets, all who were inspired by the Spirit of God, confessed; and it must be taught to the untaught with all the greater care because it seems most alien to all human philosophy and, above the other articles of our religion, is most hostilely assailed by our adversaries. For among the Jews, who had the Law and the Prophets, the Sadducees dared to deny the resurrection, etc. Likewise the Epicureans, and later Valentinus. Moreover, since nothing more certain can be put forward for the consolation of consciences in adversity, above all in the fear of death, likewise in bearing the death of friends, and likewise for our confirmation concerning the salvation and glory won for us through Christ, than that Christ, as he died for our sins, so also rose again for our justification, and that by the example and power of that resurrection we too ought at some time to rise again, this foundation is rightly proposed at once to the untaught in Christ, as most wholesome. Not to mention that this doctrine of the resurrection can lead us to contempt of earthly things and call us back from the commission of evil. But this resurrection has been ordained by God so that the whole man, that is, soul together with body, may receive eternal glory.

units.la: Porrò testimonia varia extant resurrectionem mortuorum astruentia, Ezechielis tricesimo septimo, Aperiam tumulos vestros, & educam vos de sepulchris vestris. Esaiae vicesimo sexto, Viuent mortui tui cum cadauere meo resurgent: expergescimini, & laudate habitatores pulueris: quia vt ros olerū ros tuus, & terra mortuos proijciet. Iob. 19. In nouissimo die de terra surrecturus sum, & in carne mea videbo Deum. Daniel. duodecimo, Multique dormientium in terra pulueris expergiscentur, hi ad vitam aeternam, & illi ad opprobrium, & ad contemptum sempiternum. Christus Ioannis sexto, Haec est voluntas patris qui misit me, ne quid perdam ex omnibus, quae dedit mihi, sed resuscitè illa in nouissimo die. Ioannis quinto, Veniet hora, & nunc est, qua omnes, qui in monumentis sunt, audient vocem filij Dei, & prodibunt, qui bona fecerunt, in resurrectionem vitae: qui verò mala egerunt, in resurrectionem condemnationis. Ioannis vndecimo, Martha, Scio, inquit, quòd resurget in nouissimo die. Item prima Corinthiorum decimoquinto. Philippensi secundo. Prima Thessalonicensi quarto, plenissimè autem prima Corinthiorum decimoquinto.
units.tr: Moreover, there are various testimonies that establish the resurrection of the dead: Ezekiel 37, "I will open your graves and bring you up out of your sepulchres." Isaiah 26, "Your dead shall live; with my body they shall rise. Awake and sing, you who dwell in the dust, for your dew is as the dew of herbs, and the earth shall cast out the dead." Job 19, "At the last day I shall rise from the earth, and in my flesh I shall see God." Daniel 12, "Many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, these to everlasting life, and those to shame and everlasting contempt." Christ, John 6, "This is the will of the Father who sent me, that I lose nothing of all that he has given me, but raise them up at the last day." John 5, "The hour is coming, and now is, when all who are in the tombs shall hear the voice of the Son of God, and shall come forth: those who have done good, to the resurrection of life; but those who have done evil, to the resurrection of condemnation." John 11, Martha: "I know," she says, "that he will rise at the last day." Likewise 1 Corinthians 15, Philippians 2, 1 Thessalonians 4, and most fully 1 Corinthians 15.

units.la: Et iudicij aeterni) Septimum fundamentum, sine cuius cognitione praecedentia omnia non videntur multum pro futura. Quanti enim fient illa, si non de altera vita, melioriq; post hanc vitam statu certi efficiamur? Ergo hic articulus sicut postremo loco numeratur, ita omnium aliorum vere clausula est & catastrophe. Dicitur porrò iudicium aeternū, non quòd semper & sine fine exerceatur, sed quòd sit de rebus aeternis, nempe de aeterna vita, vel de aeterna morte. Iudex ipse Christus est, cui pater omne commisit iudicium, iudicandi sunt omnes homines boni & mali simul, è quibus illis conferet Christus vitam aeternam, his verò mortem seu damnationem aeternam.
units.tr: And of eternal judgment. The seventh foundation, without the knowledge of which all the preceding seem to matter little for the future. For how much would those things count if we were not made certain of another life and of a better state after this life? Therefore this article, as it is numbered last, so is truly the conclusion and catastrophe of all the others. Moreover, it is called eternal judgment, not because it is exercised always and without end, but because it concerns eternal things, namely eternal life or eternal death. The judge himself is Christ, to whom the Father has committed all judgment; all men, both good and evil, are to be judged together, and of these Christ will bestow eternal life on the one sort, and on the others eternal death or damnation.

units.la: Valde prodest huius extremi iudicij cognitio & contemplatio, ad confirmandos bonos in primis, in fide, item in spe. Quae enim erit fides vel spes, nisi quid melius post hac vitam in nobis sit propositum: item ad confirmandos eosdem in perpetuo exercitio bonorum operum, quae in extremo illo die largiter ipsis à Deo renumerantur. Mali verò huius iudicij contemplatione deterrentur à male agendo, cùm sciant, se, si suo more pergant male agere, aeternis ignibus cruciandos. Qui de isto iudicio non audiunt, vel non intelligunt, eos pro Epicureis & prorsus atheis habebimus: quando etiam gentiles plurimi iudicium hoc agnouerunt, eiusque expectatione ad vitanda amplectendaque bona fuerint permoti. Testimonia autem, quibus probatur, ac describitur istud iudicium, habes Esaiae 66. Daniel. 12. Marthaei 25. Marci 9. Ioan. 5. Itè omnes promissiones apud prophetas & Apostolos de vita aeterna, sicut & comminationes apud eosdem de morte aeterna. Item vota & precationes sanctorum, quibus petunt dissolui & cum Deo viuere. Constantia item martyrum in supplicijs, metus impiorum in periculis mortis, non obscurè testantur, aliam vitam vel mortem post hanc vitam seu mortem restare. Sed non opus est nunc de his copiosius agere. Dignum hoc obseruatu, ex uno hoc loco Apostoli clarissimè posse colligi, quae ratio fuerit instituendorum rudium in primitiua ecclesia: & si nunc volumus omnibus modis synceram doctrinam reducere in ecclesiam, necessum est hoc praescriptum Apostoli in docendis rudibus sequamur, & hunc in tradendo catechismo seruemus ordinem.
units.tr: The knowledge and contemplation of this final judgment is very profitable, chiefly for confirming the good in faith and likewise in hope. For what would faith or hope be, unless something better were set before us after this life? Likewise it confirms the same in the constant practice of good works, which on that last day will be richly repaid to them by God. The wicked, however, by contemplating this judgment are deterred from doing evil, since they know that if they go on doing evil in their usual way they will be tormented in eternal fires. Those who do not hear or do not understand about this judgment we must regard as Epicureans and utter atheists, since very many even of the Gentiles acknowledged this judgment and were moved by its expectation to avoid evil and embrace good. The testimonies by which this judgment is proved and described you have in Isaiah 66, Daniel 12, Matthew 25, Mark 9, John 5. Likewise all the promises in the prophets and Apostles about eternal life, as also their threats about eternal death. Likewise the vows and prayers of the saints, by which they ask to be loosed and to live with God. The constancy of the martyrs under torments and the fear of the impious in danger of death testify not obscurely that another life or death remains after this life or death. But there is no need to treat of these things more fully now. It is worth observing that from this one passage the reason for instructing the untaught in the primitive Church can very clearly be gathered from the Apostle; and if we now wish to bring sound doctrine back into the Church in every way, we must follow this precept of the Apostle in teaching the untaught, and keep this order in handing down the catechism.

units.la: Namfieri non potest, vt qui semel fuerint illuminati, gustauerintq; donum caeleste, & participes facti fuerint spiritus Sancti, gustauerintque bonum Dei verbum ac virtutes futuri seculi, si prolabantur, denuò renouentur per poenitentiam, ab integro crucifigentes sibimetipsis filium Dei, & ludibrio exponentes.
units.tr: It is impossible for those who have once been enlightened, and have tasted the heavenly gift, and have been made partakers of the Holy Spirit, and have tasted the good word of God and the powers of the age to come, if they fall away, to be renewed again through repentance, crucifying again for themselves the Son of God and putting him to open shame.

units.la: Ratio, quare pgrediendū sit ad perfectionē, & nō denuò iaciedū fundamētū pœnitētię, sumpta ab absurdo & incōuenieti, idq; quadā forma similitudinis. Hęc, n. est sententia: ImpolImpossibile est, vt qui semel suscepto baptismo fuerint illuminati, gustauerintque donum cœleste, &c. & postea prolapsi sunt in peccata, denuò per baptilmum pœnitentiæ renouentur. Vnde iam quoque fubintelligendum est, absurdum & inconueniens fore,vt,qui à multo iam tempore fœliciter iecerant fundamenta doctrinæ euangelicæ, denuò propter segnitiem velint ad eadem fundamenta redire,ijsq; perpetuò inhærere. Ita namq; significat Apostolus,redire ad elementa,& non velle progredi,perinde esse at-que denuò baptizari:ideoque sicut istud fieri non potest,ita valde absurdum,si illud sibi faciendum quisquam putet.
units.tr: This is the reason why one ought to press on to perfection and not lay again the foundation of repentance. It is drawn from the absurd and the inconvenient, in a certain form of likeness. The sense is this: it is impossible that those who, having once received baptism, have been enlightened and have tasted the heavenly gift, etc., and afterwards have fallen into sins, should be renewed again through the baptism of repentance. From this it must also be understood that it would be absurd and inconvenient for those who have for a long time happily laid the foundations of evangelical doctrine to wish, through sloth, to return to those same foundations and to cling to them for ever. For this is what the Apostle means: to return to the elements and not to wish to advance is just the same as being baptized again. Therefore, just as the latter cannot be done, so it is very absurd if anyone thinks he should do the former.

units.la: Ita verò debere exponi ista quadam forma similitudinis,satis liquet & ex præceden-tibus:quandoquidem prædecessit obiurgatio segnitiei,secuta deinde exhortatio ad no-uam diligentiam,debent præsentia verba pro ratione exhortationis accipi:id quod & se-quens similitudo de terra proferente fructum, & accipiente benedictionem non ob-scurè indicat.Alias quidem,si simpliciter accipiamus, declarari hic, non esse iterandum baptismum,sicut plurimi notant,quantulum quæso istud ad causam,quæ agitur,condu-cet?Atque ista ratio per similitudinem ita ducta valde efficax est ad deterrendum eos,ne elementis amplius immorentur, difficilemque scrupum inijcit conscientijs, dum hoc pacto suggerit,eos,qui semper redire volunt ad elementa,non minus culpandos,quàm si denuò post lapsum baptizarentur.
units.tr: That these words are to be explained in this form of likeness is clear enough also from what precedes. A rebuke of sloth came first, and then an exhortation to new diligence followed, so the present words ought to be taken in accordance with the purpose of the exhortation. The likeness that follows, of the earth bringing forth fruit and receiving blessing, also clearly indicates this. Otherwise, if we take the words simply, it is declared here that baptism is not to be repeated, as very many note. But how much, I ask, does that contribute to the matter in hand? This argument, drawn through a likeness, is very effective for deterring people from lingering any longer among the elements. It also casts a difficult scruple upon consciences, since in this way it suggests that those who always want to return to the elements are no less to be blamed than if they were baptized again after a fall.

units.la: Sed præterea,ut magis etiam perterrefaciat, culpam illorum multò artificiosisimè exaggerat,dum quare impossibile & nullo modo committendum sit,vt quis denuò baptizetur,exponit,dicens:ab integro crucifigentes sibimetipsis filium Dei,& ludibrio exponentes: In-terpretantur enim quidam,& non sine apposita amplificatione, rebaptizari maximum crimen esse in personam Christi,ac plane iuxtà peccare,qui id faciat, atque si Christum cruci affigeret, nècnon exponeret ludibrio.Vt inde quoque colligatur,eos, qui primis elementis religionis perceptis,nihil,cùm tamen possint,volunt adiungere, simili pro-pemodum peccato obnoxios.Quo profectò nihil dici potest atrocius magisùe exectan-dum,præsertim apud eos,qui nominis Christi haberi volunt præclari & fortes confes-sores.Et reuera non velle vlterius proficere,imò potius retrogredi,maximè post totpræ clara dona in baptismo,& cum baptismo semel accepta, nònne erat Christum eiusque dona abijcere,& sic Christum contemnere,damnare,crucifigere,deridere? Itaque dum Apostolus illos,qui redire ad fundamenta semper volunt,similes facit illis, qui denuò volunt baptizari,quod tamen immane esse scelus nullus non agnoscebat, valde acritet segnes Iudæos urget,& probè animaduertisse videtur,quomodo cum duris & pertina-cibus animis agendum sibi foret,quodque ad eos terriculamenta & minas huiusmodi proferri conueniret,sicut vulgò dici solet,duro nodo durum adhibendum esse cuneum. Nihil verò habet obscuritatis hæc nostra interpretatio,maximè si hæc verba,denuò renouari per pœnitentiam,accipiamus pro eo,quod est regenerari per baptismum. Ita verò ac-cipi debere,liquet ex eo,quòd renouatio alias renascentia vel regeneratio baptismo pro-pria tribuitur,quia spiritus Sanctus in baptismo nouos atque alios homines efficit. ad Titum 3. Non ex operibus,quæ sunt in iustitia, quæ faciebamus nos, sed secundum suâ misericordiam saluos nos fecit,per lauacrum regenerationis, ac renouationis spiritus Sancti,quem effudit in nos opulente.
units.tr: Moreover, in order to terrify still more, he exaggerates their guilt most skilfully. While setting out why it is impossible, and in no way to be committed, that someone be baptized again, he says: "crucifying again for themselves the Son of God and putting him to open shame." For some interpret this, and not without added amplification, to mean that rebaptism is the greatest crime against the person of Christ, and that whoever does it sins just as if he were nailing Christ to the cross and exposing him to mockery. From this it is also inferred that those who, having received the first elements of religion, do not want to add anything, although they could, are liable to a sin almost like this. Nothing more atrocious can be said, and nothing more to be shunned, especially among those who wish to be regarded as illustrious and brave confessors of the name of Christ. And indeed, to be unwilling to advance further, or rather to go backwards, especially after so many splendid gifts received once in baptism and together with baptism: is this not to cast off Christ and his gifts, and so to despise, condemn, crucify and deride Christ? Therefore, while the Apostle makes those who always want to return to the foundations like those who want to be baptized again (which everyone acknowledged to be a monstrous crime), he presses the sluggish Jews very sharply. He seems to have seen well how he must deal with hard and stubborn minds, and that it was fitting to put before them such frightening threats, as is commonly said: a hard wedge must be applied to a hard knot. Yet this our interpretation has no obscurity, especially if we take the words "renewed again through repentance" to mean what is "to be regenerated through baptism." That they must be so taken is clear from the fact that renewal, which is otherwise rebirth or regeneration, is attributed to baptism as its proper work, because the Holy Spirit in baptism makes new and different men. Titus 3: "Not by works of righteousness which we did, but according to his mercy he saved us, through the washing of regeneration and renewal of the Holy Spirit, whom he poured out upon us abundantly."

units.la: Similiter Ephesiorum quarto,Apostolus refricans memoriam suscepti baptismi, Vos autem nõ sic didicistis,inquit, Christum,siquidé illum audistis,& in eo doči fuistis,què admodum est veritas in Iesu,deponere iuxta priorem conuersationem veterem homi-nem,qui corrumpitur iuxta concupiscentias erroris,renouari verò spiritu metis vestræ, & induere nouum hominem,qui iuxta Deum conditus est, per iustitiam & sanctitatem veritatis.Item Colossensium tertio, Ne mentiamini alius aduersus alium, posteaquam exuistis veterem hominem cum factis suis,& induistis nouum, qui renouatur ad agni-tionem & imaginem eius qui condidit illum. Vbi argumentatur sumptis rationibus à renouatione ante facta in baptismo. Ita renouatio proprie baptismo attribuitur. Sed & pœnitentia pro baptismo, videlicet signatum pro signo, per Metonymiam non inepte accipitur: Quomodo Actorum vndecimo, Igitur & gentibus Deus pœniten-tiam concessit ad vitam. Vbi pœnitentiam significare baptilmum,liquet ex eo, quòd Petrus ibidem præmisisset:cùm autem exorsus essem sermonem, illapsus est spiritus Sanctus in illos,quemadmodum & in nos fuerat illapsus smitio.
units.tr: Likewise Ephesians 4, where the Apostle, recalling the memory of the baptism received: "But you have not so learned Christ, if indeed you have heard him and been taught in him, as the truth is in Jesus: to put off, according to your former way of life, the old man, who is corrupted according to the lusts of error; and to be renewed in the spirit of your mind, and to put on the new man, who after God is created in righteousness and holiness of truth." Also Colossians 3: "Do not lie to one another, since you have put off the old man with his deeds and have put on the new, who is renewed unto knowledge according to the image of him who created him." Here he argues from the renewal that took place before, in baptism. So renewal is properly attributed to baptism. But repentance too can be taken for baptism, by metonymy, not unfittingly, the thing signified being put for the sign. So Acts 11: "Then God has granted repentance to the Gentiles unto life." That repentance here means baptism is clear from the fact that Peter had said just before: "When I began to speak, the Holy Spirit fell upon them, just as upon us at the beginning."

units.la: Veniebat autem in mentem, quod dixerat Dominus, Ioannes quidem baptizauit aqua, cæterùm vos baptizabimini spiritu Sancto. Passim præterea baptismus vocatur, non ita simpliciter, sed baptismus pœnitentiæ. Matthæi tertio, Ioannes dicit:Ego quidem baptizo vos aqua ad pœnitentiam, &cæt. Vbi non ita distinguitur baptismus Ioannis à baptismo Christi, quasi huius non esset ad poenitentiam, sed ad remissionem peccatorum, illius vero tantùm ad poenitentiam, ad remissionem autem neq̄uaquam: quemadmodum alicubi disseruit Chrysostomus. Nam etiá Christi baptismus appellatur baptismus poenitentię, quia poenitentia semper habet adiuncta, vt effectû spiritualequis ex baptismo consequatur: sicut Christus iussit baptismū cū poenitentia praedicari, susceptio baptismi externa est internae poenitentiae ac fidei contestatio: qua de re etiam Romanorum sexto, Colossensium secundo, vbi de mortificatione, cuius admonemur in baptismo, pluribus agitur: & baptismum Scriptores sacramentum poenitentiae appellare non dubitant. Sed ne quis hanc interpretationem ceu parum commodâ reiciat, adferemus lubenter aliorum interpretationes, quibus nostra confirmari queat.
units.tr: Moreover, there came to mind what the Lord had said: "John indeed baptized with water, but you shall be baptized with the Holy Spirit." Furthermore, baptism is everywhere called not simply baptism, but the baptism of repentance. Matthew 3: John says, "I indeed baptize you with water unto repentance," etc. Here John's baptism is not so distinguished from Christ's baptism as if the latter were not unto repentance but unto remission of sins, while the former was only unto repentance and not at all unto remission, as Chrysostom has argued somewhere. For even the baptism of Christ is called the baptism of repentance, because repentance is always joined to it, as the spiritual effect that follows from baptism. Christ commanded that baptism be preached together with repentance. The external reception of baptism is a testimony to inward repentance and faith. On this account Romans 6 and Colossians 2 speak at length of mortification, of which we are reminded in baptism. And writers do not hesitate to call baptism the sacrament of repentance. But lest anyone reject this interpretation as not very suitable, we will gladly bring forward the interpretations of others, by which ours may be confirmed.

units.la: Chrysostomus inprimis exponens haec verba, Denuò renouari per poenitentiam: Quid ergo, inquit, exclusa est poenitentia? Non poenitentia exclusa est: abest, sed renouatio per lauacrum regenerationis. Et addit, renouari, hoc est, nouos fieri: renouatio quippe lauacri est. Renouabitur, inquit, sicut aquila iuuentus tua. Paulò post: Qui secundo baptizat, rursum crucifigit. Alia in eandem sententiam sequuntur.
units.tr: Chrysostom, first, expounding these words, "renewed again through repentance": "What then," he says, "is repentance excluded? Repentance is not excluded; it is absent, but renewal is through the washing of regeneration." And he adds: renewed, that is, made new, for renewal belongs to the washing. "Your youth shall be renewed like the eagle's." Shortly after: "He who baptizes a second time crucifies again." Other writers follow to the same effect.

units.la: Theophylactus item ut in caeteris, ita & praesenti loco eandem habet Chrysostomi interpretationem. Ambrosius libro secundo de poenitentia capite secundo, contra Nouatianos disputans, haec citat verba, & interpretatur, his simpliciter baptismi iterationem prohiberi, non autem lapsis viam ad poenitentiam praecludi.
units.tr: Theophylact likewise, as elsewhere, so also in the present passage, has the same interpretation as Chrysostom. Ambrose, in the second book On Repentance, chapter 2, disputing against the Novatians, cites these words and interprets that they simply forbid the repetition of baptism, but do not close the way to repentance for the fallen.

units.la: Primasius in hunc locum sic habet, impossibile est, renouari posse eos per poenitentiam & baptismum. Statim subijcit: Quid ergo? Exclusa est poenitentia post baptismum, & venia delictorum? Ablit. Duo siquidem sunt genera poenitentiae. Vnum quidem ante baptismum, quod deprecatio baptismi potest appellari, quia iniungitur illis, qui instruuntur, antequam ad baptismum perueniant, quam beatus Apostolus hic excludit, dicens: non posse iterum renouari per poenitentiam, quatenus poenitentia facta iterum baptizetur.
units.tr: Primasius on this passage says: "It is impossible for them to be renewed through repentance and baptism." Immediately he adds: "What then? Is repentance excluded after baptism, and forgiveness of sins? Far from it. For there are two kinds of repentance. The one, before baptism, may be called the prayer of baptism, because it is enjoined on those who are instructed before they come to baptism. This the blessed Apostle excludes here, saying that they cannot again be renewed through repentance, inasmuch as repentance made would then be baptized again."

units.la: Alterum autem genus poenitentiae est, per quod post baptismum delentur peccata: quod beatus Apostolus non excludit. Terret ergo omnes ut timeant post baptismi gratiam grauioribus peccatis se implicare: quia non potest fieri secunda renouatio per lauacrum baptismatis. Nam sicut Christus semel mortuus est, & semel resurgens iam non moritur: ita semel gratia baptismatis agenda est, nec potest iterari, nisi dubiû fuerit, utrû nam quis captus ab hostibus sit baptizatus. Renouari autem dixit nouum fieri: nouum autem facere hominem sacri baptismatis est.
units.tr: The other kind of repentance is that through which sins are blotted out after baptism, and this the blessed Apostle does not exclude. He therefore terrifies all, so that after the grace of baptism they do not entangle themselves in graver sins, because a second renewal through the washing of baptism cannot take place. For as Christ died once, and rising once dies no more, so the grace of baptism is to be received once and cannot be repeated, unless it is doubtful whether someone was baptized when captured by enemies. He said "renewed," meaning made new; but to make a man new belongs to sacred baptism.

units.la: Oecolampadius etiam hanc interpretationem amplectitur, citans Ambrosium. Quâobrem cûm omnes hi & plerique alij haec verba, Denuò renouari per poenitentiam, eodem modo sint interpretati, rectè nos quoque ad eundem modum exposuimus, & quadam similitudinis forma locutum esse Apostolum diximus, vt sententia sit: Semel baptizari hominem, semel renasci, semel renouari: semper tamen peccatorum poenitudine duci, mortificaque carnem cum concupiscentijs suis: hoc fieri oportere saepius & assiduè: illud verò faciendum semel duntaxat.
units.tr: Oecolampadius also adopts this interpretation, citing Ambrose. Therefore, since all these writers and most others have interpreted the words "to be renewed again through repentance" in the same way, we too have rightly explained them in the same manner, and we have said that the Apostle spoke in a certain form of likeness, so that the meaning is this: a man is baptized once, is born again once, and is renewed once; yet he must always be led by repentance for sins and mortify the flesh with its lusts. This ought to be done often and continually, but the other only once.

units.la: Pari ratione semel discendum esse Christum, & elementis ad perfectionem aspirandum: illis inhaerere semper, ad hanc verò nunquam contendere, Christi discipulo esse indignissimum.
units.tr: In the same way, we must learn Christ once and strive toward perfection with the elements, always cling to the elements but never strive for perfection, which would be most unworthy of a disciple of Christ.

units.la: Nec verè dissimulandum est, interea fuisse, qui non satis animaduertentes in has voces, denuò renouari per poenitentiam, existimarunt, simpliciter hic negari ijs, qui lapsi essent post baptismum, poenitentiam & reparationem, planeque spem veniae talibus nullam superesse. Atque ita hunc locum patrocinari Nouato & Catharis, qui huiusmodi impium dogma circiter annum Christi ducentesimum quinquagesimum quintum, pugnans cum vniuersa Scriptura aliquando sparserunt: eamque ob causam nonnulli epistolam hanc suspectam habuere, tanquam minimè apostolicam, ac reiiciendam e numero canonicarum arbitrati sunt. Et certè si ita, ut Nouatus accepit, sensisse apostolum probabile esset, merito epistola haec reiceretur. Sed cûm ea sententia nusquam aliibi in Scripturis probetur, imò cûm hac ipsa epistola habeantur aperta testimonia contrà talem interpretationem facientia, non est quod ita crasse locutum Apostolum suspicemur, & tam à vero dissentientem interpretationem feramus.
units.tr: Nor should we truly conceal that there have been some who, not paying close enough attention to the words "to be renewed again through repentance," thought that the passage simply denies repentance and restoration to those who had fallen after baptism, and that no hope of pardon remains for such people. And so they thought this passage supported the Novatians and Cathari, who at some time, about the year of Christ 255, spread this impious dogma, which contradicts the whole of Scripture. For this reason some regarded this epistle with suspicion, as by no means apostolic, and judged that it should be rejected from the number of canonical books. And certainly, if it were probable that the Apostle thought as Novatus understood him, this epistle would rightly be rejected. But since that view is nowhere else proved in the Scriptures, and since clear testimonies opposed to such an interpretation are found in this very epistle, there is no reason to suspect that the Apostle spoke so crudely, or to accept an interpretation so far removed from the truth.

units.la: Caeterum in hac epistola, lapsis veniam paratam esse, omnes ij loci testantur, qui Christum pontificem & mediatorem constituunt, ac describunt vnicâ hostiam satisfacientem pro peccatis omnium hominum: vide caput septimum, octauum, nonum, decimum.
units.tr: Moreover, that pardon is prepared for the fallen in this epistle is attested by all those passages which set up Christ as high priest and mediator, and describe the one sacrifice that makes satisfaction for the sins of all men: see chapters seven, eight, nine and ten.

units.la: Et capite praecedenti, Accedamus cum fiducia ad thronum gratiae, vt consequamur miserimisericordiam: capite vndecimo enumerat multos, qui post lapsum iterum per fidem sunt misericordiam consecuti. Et capite duodecimo, Nos quoque cum tanta septi-mus nube testium, depos ito onere omni, & tenaciter inhærente peccato, per toleran-tiam curramus in propo sito nobis certamine, respicientes ad fidei ducem & consum-matorem Iesum, &c.
units.tr: And in the preceding chapter: "Let us draw near with confidence to the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy." In chapter eleven he lists many who, after falling, obtained mercy again through faith. And in chapter twelve: "Let us also, since we are surrounded by so great a cloud of witnesses, laying aside every weight and the sin that clings so closely, run with endurance the race set before us, looking to Jesus, the author and perfecter of faith," and so on.

units.la: Et Apostolus in cæteris epistolis passim docet, lapsos in gratiam recipi. 2. Corinth. 2. recipi iubet in cestuosum. Galat. 4. Filioli mei, quos iterum parturio, &c. Ioannes in sua epistola: Si quis peccauerit, aduocatum habemus apud patrem Iesum Christum iustum, &c. Sed, quid ego ista congero, quasi vero institutum esset contra Nouatum pluribus disputare: Si quis plura hac in parte desiderat, legat Cypriani epistolam ad Nonatianum, in qua, quod lapsis spes veniæ non sit deneganda, copiosissime declarat: item eiusdem Cypriani epistolam quartam ad Antonianum. Item Augustinum in libro quæstionum veteris & noui testamenti, quæstione 102. qua plenissime docet, quomodo Nouatianis negantibus pœnitentiam sit respondendum: Item Chrysostomus in libro de reparatione lapsi, tomo sexto, habet nonnulla, quæ huc conducunt.
units.tr: And the Apostle everywhere in his other epistles teaches that the fallen are received again into grace. In 2 Corinthians 2 he bids that the incestuous man be received back. Galatians 4: "My little children, for whom I am again in labour," and so on. John in his epistle: "If anyone sins, we have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous," and so on. But why do I heap up these things, as if it were my purpose to dispute at length against Novatian? If anyone desires more on this point, let him read Cyprian's epistle to Novatianus, in which he declares very fully that hope of pardon must not be denied to the fallen; likewise Cyprian's fourth epistle to Antonianus. Also Augustine in his book of questions on the Old and New Testament, question 102, where he most fully teaches how the Novatians who deny repentance are to be answered. Likewise Chrysostom, in his book on the restoration of the fallen, in volume six, has some things that bear on this.

units.la: Iam vero, quod quidam studuerunt mollire sententiam, explicando, impossibile dici ab Apostolo, pro eo, quod est valde difficile: quasi impossibile dixerit quadam hyperbole seu hyperoche exaggerandi ac terrendi causa: ne hoc quidem existimo satis conuenire, præsertim cum sententia hæc, videlicet lapsos difficulter admodum renouari per pœnitentiam, neque cum præcedentibus, neque cum sequentibus cohæreat. Quanquam videtur hyperocha hic esse, eo quod paulo post veluti ad emolliendum ea subijcitur, tametsi sic loquamur: ista interpretatio tamen non est absurda. Quibusdam placuit exponere verba ista de peccato in spiritum Sanctum, cui, ut Christus testatur Matthæi duodecimo, Marci tertio, Lucæ vndecimo, venia denegatur. Cum enim peccatum in spiritum Sanctum sit, aperta & manifesta veritatem Dei, postquam agnoueris ea, cōtra conscien-tiam & experimentum fidei negligere, reijcere, impugnare, & negare, eam esse Dei, nec gare eam esse salutiferam (sicut Marc. 3. Iudæi faciebant, dicentes, Christum non virtute Dei, sed Beelzebub eijcere dæmonia) rectè his, aduersus eos, qui ulterius progredi detrectarint, dicitur, quod, qui postquam illuminati semel sunt, gustaueruntque donū Dei cœleste, &c. prolabuntur, id est, retrocedunt, veritatem agnitam incipietes contemnere ac damnare, nullo pacto veniam accipient, sed rei fiunt non minus quam illi, qui Christum crucifixerunt & ludibrio habuerunt. In quam sententiam legitur sequenti capite decimo: Si uolentes peccauerimus post acceptam cognitionem veritatis, non ultra pro peccatis reliqua est hostia, sed formidabilis quædam expectatio iudicij, & ignis vehemen-tia, qui deuoraturus est aduersarios. Et alia ibi sequuntur de ijs, qui filium Dei con-culcarint.
units.tr: Now, as to what some have tried to soften the sense by explaining "impossible" as said by the Apostle for "very difficult": as if he had said "impossible" by a hyperbole, or hyperoche, for the sake of exaggerating and frightening. I do not think even this fits well, especially since this view, namely that the fallen are renewed through repentance only with great difficulty, coheres neither with what goes before nor with what follows. Although there does seem to be a hyperbole here, since shortly afterwards something is added as if to soften it, and although we may speak this way, this interpretation is nevertheless not absurd. Some have chosen to explain these words as referring to the sin against the Holy Spirit, for which, as Christ testifies in Matthew 12, Mark 3 and Luke 11, forgiveness is denied. For since the sin against the Holy Spirit consists in clearly and manifestly recognizing the truth of God, and then, against conscience and the experience of faith, neglecting, rejecting, opposing and denying it, saying that it is not God's and is not saving (as the Jews did in Mark 3, saying that Christ cast out demons not by the power of God but by Beelzebub), then rightly against those who refused to go further it is said that those who have once been enlightened, have tasted the heavenly gift of God, and so on, and fall away, that is, turn back, beginning to despise and condemn the truth they have known, will by no means receive pardon, but become guilty no less than those who crucified Christ and mocked him. To this sense the following chapter ten points: "If we sin wilfully after receiving the knowledge of the truth, there no longer remains a sacrifice for sins, but a certain fearful expectation of judgment and a fierce fire which will devour the adversaries." And there follow other things there about those who trampled underfoot the Son of God.

units.la: Quæ, sicut dissimulari non potest, appositè ibi dici ad deterrendum Hebræos, ne post agnitam veritatem retrocedant, eamque contemnant, & beneficia per Christum acce-pta aspernentur: ita non male quis dixerit, & præsenti loco rationem contineri, cur sem-per in melius proficere, & ad perfectionem tendere debeant, sumptam à comminatio-ne iræ Dei, quam incurrent, si, postquam semel mirabiliter illuminati sunt, amplissimaq; beneficia spiritualia acceperunt, &c. iterum prolabantur, agnitam veritatem contemnant, abijciantque. Tunc enim eadem seueritate puniendos, quam promeriti sunt, qui Christum crucifixerunt. Quæ interpretatio nequaquam repuenda, tum quod exhortationi acriori mire conuenit, tum quod præsentia verba & antecedentibus & sequetibus apte copulat: imo clarè dicitur, qui participes facti fuerint spiritus Sancti, gustauerint q; bo-num Dei uerbum ac virtutes futuri seculi, &c. De accepto spiritu Sancto est accipiendū. Ita etiam interpretatur Bullingerus in libris contra Anabaptistas, lib. 1. tractatu 8. vbi et-iam apte satis exponit locum similem cap. 10. huius epistolæ. Certè quomodocunq; in-terpremur, nihil hic dicit, quod Nouatianis patrocinetur, satis est manifestum. Sed de his satis: nunc ad partes examinandas veniamus.
units.tr: As it cannot be denied that these words are fittingly spoken there to deter the Hebrews from turning back after they have recognized the truth, despising it, and scorning the benefits received through Christ, so one may not badly say that the present passage also contains the reason why they ought always to advance toward better things and strive for perfection, taken from the threat of God's wrath which they will incur if, after they have once been wonderfully enlightened and have received the great spiritual benefits, they again fall away, despise the truth they have known, and cast it off. For then they will be punished with the same severity as those who crucified Christ deserve. This interpretation is by no means to be rejected, both because it fits remarkably well with a sharper exhortation, and because it aptly links the present words with both what precedes and what follows; indeed it is plainly said that "they became partakers of the Holy Spirit, and tasted the good word of God and the powers of the age to come," and so on. It must be understood of the Holy Spirit received. Bullinger also interprets it this way in his books against the Anabaptists, book 1, treatise 8, where he also explains quite aptly a similar passage in chapter 10 of this epistle. Certainly, however we interpret it, it is quite clear that nothing here supports the Novatians. But enough of these matters: let us now come to examine the parts.

units.la: Nam fieri non potest, vt, qui semel fuerint illuminati, gustauerintq; donum cœleste, & participes facti fuerint spiritus Sancti, gustauerintq; bonum Dei verbum, ac virtutes futuri seculi, si prolabantur, denuò renouentur per pœnitentiam.
units.tr: For it is not possible that those who have once been enlightened, have tasted the heavenly gift, have become partakers of the Holy Spirit, have tasted the good word of God and the powers of the age to come, and then fall away, should be renewed again through repentance.

units.la: Hoc inprimis notandum est, Apostolum per congeriem & expolitionem enumerare diuersa ac multiplicia dona spiritualia, ab ijs qui in religione fundamenta fœliciter iecerant, & iam primum baptizati erant, accepta, ut ita amplificet illorum crimen, qui post tanta beneficia prolabi & retrocedere non uerentur. Certum est, quo qui ampliores fructus & fœliciores successus experti sunt in ipsis discendæ religionis primordijs,eò magis excitari eos decebat ad progrediendum ad altiora. Vbi tanta dona statim in initio collata fuerunt, longè plura & præstatiora expectanda sunt in successu. Et ea est Dominus in suos benevolentia, vt quib.plura dederit,ijsdé,si bene vtatur,plura velit dare:id quod aperte docet parabola illa de talentis Matth. 25. Eamque ob causam eos,qui feliciter sunt viam religionis ingressi,decet semper progredi, & quodammodo cum fœnore subinde noua dona Dei accipere. Tantum de amplificatione hîc necessario obseruanda.
units.tr: This must be noted first of all: the Apostle, by heaping up and elaborating, enumerates the various and manifold spiritual gifts received by those who had happily laid the foundations in religion and had already been baptized for the first time, so that he may magnify the guilt of those who, after such great benefits, do not hesitate to fall away and turn back. It is certain that those who have had richer fruits and more fortunate progress in the very beginnings of learning the religion ought therefore to be stirred up all the more to advance toward higher things. Where such great gifts have been bestowed at the very start, far greater and more excellent gifts are to be expected in the course of progress. And such is the Lord's goodwill toward his people that to those to whom he has given more, he is willing, if they use it well, to give still more; this the parable of the talents in Matthew 25 plainly teaches. And for this reason those who have happily entered the way of religion ought always to advance, and, as it were, with interest, receive new gifts of God from time to time. This much is to be necessarily observed here about the amplification.

units.la: Nam fieri non potest) Siue interpretemur sententiam de non repetendo baptismo, siue de non retrocedendo, & impugnando cognitam veritatem, peraptè, vt magis deterreat, magisque commoueat, dixit, impossibile esse, denuò renouari. Non iam speras, inquit Chrysostomus, quod impossibile est. Non enim dixit, non decet, neque prodest, neque licet, sed impossibile est: Ergo in desperationem eos adduxit. Atque ita meo iudicio quasi cogit Apostolus Hebræos, vt ad proficiendum sese accingant. Quare autem impossibile sit denuò renouari per baptismum, Chrysostomus duas caussas siue rationes ponit:Alteram, quia, qui antea semel tanta dona spiritualia accepit, & tamen non habuit in honore, indignus est qui eadem iterum accipiat. Alteram, quia, cùm in baptismo & commoriamur ac sepeliamur cum Christo, sicut dicitur Roman.o&tauo, & Christus dun-taxat semel mortuus sit, nec mors illi ultrà possit dominari: non magis possumus denuò baptizari, quàm Christus potest denuò mori.
units.tr: For it is not possible: whether we interpret the passage as concerning not repeating baptism, or as concerning not turning back and opposing the truth once known, he has said, very aptly so as to deter more and move more, that it is impossible to be renewed again. "Do not hope for what is impossible," says Chrysostom. For he did not say "it is not fitting," nor "it is not profitable," nor "it is not lawful," but "it is impossible." Therefore he has brought them into despair. And so, in my judgment, the Apostle as it were compels the Hebrews to gird themselves to advance. Why it is impossible to be renewed again through baptism, Chrysostom gives two causes or reasons. The first is that he who has once received such great spiritual gifts and yet has not held them in honour is unworthy to receive them again. The second is that, since in baptism we both die with Christ and are buried with him, as is said in Romans 6, and Christ died only once and death can no longer have dominion over him, we cannot be baptized again any more than Christ can die again.

units.la: Vnde velle denuò baptizari, est Christum iterum crucifigere & ludibrio habere. Nam si denuò baptizaueris, ergo eneruas vires mortis Christi, quæ in primo baptismo fuerant,Christus frustra tibi semel mortuus est: & secundus baptismus dissoluit priorem, & sic in infinitum posset procedi.
units.tr: Hence to wish to be baptized again is to crucify Christ anew and hold him up to mockery. For if you are baptized again, you nullify the power of Christ's death, which was at work in your first baptism. Christ died for you in vain once, and the second baptism dissolves the first, and so one could proceed to infinity.

units.la: Posset & hæc addi ratio, quòd alia ratio remedia lapsis sunt proposita, nimirum pœnitentia, quæ per omnem vitam debet durare, & esse perpetua: & vsus cœnæ Domini, quam sæpe licet iterare: & quoties vulneratus es per peccatum,toties pro medicina opponere. Quòd si exponamus,impossibile esse renouari eos,qui prolabuntur, oppugnando agnitam veritatem, & hoc quoque rectè dictum propter verbum Christi dicentis,peccatum in spiritum Sanctum, neque in hoc, neque in futuro seculo remitti posse.
units.tr: This reason too could be added: other remedies have been set before the fallen, namely repentance, which ought to last through the whole of life and be perpetual, and the use of the Lord's Supper, which may be repeated often; and as often as you have been wounded by sin, so often you are to apply it as a medicine. But if we expound the passage as meaning that those who fall away cannot be renewed while they oppose the truth once acknowledged, this too is rightly said, on account of the word of Christ saying that sin against the Holy Spirit is not forgiven, neither in this age nor in the age to come.

units.la: Vt,qui semel fuerint illuminati) Vide quàm appositè hoc dictum. Primum vt aliqui ad Christum veniant, & ea quæ religionis sunt,addiscant,oportet illuminari, id est, oportet ex tenebris,in quibus nati & educati sunt toti,eruere, & lumen Spiritus concedere, quo videre possint spiritualia bona ad salutem suam necessaria. Hinc Ioannis primo,Christus lux appellatur illuminans, & tenebræ non apprehendentes Christum describuntur.Ephes.5.Eratis quondam tenebræ, nunc autem lux in Domino, vt filij lucis ambulate.Ephes.1. Deus Domini nostri Iesu Christi, pater gloriæ det vobis Spiritū sapientiæ & reuelationis per agnitionē sui,illuminatos oculos mentis vestræ,vt sciatis,quę sit spes, ad quam ille vocauit,&c.1.Petri 2.Prædicetis virtutes illius,qui è tenebris vos vocauit in admirabilem suam lucem,&c.
units.tr: "Those who have once been enlightened" See how aptly this is said. First, for some to come to Christ and learn the things of religion, it is necessary to be enlightened, that is, to be drawn out of the darkness in which all are born and brought up, and to be granted the light of the Spirit, by which they can see the spiritual goods necessary for their salvation. Hence in John 1 Christ is called the light that enlightens, and those who do not receive Christ are described as darkness. Eph. 5: "You were once darkness, but now are light in the Lord; walk as children of light." Eph. 1: "The God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of glory, give you the spirit of wisdom and revelation in the knowledge of himself, the eyes of your mind enlightened, that you may know what is the hope to which he has called you, etc." 1 Pet. 2: "That you may proclaim the virtues of him who called you out of darkness into his marvellous light, etc."

units.la: Vnde & veteres,quemadmodũ Dionysius,vocabant baptismum μυστήριον φωτισμῶς sacramentum illuminationis, & baptismum appellabant φώτισμα, quòd idololatriâ tenebras esse,legem item vmbram,baptizati scirent, & dies illi, quibus baptisma conferebatur,publicè vocabantur dies luminarium ,teste Nazianzeno in oratione quadam de baptismate,quia multis facibus accensis illuminationem spiritualem volebant significare,sicut hodie quoque in nonnullis ecclesijs facem in ceremonijs baptismi solent adhibere.Ita veteret,quas adhibebant ceremonias,eiusmodi tamen, quæ aliquid docerét: quòd etiam semper liberum fuit imitari.Etsi illas veterum ausi sunt imitari pontifices, & alij successores, quid tantopere nunc rixamur de quarundam valde leuium immutatione?
units.tr: Hence also the ancients, as Dionysius does, called baptism "sacrament of illumination" [μυστήριον φωτισμοῦ], and they called baptism "illumination" [φώτισμα], because those who were baptized knew that idolatry is darkness and the law likewise a shadow. And the days on which baptism was conferred were publicly called "days of lights," as Nazianzen testifies in a certain oration on baptism, because by many lit torches they wanted to signify spiritual illumination, just as today too in some churches they are accustomed to use a torch in the ceremonies of baptism. So the ancients used ceremonies of this kind, which nevertheless taught something; and it has always been free to imitate them. Even if the pontiffs and other successors have dared to imitate those of the ancients, why do we now quarrel so much about the alteration of some very trivial things?

units.la: Etsi verò rectè accipere possimus exposita hîc esse beneficia spiritualia omnia, quæ credentes ab initio suscepti euangelij ad id usque tempus, quo Apostolus epistolam hanc scribebat,acceperant:tamen non dubiū est, de ijs præcipuè, quæ in baptismate à tempore primæ institutionis acceperant, beneficijs sermonem fieri,adeò vt omnia fere, quæ hîc dicuntur,baptismo,tanquam proprij ipsius effectus, tribui rectè queant. Ethis omnibus tantundem significat Apostolus,atque si simpliciter dixisset,eos, qui semel fuerint baptizati,& postea prolabuntur,non posse denuò per baptismum renouari. Sequitur ergo:
units.tr: Although we may rightly take all the spiritual benefits set out here to be those which believers had received from the beginning of the gospel up to the time when the Apostle was writing this letter, there is no doubt that the discussion is chiefly of those benefits which they had received in baptism from the time of its first institution, so that almost everything said here can rightly be attributed to baptism as its proper effects. By all this the Apostle means just as much as if he had simply said that those who have once been baptized and afterwards fall away cannot be renewed again through baptism. Therefore it follows:

units.la: Gustauerintq; donum cœleste) Elegans metaphora à sensu corporis ad animum & spirituale, in voce gustandi.
units.tr: "And have tasted the heavenly gift" An elegant metaphor, moving from the bodily sense of taste to the mind and the spiritual.

units.la: Significat autem, nos hic ex parte, vt Apostolus quoque loquitur 1. Corinth. 13. percipere bona coelestia & spiritualia. Quando enim carne adhuc vestiti sumus, non possumus spiritualia & diuina plene assequi, sed tantum gustus quidam eorum nobis propinatur: id quod significatum est Exodi 33. vbi Mosi, postquam petiisset videre gloriam & faciem Domini, responsum est, Non poteris videre faciem meam: non enim videbit me homo, & viuet. Et paulo post: Videbis posteriora mea, faciem autem meam videre non poteris. Matth. 17. discipuli in monte, vbi Christus transfiguratus se, gustum quendam accipiebat. Et Psalm. 33. eadem metaphora, Gustate & videte, quoniam suauis est Dominus. 1. Pet. 2. Gustastis, quod benignus sit Dominus. Et reuera, quantum differt gustus alicuius rei plena eius saturitate, tantum differt quoque dignitas donorum spiritualium, quae hic percipiuntur, ab illa, quae post hanc vitam promissa est.
units.tr: He signifies, however, that we here in part, as the Apostle also says in 1 Cor. 13, perceive heavenly and spiritual goods. For while we are still clothed in flesh we cannot fully attain spiritual and divine things, but only a certain taste of them is offered to us. This was signified in Exod. 33, where, after Moses asked to see the glory and face of the Lord, the answer came: "You cannot see my face; for man shall not see me and live." And a little later: "You shall see my back parts, but my face you cannot see." Matt. 17: the disciples on the mountain, where Christ was transfigured, received a certain taste. And Ps. 33 uses the same metaphor: "Taste and see that the Lord is sweet." 1 Pet. 2: "You have tasted that the Lord is kind." And indeed, as the taste of a thing differs from being fully satisfied with it, so the dignity of the spiritual gifts received here differs from that which is promised after this life.

units.la: Porro quod donum gustatum esse sentiat, non exprimit: at vero quia emphaticas generauit articulum graecus interpres, quasi diceretur: donum illud coeleste: videtur emphasis ea antonomasiae habere rationem, & plane tale donum significare, quod caetera omnia particularia excellat. Hoc vero est gratia & benedictio spiritualis, quae in baptismo vniuersaliter suscipitur, qua Deo grati & accepti propter Christum efficimur, de qua Ioann. 1. Gratia & veritas per Iesum Christum data est. Et Ephes. 1. Benedictus Deus & pater Domini nostri Iesu Christi, qui benedixit nos omni benedictione spirituali in coelestibus.
units.tr: Further, that he says the gift was tasted he does not express; but since the Greek translator has supplied an emphatic article, as if it were said "that heavenly gift," this emphasis seems to have the force of an antonomasia, and plainly to signify such a gift as excels all the other particular ones. This is the grace and spiritual blessing received universally in baptism, by which we are made pleasing and acceptable to God on account of Christ; of which John 1: "Grace and truth came through Jesus Christ." And Eph. 1: "Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed us with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly places."

units.la: Certe nomine doni gratuita misericordia aperte significatur. Et coelestes vocatur donum, quia ad res coelestes & spirituales, non terrenas vel corporales pertinet, vnde eius excellentia colligi rite potest: item quia a coelis, &, vt Iacobus loquitur, a patre luminum ad nos deriuatur.
units.tr: Certainly by the name of gift, free mercy is openly signified. And it is called "heavenly" because it pertains to heavenly and spiritual things, not earthly or bodily ones, whence its excellence can rightly be gathered. It is also called heavenly because it comes down to us from heaven and, as James says, from the Father of lights.

units.la: Caeterum ad declarandum rudibus animis hunc effectum in baptismo suscepturn, solebant veteres, alicubi salem, alicubi lac & mel, (quod Tertullianus habet libro de corona militis) alicubi vinum & lac recens baptizatis gustandum propinare, vt videre est apud Hieronymum contra Luciferianos, qui dicit id factitatum in ecclesijs Occidentalibus.
units.tr: Moreover, to make this effect received in baptism clear to rude minds, the ancients were accustomed in some places to offer salt, in others milk and honey (as Tertullian has in his book On the Soldier's Garland), and in others wine and fresh milk, to be tasted by the newly baptized. This can be seen in Jerome against the Luciferians, who says this was practised in the Western churches.

units.la: Et participes facti fuerint spiritus sancti) Hoc quoque singulare contingebat illis, qui baptizabantur, praesertim in primitiua ecclesia, praeter donum coeleste, id est, gratiam & benedictionem spiritualem, qua grati & accepti fiebant Deo, accipiebant etiam spiritum Sanctum, id est, per metonymiam, aliqua insignia & peculiaria dona, plerunque etiam externa, e quibus ipsi in primis credentes intus sentiebant, & ab alijs quoque animaduerti poterat, spiritum Sanctum efficaciter in ipsis agere. Cum enim in baptismo contingeret innouatio quaedam, & mutatio vitae in melius, atque ista quidem nequaquam parari posset humanis viribus, datus est in baptismo spiritus Sanctus, qui sua virtute innouationem illam perficeret, & saepe conferebatur, seu collatis significabatur spiritus Sanctus manuum impositione.
units.tr: And have been made partakers of the Holy Spirit. This too happened in a distinctive way to those who were baptized, especially in the primitive church. Besides the heavenly gift, that is, the grace and spiritual blessing by which they were made pleasing and acceptable to God, they also received the Holy Spirit, that is, by metonymy, certain distinctive and peculiar gifts, mostly even external ones, from which the believers themselves first felt inwardly, and others could also perceive, that the Holy Spirit was working effectively in them. For since in baptism a certain renewal and change of life for the better took place, which by no means could be brought about by human powers, the Holy Spirit was given in baptism, to complete that renewal by his power. He was often conferred, or the Holy Spirit was signified, by the laying on of hands.

units.la: Porro dona spiritus Sancti interna sunt eiusmodi, quae enumeratur Esaiae vndecimo, Spiritus sapientiae & intellectus, Spiritus consilij & fortitudinis, Spiritus scientiae & pietatis, & Spiritus timoris Domini: quae etiam in apostolicis scriptis passim commendantur. Ioan. 16. Spiritus docebit vos omnem veritatem: ecce Spiritum intellectus. Rom. 8. Prudentia Spiritus vita & pax: en spiritum sapientiae. Ibidem, Spiritus adiuuat infirmitatem nostram: En Spiritus fortitudinis, &c. Iam dona externa proponuntur. 1. Corinth. 12. Vbi postquam dixisset, Huic quidem per Spiritum datur sermo sapientiae, alij vero sermo scientiae, secundum eundem spiritum, alij vero fides per eundem spiritum (quae utique possunt referri ad dona interna) ita subijcit: alij vero dona sanationum per eundem spiritum, alij vero efficaciae potentiarum, alij vero prophetia, alij vero discretiones spirituum, alij vero genera linguarum, alij vero interpretatio linguarum. Sed haec omnia efficit vnus ille & idem Spiritus, diuidens peculiariter vnicuique sicuti vult. Atque illa inquam dona interna omnibus recte vtentibus sacramento conferri solent, & nunc etiam conferuntur: haec autem peculiaria erant, & illi tempori, quo ecclesia recens erat etiam signorum varietate plantanda confirmandaque, magis conueniebant.
units.tr: The internal gifts of the Holy Spirit are of the kind listed in Isaiah 11: the Spirit of wisdom and understanding, the Spirit of counsel and strength, the Spirit of knowledge and godliness, and the Spirit of the fear of the Lord. These are also commended everywhere in the apostolic writings. John 16: "The Spirit will teach you all truth": behold the Spirit of understanding. Rom. 8: "The wisdom of the Spirit is life and peace": see the spirit of wisdom. Likewise: "The Spirit helps our weakness": see the Spirit of strength, etc. Now the external gifts are set forth. In 1 Cor. 12, after saying, "To one is given through the Spirit the word of wisdom, to another the word of knowledge according to the same Spirit, to another faith through the same Spirit" (which can certainly be referred to the internal gifts), he adds: "to another gifts of healing through the same Spirit, to another workings of powers, to another prophecy, to another discernings of spirits, to another kinds of tongues, to another interpretation of tongues. But all these one and the same Spirit works, dividing to each one individually as he wills." Those internal gifts, I say, are usually conferred on all who use the sacrament rightly, and are conferred even now; but these peculiar ones belonged to that time, when the church was newly being planted and confirmed also by a variety of signs, and were more suited to it.

units.la: Proinde huiusmodi dona spiritus Sancti seu interna, seu externa omnes in fidebaptizati acceperant, seu, vt ipse magis proprie loquitur, participauerant: Sic enim loqui conuenit, siue quia cum multis alijs communiter dona acceperant: siue quia duntaxat partem donorum, & prout vnicuique expedit, &, vt alias dicitur, secundum mensuram fidei ea conferebantur.
units.tr: Accordingly, gifts of the Holy Spirit of this kind, whether internal or external, all who were baptized in faith had received, or, as he speaks more properly, had partaken of. For it is fitting to speak thus, either because they had received them in common with many others, or because such gifts were conferred only in part, as is expedient for each, and, as is said elsewhere, according to the measure of faith.

units.la: Solus quippe Christus plenitudinem donorum habet, & non ad mensuram. Ioannis primo, Vidimus eum plenum gratia & veritate, & de plenitudine eius omnes accepimus.
units.tr: Christ alone has the fullness of the gifts, and not in measure. John 1: "We saw him full of grace and truth, and from his fullness we have all received."

units.la: Quae quib. dona conferatur, & quib. non. Dona collata iuxta mensuram fidei. Christo e donorum omnium plenitudo.
units.tr: Which gifts are conferred, and on whom they are not. The gifts were conferred according to the measure of faith. The fullness of all gifts belongs to Christ.

units.la: Ioannis tertio, Baptista de Christo, Non enim huic ad mensuram dat Deus spiritum. Cæterum veteres etiam donationem spiritus Sancti quibusdam ceremonijs volebant adumbrare. Quibusdam enim locis oleo vngere baptizandos aliqua parte corporis receptum fuit: quia vnctio etiam spiritui Sancto tribuitur, vt licet videre Lucæ 4. vbi Christus legit illud ex Esaiæ 61. Spiritus Domini super me, propterea, quòd vnxit me.
units.tr: John 3, where the Baptist speaks of Christ: "For God does not give the Spirit to him by measure." Moreover, the ancients also wanted the giving of the Holy Spirit to be shadowed forth by certain ceremonies. In some places it was customary to anoint those to be baptized with oil on some part of the body, because anointing is also attributed to the Holy Spirit, as can be seen in Luke 4, where Christ reads that passage from Isaiah 61: "The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me."

units.la: Gustaucrintq; bonum Dei uerbum) Hoc est, cùm edocti fuerint verbo Dei. Huc pertinet, quòd paulò ante inter fundamenta religionis, numerarit etiâ fundamentum doctrinæ. Oportebat enim illos de varijs rebus pertinentibus ad religionem institui, & quidem ex Dei verbo, seu ex doctrina ipsius Christi. Significanter autem vsus est metaphora in voce, gustauerit, idq; non solùm, quia verbum Dei se habet instar cibi, quo pascitur anima, verumetiam, quia significare voluit, illos nondum plenè edoctos, seu ad altiora penetrasse: sicut reuera catechumenis solidus cibus doctrinæ non proponebatur, sed tantùm lac. Itaq; gustum tantùm habuerunt doctrinæ euangelicæ, nondum saturari potuerunt. Eiusdem metaphoræ ratio habita videtur psalm. 118. Quàm dulcia faucibus meis eloquia tua super mel ori meo? Item significanter dicitur, bonum Dei uerbum, vt videlicet fructu aliqué huius percepisse eos intelligatur, & bonum dulceq; illud sensisse. Quandoquidé verbū Domini (vt habetur Esaiæ 55.) non redit ad Deum vacuum, sed semper fructum aliquem in auditorum cordibus producit, & non nisi ad bonum & salutem audientium proponi tur. Hinc & illud psal. 118. Bonum mihi lex oris tui, super millia auri & argenti. Sed non posset verbum Dei satis dignis epithetis ornari, tanta est eius excellentia & vtilitas.
units.tr: They have tasted the good word of God. That is, when they had been taught the word of God. To this belongs what he said a little earlier, that among the foundations of religion he also counted the foundation of doctrine. For those people had to be instructed in various matters pertaining to religion, and indeed from the word of God, or from the teaching of Christ himself. He uses the metaphor in the word tasted with meaning, and not only because the word of God is like food by which the soul is nourished, but also because he wished to signify that they had not yet been fully taught, or had not yet penetrated to higher things. Indeed, catechumens were not offered solid food of doctrine, but only milk. So they had only a taste of evangelical doctrine and could not yet be satisfied. The reason for this metaphor seems to be found in Psalm 118: "How sweet are your words to my palate, sweeter than honey to my mouth!" Likewise it is significantly said the good word of God, so that it is understood that they had received some fruit from it and had perceived it as good and sweet. For the word of the Lord (as is said in Isaiah 55) does not return to God empty, but always produces some fruit in the hearts of the hearers, and is set before them only for their good and salvation. Hence also that verse of Psalm 118: "The law of your mouth is good to me, better than thousands of gold and silver." But the word of God could not be adorned with epithets worthy enough, so great is its excellence and usefulness.

units.la: Ac uirtutes futuri seculi) ἀλλ' ἀμφίτεις ἐπιβ ἐτ ἂν λοιπ... Chrysostomus virtutes futuri seculi interpretatur operationes miraculorum, vel eiusmodi vitā, quae sit similis angelicæ, nihil habens cum terrenis rebus commune, solis cœlestibus contemplandis & expetendis occupata. Sed rectius, gustare virtutes futuri seculi, significauerit nobis, per doctrinam spiritus certos reddi & confirmari de bonis illis, quæ post hanc vitam sunt nobis expectanda, de quibus supra dixit in fundamentis religionis, & docemur in symbolo, in illis articulis: Carnis resurrectionem & uitam æternam: quos etiam inter fundamenta religionis paulò ante numerauit, quia ista rudibus diligenter inculcantur. Erasmus, ut hic intelligas infirmitatem, illic potentiam, quæ nunc incipit in pijs ceu pignus immortalitatis futuræ. Eiusmodi autem bona vocat virtutes, propter admirandam eorum excellentiam: quam etiam Apostolus significare volens ex Esaiæ 65. ait. 1. Corinthior. 2. Quæ oculus non vidit, quæ auris non audiuit, & in cor hominis non ascenderunt, quæ præparauit Deus diligentibus se.
units.tr: And the powers of the age to come [καὶ δυνάμεις μέλλοντος αἰῶνος]. Chrysostom interprets "the powers of the age to come" as the working of miracles, or as a kind of life like that of the angels, having nothing in common with earthly things and occupied only with contemplating and desiring heavenly things. But more correctly, "to taste the powers of the age to come" signifies to us that by the teaching of the Spirit we are made certain and confirmed about those good things which we are to expect after this life, of which he spoke above among the foundations of religion, and which we are taught in the creed, in those articles: the resurrection of the flesh and eternal life. He also counted these among the foundations of religion a little earlier, because they are carefully impressed upon beginners. Erasmus [explains] that here you understand weakness, there power, which now begins in the godly as a pledge of future immortality. He calls such goods "powers" because of their wonderful excellence, which the Apostle also wished to signify when, quoting Isaiah 65, he says in 1 Corinthians 2: "What eye has not seen, nor ear heard, nor has entered into the heart of man, these things God has prepared for those who love him."

units.la: Gustus autè eorum bonorum contingit credentibus, simul dum in aduersitatibus & tentationibus accipiunt hic mirabiles consolationes, minimeque malis commouentur, simul dum per doctrinam & spiritum sanctum certi redduntur, quòd illa ipsis sint à Deo parata. Huc refer illa Romanorum 8. Spiritus Dei testatur vnà cum spiritu nostro, quòd sumus filij Dei. Quòd si filij, & hæredes quidem Dei, cohæredes autem Christi: si quidem simul cum eo patimur, vt & vnà cum illo glorificemur. Nam reputo, non esse pares afflictiones, &c. Item omnes illi loci, qui de certitudine, de gloria vitæ æternæ & cœlestis loquuntur: item omnia exempla Sanctorum mirabiliter liberatorum à periculis: propria experientia liberationis & consolationis in certaminibus: effectus renouationis spiritualis: hæc omnia quasi gustum præbent nobis earum virtutum & amplissimorum bonorum, quæ post hanc vitam sunt expectanda. Hæc igitur tam multa tam varia sunt bona spiritualia, quæ recens amplexi euangelium & baptizati suscepepunt, quæ omnia coniunctia sunt inuicem, & consequuntur sese mutuò, magnitudinemque beneficiorum Dei statim collatorum egregiè ostendunt, vt habita eorum ratione omnes merito constantes in fide esse debeant, necnon tantò auidius progredi ad ampliora percipienda. Sed ad reliqua prodgrediamur.
units.tr: A taste of these goods comes to believers at the same time as they receive here, in adversities and temptations, wonderful consolations, and are moved very little by evils, and at the same time as they are made certain through doctrine and the Holy Spirit that those things have been prepared for them by God. Refer here Romans 8: "The Spirit of God bears witness together with our spirit that we are children of God. And if children, then heirs, heirs of God and fellow heirs with Christ; if indeed we suffer together with him, so that we may also be glorified together with him. For I reckon that the sufferings of this present time are not worth comparing..." Likewise all those passages which speak of the certainty and the glory of eternal and heavenly life; likewise all the examples of the saints marvellously delivered from dangers; the personal experience of deliverance and consolation in conflicts; the effects of spiritual renewal. All these things, as it were, provide us with a taste of those powers and of the very great goods which are to be expected after this life. Therefore these so many and so varied spiritual goods, which those who had recently embraced the gospel and been baptized received, are all joined together and follow one another, and they clearly show the greatness of God's benefits bestowed at once, so that, having regard to them, all should rightly be steadfast in the faith, and be all the more eager to advance to receive greater things. But let us proceed to the rest.

units.la: Si prolabantur) Aptè verò exprimit, ne metaphora naturæ humanæ infirmitatem, qua non possumus in iustitia Spiritus subsistere, sed necessariò, si non adsit sustentatio diuinæ opis, in peccata in cidimus.
units.tr: If they fall away. He expresses it aptly, lest by the metaphor we think of the weakness of human nature, by which we cannot stand in the righteousness of the Spirit, but necessarily fall into sins unless the support of divine help is present.

units.la: Denuò renouari per pœnitentiam) Græcè, πάλιν ἀνακαινίζειν, hoc est, rursus renouare. Nam actua vox est, sed subaudiendum, se, quasi diceret: Impossibile est illos renouare se. Interpres annotauit ex Chrysostomo, εἰς positum pro ἐν, & ἐν pro ἀπό, more Hebraeo, (licut initio epistolæ, ἐν τοῖς προφήταις) sequè id uertisse, per pœnitentiam. Fortasis non tam longè deducendo, significantius dixisset, renouare in pœnitentia, id est, baptismo, quod est sacramentum pœnitentiæ: εἰς simpliciter accipiendo pro ἐν: sed istud nullius momenti est.
units.tr: To be renewed again through repentance. In Greek, πάλιν ἀνακαινίζειν [palin anakainizein], that is, to renew again. For the verb is active, but "themselves" must be understood, as if he said: it is impossible for them to renew themselves. The translator noted, following Chrysostom, that εἰς is put for ἐν, and ἐν for ἀπό, after the Hebrew manner (as at the beginning of the epistle, ἐν τοῖς προφήταις), and so he translated it "through repentance".
