Yet God willed that such helps and instruments exist, by which our weakness and memory might be aided. And in those very things the will of God is set before us, so that when we have applied ourselves to the things themselves with our whole mind, and with the help of the Holy Spirit implored, we may also perceive inwardly a wonderful fruit from the doctrine set forth there, just as we said above about vocal preaching and the gathering and searching of the Scriptures.

units.la: Quæcunque scripta sunt, ad nostrā doctrinā præscripta sunt, Roman. 15. Item Actor. 8. multum profuit Eunucho præfecto Candaces reginæ Aethiopū, quòd iter faciens sacris literis legendis occuparetur. O quale exemplū diligentię in gentili Apollos (Actor. 18.) commendatur, quòd in scripturis esset diu ac bene versatus. 1. Timoth. 4. Donec venero attende lectioni, exhortationi, doctrinæ, 2. Timoth. 3. At tu perfistito in his, quæ didicisti, & quæ tibi credita sunt, sciens, à quo didiceris, & quòd à puero sacras literas noueris, quæ te possunt eruditum reddere ad salutem, per fidem, quæ est in Christo Iesu, omnis scriptura diuinitus inspirata, & vtilis ad doctrinam, ad redargutionem, ad correctionem, ad institutionem, quæ est in iustitia. Viden' sacris literis tribui, quòd possint eruditū reddere ad salutem? Atque hinc clarum est, quod si quibus videatur noxium scripturarum studium, vel, si videatur parum proficere, id non est imputandum ipsi scripturæ, sed perverso abutentium ea ingenio.
units.tr: Whatever things have been written were written for our teaching (Rom. 15.). Likewise in Acts 8, the eunuch, chief officer of Candace queen of the Ethiopians, greatly profited because, while travelling, he occupied himself with reading the holy letters. O what an example of diligence is commended in the Gentile Apollos (Acts 18.), that he was long and well versed in the Scriptures. 1 Tim. 4: "Until I come, attend to reading, exhortation, and teaching." 2 Tim. 3: "But you, persist in those things which you have learned and which have been entrusted to you, knowing from whom you learned them, and that from childhood you have known the holy letters, which can make you wise unto salvation through faith which is in Christ Jesus. All Scripture is divinely inspired and profitable for teaching, for reproof, for correction, for instruction, which is in righteousness." Do you see that the holy letters are credited with being able to make one wise unto salvation? And hence it is clear that if to some the study of the Scriptures seems harmful, or if it seems to profit little, this is not to be imputed to Scripture itself, but to the perverse disposition of those who abuse it.

units.la: Omnibus ad salutē est propositā scriptura ex æquo: sed multū refert, quo quis animo eam legat siue tractet: sicut de Christo dixit Simeon, signum esse aliis in ruinam, aliis in resurrectionem, ita & de scriptura rectè potest statui. Apostolus 1. Corinth. 1. dicit, Euangelium, siue sermonem de cruce & morte Christi, ijs quidem, qui pereunt, stultitiam esse, at nobis, qui salutem consequimur, potentiam esse Dei. Quemadmodum igitur pleræque aliæ res, imò cibus, potus, vestitus, quibus omnino carere nō possumus, alijs rectè vtentibus sunt salutares, alijs verò, abutentibus inquam, vt ad crapulam, faustum, sunt noxiæ. Ita de Scripturis imò & de vniuersa cognitione Dei iudicari potest. Legit pius scripturā, & instar apiculæ colligit mel sanæ doctrinæ & consolationum: legit impius scripturam, & instar aranei exfugit venenum falsorum dogmatum & hæreseos. Non est ergo, quod patiantur pij, sibi ob has causas excuti e manibus sacra biblia, aut quòd remisiores in legendo & proficiēdo reddantur. Cauete tales pestes studiosi iuuenes, & scripturam, quæ propositā est, vt reddat vos eruditos ad salutem, sicut Paulus ad suum Timotheum ait, date operam, vt ad vestram vtilitatem conuertatis.
units.tr: Scripture is set before all alike for salvation, but it matters greatly with what mind a person reads or handles it. Just as Simeon said of Christ that he was a sign for the fall of some and the rising of others, so one may rightly judge concerning Scripture. The Apostle in 1 Cor. 1 says that the gospel, or the word about the cross and death of Christ, is foolishness to those who perish, but to us who obtain salvation it is the power of God. Just as many other things, indeed food, drink and clothing, which we cannot at all do without, are salutary to those who use them rightly, but harmful to those who abuse them, that is, to gluttony and drunkenness, so one may judge concerning the Scriptures, and indeed concerning the whole knowledge of God. The pious man reads Scripture and, like a little bee, gathers the honey of sound doctrine and consolations; the impious man reads Scripture and, like a spider, sucks out the poison of false dogmas and heresy. There is therefore no reason for the pious to allow the sacred Bible to be snatched from their hands on these grounds, or to become more lax in reading and profiting. Beware of such pests, studious young men, and of the Scripture set before you so that it may make you wise unto salvation; as Paul said to his Timothy, "Take care that you turn these things to your own profit."

units.la: Iam etiam non erit difficile conciliare locos hos, qui in speciem videntur pugnantes, quibus videlicet dicitur, Omnes doctos à Deo, seu Spiritu sancto, hic apud Ieremiam. Item Ioelis 2. Esaiæ 45. &c. Et rursus, quibus monentur homines ad legendum, audiendum, & discendum, item quibus constituuntur in ecclesia doctores, Euangelistæ & fi-miles: vt 1. Corinth. 12. Ephes. 4.
units.tr: Now it will not be difficult to reconcile these passages which seem at first sight to conflict: those in which it is said that all are taught by God or by the Holy Spirit (here in Jeremiah; likewise Joel 2, Isaiah 45, etc.), and again those in which men are urged to read, hear and learn, and likewise those in which teachers, evangelists and the like are appointed in the Church, as in 1 Cor. 12 and Eph. 4.

units.la: Respondendum est, quòd, quia non omnibus datur exacta cognitio, vt experientia ipsa docet: & fides est ex auditu: atq; oportet etiam infirmas conscientias & fide & patientia alere & conseruare: idque tum propter ingenitam hominibus infirmitatem, tum propter graues tentationes subinde obuenietes: ideo debent in ecclesia haberi, qui alios doceant in verbo, atq; instituant: et licet plures fortasis doctrina præsteret in loco aliquo, aut reuelationem à spiritu habeant, tamē, vt omnia cum decoro et ordinatē fiant in ecclesia, docente eo, qui publicē ad id ordinatus est, illi taceant, neq; temerē docendi munus usurpant. Rursus autem & si doctores esse hoc modo necessum sit, tamen profectus discentium his acceptus non feretur, sed Deo seu Spiritui sancto intus agenti & incrementum danti, sicut supra diximus. Atque ita simul erunt, qui discant, & qui doceant, & tamen qui verè edocti fuerint, à Spiritu sancto edocti erunt. Tantum contra phanaticos nostri temporis Spiritus. Nunc quæ ad doctrinam & consolationem faciunt, congeramus. Illud inprimis valde consolatorium est, & quod ad bene agendum debet nobis magnum calcar addere, quòd Euangelium prædicatur, sancitum esse præstantioribus promissis, quàm lex Lex.
units.tr: It must be answered that, since exact knowledge is not given to all, as experience itself teaches, and faith comes by hearing, and it is also necessary to nourish and preserve weak consciences by faith and patience, and this both on account of the weakness innate in men and on account of the grievous temptations which arise from time to time, therefore there ought to be in the Church those who teach others in the word and instruct them. And although perhaps some in a certain place excel in learning, or have a revelation from the Spirit, nevertheless, so that everything may be done in the Church decently and in order, while the one who has been publicly ordained for this purpose is teaching, those others should keep silent and not rashly usurp the office of teaching. Again, although it is necessary in this way that there be teachers, the progress of the learners is nevertheless not to be credited to these, but to God or the Holy Spirit working inwardly and giving the increase, as we said above. And so at once there will be those who learn and those who teach, and yet those who have truly been taught will have been taught by the Holy Spirit. This is enough against the fanatics of our time. Now let us gather together what pertains to doctrine and consolation. Above all this is very consoling, and ought to add a great spur to acting well, that the gospel is proclaimed as sanctioned by more excellent promises than the law.

units.la: Promissa & propositā præmia quemuis extimulent ad laborem ac diligentiam. Hoc à natura omnibus inditū est. Quamobrem Deus patribus in lege propositū semper præmia, quoties de obseruandis præceptis ageret, sicut licet vbique videre in lege & prophetis. phetis. Atque illa ferè erant temporalia, & de bonis temporalibus. Et nihilominus plu<note side="right">A minori ad maius.</note>rimi è patribus fuerunt multò diligentissimi obseruatores legis.
units.tr: Promises and set rewards stir anyone to labour and diligence. This is implanted in all by nature. Wherefore God always set before the fathers rewards under the law, whenever he spoke of observing the precepts, as can be seen everywhere in the law and the prophets. And those rewards were for the most part temporal, concerning temporal goods. Yet nonetheless very many of the fathers were far more diligent observers of the law. [From the lesser to the greater.]

units.la: Quare nos decet multo esse diligentiores ad perficiendum voluntatem Dei, quando proposita habemus præmia multo ampliora, nempe spiritualia & æterna: ac pudere nos debet, si nostra iustitia non plus, quàm iustitia scribarum & pharifæorum, abundauerit.
units.tr: Wherefore it becomes us to be much more diligent in performing the will of God, since we have set before us much greater rewards, namely spiritual and eternal ones; and we ought to be ashamed if our righteousness does not abound more than the righteousness of the scribes and Pharisees.

units.la: Quid dico scribarum &Pharisæorum? Imò & patrum antecedentium corruptissima illa scribarum & pharisæorum tempora. Discipiat obsecro quiuis apud se, an habeat aliquando talium præmiorum rationem, an horum magnitudine se excitet ad virtute: aut an se in aduersis consoletur?
units.tr: What do I say, of the scribes and Pharisees? Indeed, of the most corrupt times of the scribes and Pharisees, and of the fathers who went before them. Let anyone, I beg, examine himself: does he ever take account of such rewards, and is he stirred to virtue by their greatness, or does he console himself in adversities?

units.la: Nam, ut de consolatione dicam, nonne consolatio amplissima est proposita ad constanter ferenda aduersa, in spe tantorum bonorum? Quid aliud sibi vult apostolus, vbi ait Roman. 8. Non reputo, esse pares afflictiones præsentis temporis, ad gloriam quæ reuelabitur erga nos: nisi, ut respectu præmiorum simus in omnibus aduersitatibus constates?
units.tr: For, to speak of consolation, is not the most ample consolation set before us for bearing adversities steadfastly, in the hope of such great goods? What else does the apostle mean when he says in Rom. 8: "I reckon that the sufferings of the present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory that shall be revealed in us," unless it is that, with regard to the rewards, we may be constant in all adversities?

units.la: Tertiò, cùm dicitur, prius illud testamentum tale fuisse, ut in eo adhuc sit aliquid desideratum, id verò fuerit, quòd per illud non potuerit obtineri iustitia coram Deo, quando quidem neque in illum finem fuit datum: debet istud quoque nos extimulare ad bene agendum: quando videlicet ita nobis proposita est iustitia coram deo per fidem in Christum obtinenda in euangelio, quod patribus sanè nunquàm ita aperte & certò fuit manifestatum: pariterq; est, quod agamus gratias, quibus datum est videre, quæ patres non viderunt, sicut Christus quoq; Lucæ 10. ait, Beati oculi, qui vident, quæ vos videtis. Dico enim vobis, quòd multi prophetæ & reges voluerunt videre, quæ vos videtis, & non viderunt, & audire quæ auditis, & non audierunt.
units.tr: Thirdly, when it is said that the former covenant was such that something was still lacking in it, namely that through it righteousness before God could not be obtained, since it was not given for that purpose at all, this too ought to spur us on to live well. For righteousness before God, to be obtained through faith in Christ, is now set before us in the gospel, which was certainly never so openly and certainly revealed to the fathers. Likewise we should give thanks, we to whom it has been given to see what the fathers did not see, as Christ also says in Luke 10: "Blessed are the eyes that see what you see. For I tell you that many prophets and kings have desired to see what you see and did not see it, and to hear what you hear and did not hear it."

units.la: Magna est ergo eorum fœlicitas, meritòque agent Deo gratias, quibus contigit reuelationem Euangelij agnoscere, de qua Christus etiam ante illa verba apud Lucam disserit.
units.tr: Great, then, is the happiness of those to whom it has fallen to recognise the revelation of the gospel, and they will rightly give thanks to God. Christ speaks of this before those words in Luke.

units.la: Sed nos, qui incidimus in hæc quoque tempora, quibus denuò cœpit lux euangelica post totseculorum tenebras illucescere, qua ratione Deo grati erimus? Væ interim nobis si beneficijs Dei non recte utamur.
units.tr: But we, who have fallen upon these times also, in which the light of the gospel has begun again to dawn after the darkness of so many ages, how shall we be grateful to God? Woe to us, meanwhile, if we do not use the benefits of God rightly.

units.la: Cùm verò dicitur, istud nouum testamentum consummandum, super domum Israel, & domum Iuda, admonemur sedulò orare Dominum, ut nos quoque velit his annumerare familijs, id est, nos pro ueris Israelitis secundum spiritum agnoscere, & fide Sanctorum patrum illustrare, & sic in fœdus suum recipere, nec no spiritualium promissionum participes efficere.
units.tr: When it is said that this new covenant is to be completed "upon the house of Israel and the house of Judah," we are urged to pray diligently to the Lord that he would also deign to count us among these families, that is, to acknowledge us as true Israelites according to the Spirit, to illuminate us with the faith of the holy fathers, and so to receive us into his covenant and make us partakers of the spiritual promises.

units.la: Quinetiá discimus, quòd, sicut vanū erat iactare Israelis aut Iudæ familiá, ubi non erat sanctorum patriarcharum fides & charitas: ita vanum erit & nobis, iactare, nos esse Christianos, si interea tota uita à Christi doctrina dissentiamus & nihil tanto nomine dignum præ nobis feramus.
units.tr: Indeed we learn that, just as it was vain to boast of being of the family of Israel or Judah where the faith and love of the holy patriarchs was not present, so it will be vain for us too to boast that we are Christians, if meanwhile our whole life dissents from the doctrine of Christ and we show nothing worthy of so great a name.

units.la: Quintò, cum describitur Deus Israelitas apprehesa manu educer e ex Ægypto, monemur intueri in ipsius bonitatem & potentiam, nec non nostram ipsorum infirmitatem, ac proinde nos ipsi commendare, toti ex illo pendere, nihil sine implorata illius ope attentare.
units.tr: Fifthly, when God is described as having led the Israelites out of Egypt by the hand, we are reminded to look upon his goodness and power, and also upon our own weakness, and accordingly to commend ourselves to him, to depend wholly upon him, and to attempt nothing without imploring his help.

units.la: Ipse est, qui nos pascit, fouet, seruat, regit, defendit, in omnibus, & per omnia, & sine quo nihil possumus facere.
units.tr: He is the one who feeds us, cherishes, preserves, rules and defends us in all things and through all things, and without whom we can do nothing.

units.la: Sextò, quādo additur, ideo renouandum pactum, quòd patres non steterunt promissis, admonemur orare Deum, ut nobis donet constantiam, qua perstemus in ijs, quæ semel in accepto signo fœderis, id est, baptismo promisimus, Deo semper præstemus debitam obedietiam, agnoscamus illum pro eo, qui verè ipse est, id est, pro Deo, & nos simus ipsi fidelis populus, ne ipse nos abijciat, & alios in locum nostrum eligat, sicut cum Iudæis factum scimus, & nos nisi respiscamus, nobiscum ita faciendum metuere debemus.
units.tr: Sixthly, when it is added that the covenant had to be renewed because the fathers did not keep their promises, we are reminded to pray God to grant us constancy, so that we may persevere in what we once promised in receiving the sign of the covenant, that is, in baptism: that we always render God the obedience due to him, acknowledge him as the one he truly is, that is, as God, and that we ourselves be a faithful people, lest he cast us off and choose others in our place, as we know was done with the Jews. Unless we repent, we ought to fear that the same will be done to us.

units.la: Septimò, quādo dicitur, nouum testamentum eiusmodi fore, in quo inscribantur legis in cordibus, & donetur spiritus Sanctus vice legum, mentes gubernans, orandum nobis est, ut Deus corda nostra semper emolliat, vereque efficiat nos Spiritus Sancti habitacula, huiusque ductu possimus bonam ipsius voluntatem in omnibus perficere, & sicut decet veros filios spiritu adoptionis, non timoris præditos, ipsius nomen assiduè inuocare.
units.tr: Seventhly, when it is said that the new covenant will be of such a kind that the laws are written in hearts, and the Holy Spirit is given in place of laws, governing the minds, we must pray that God would always soften our hearts and truly make us dwelling places of the Holy Spirit, and that by his guidance we may be able to carry out his good will in all things, and, as true sons endowed with the Spirit of adoption and not of fear, call upon his name constantly.

units.la: Octauo, formula illa fœderis, Ego ero illis Deus, & ipsi erunt mihi populus, eiusmodi est, quæ merito deberet nobis per omnem vitam versari ob oculos, & nos in fide atque obedientia erga Deum confirmare: Rursus autem omnia bona nobis indubitatò ab illo solo polliceri, ut qui haud dubiè promissis stare semper velit, & nihil non possit.
units.tr: Eighthly, that formula of the covenant, "I will be their God, and they shall be my people," is of such a kind that it ought rightly to be kept before our eyes throughout our whole life, and to confirm us in faith and obedience toward God. And again, it promises us all good things from him alone, undoubtedly, since he who surely wishes always to keep his promises is able to do all things.

units.la: Nonò, promissio de donatione Spiritus Sancti, ut Deum omnes possimus plenè cognoscere, etiam ad inuocationem diuini nominis omni tempore nos debet instigare, in studijs literarijs semper pꝛæfixa esse, vt cogitemus, conatibus nostris Deum aspiraturum, daturumque mirabilem profectum in spiritualibus, si modo ipsi, quantum in nobis est, fœdus seruemus, & quod officij nostri est, diligenter faciamus.
units.tr: Ninthly, the promise concerning the gift of the Holy Spirit, so that we may all be able to know God fully, ought to stir us at all times to call upon the divine name. It ought always to be placed before us in our literary studies, so that we may reflect that God will breathe upon our efforts and give a remarkable progress in spiritual things, if only we keep the covenant with him, as far as lies in us, and diligently do what belongs to our duty.

units.la: Postremò, promissio illa de gratuita remissione peccatorum dici non potest quàm consolatoria sit in omnibus tentationibus, quæ vel à carne nostra, vel à diabolo immittuntur, hosque ad desperandum volunt cogere.
units.tr: Lastly, that promise of the free forgiveness of sins cannot be described as anything but consoling in all temptations, whether they are sent by our flesh or by the devil, and seek to drive us to despair.

units.la: Per hoc squod dicit nouum, antiquauit prius. Porrò, quod antiquatur ac senescit in propinquo est, vt euanescat.
units.tr: In that he saith, A new covenant, he hath made the first old. Now that which decayeth and waxeth old is ready to vanish away.

units.la: Productum quidem erat testimonium prophetæ, ad probandum, quòd secundo testamento quæsitus fuerit locus: iam verò licet quasi aliud agendo, peroportunè tamen arguemntum trahit Apostolus ex voce Nouum, quæ in eo posita erat, & colligit, ea aperte significari testamentum, quòd tùm habebatur, veterascere, ac proinde certo tempore abrogandum.
units.tr: The testimony of the prophet had indeed been produced to prove that a place had been sought for a second covenant. Now, although as if doing something else, the Apostle very aptly draws an argument from the word "new," which stood in that passage, and concludes that this clearly signifies that the covenant then in force is growing old, and therefore must be abrogated at a certain time.

units.la: Neque enim nouum dici, nisi respectu alicuius veteris, quod cùm prorsus antiquatur, debet ei nouum succeedere.
units.tr: For a thing is not called new except in relation to something old, and when that is utterly becoming obsolete, the new ought to succeed it.

units.la: Quod argumentum multò prudentissimè interposuit, cum quòd eo rursus confirmet id, quod capite præcedenti asseruerat, videlicet, sacerdotium pariter cum lege abrogari: tum quòd tacitè suggerat omnium animis, quid mox dicere conueniat de legalibus sacrificijs, nempe non aliud, quàm quòd hic generaliter dicitur de toto testamento, hoc est, ipsa quoque sacrificia similiter antiquata, & per nouum sacrificium Christi abolita.
units.tr: He introduced this argument most prudently: partly because by it he confirms again what he had asserted in the preceding chapter, namely that the priesthood is abrogated along with the law; and partly because he tacitly suggests to the minds of all what it is fitting to say soon about the legal sacrifices, namely nothing other than what is said here generally about the whole covenant: that the sacrifices too are likewise made obsolete and abolished through the new sacrifice of Christ.

units.la: Est autem hic, vt alias quoque, quotiescunque citantur testimonia Scripturarum, aduertendum mirabile acumen in Apostolo, qui ex vna voce tàm graue & tàm perspicuum argumentum collegerit.
units.tr: Now here, as elsewhere too, whenever testimonies of Scripture are cited, one must note the remarkable acuteness of the Apostle, who from a single word gathered an argument so weighty and so clear.

units.la: Habemus insigne exemplum diligentiæ in legendis Scripturis, & quomodo in singula verba oporteat nos valde seriò esse intentos.
units.tr: We have a notable example of diligence in reading the Scriptures, and of how we ought to be very earnestly attentive to each single word.

units.la: Reuera autem non est aliud argumentum, quo acrius punguntur Iudæi, atque isto, quod sumitur ex præsenti vaticinio Hieremiæ.
units.tr: In truth there is no other argument by which the Jews are more sharply pricked than this one, which is drawn from the present prophecy of Jeremiah.

units.la: Dicit enim propheta aperte, nouum testamentum esse constituendum, atque id quidem diuersum ab eo, quod olim percussit Dominus cum patribus, quos eduxit de terra Aegypti.
units.tr: For the prophet says plainly that a new covenant is to be established, and indeed one different from that which the Lord once made with the fathers whom he led out of the land of Egypt.

units.la: Quid obsecro dici queat manifestius? Quomodo possunt tergiuersari, aut euadere, quin cogantur concedere, clarissimè hic dici, quòd nouum quoddam testamentum fit successurum per quod aboleatur vetus? Quamobrem ad retundendam iudaicam peruicaciam hoc argumentum, & si quæ alia similia occurrunt, diligenter est obseruandum.
units.tr: What, I beg you, could be said more plainly? How can they evade or escape, without being forced to concede, that it is said here clearly that a certain new covenant is to succeed, through which the old is to be abolished? Therefore, in order to refute Jewish obstinacy, this argument, and any other similar ones that occur, must be carefully observed.

units.la: Confugiunt quidem Iudæi ad alia quædam præsidia, sed eiusmodi, quæ persistere haud possunt, & nunquam satisfaciunt nostris obiectionibus, inprimis huic petitæ ex Ieremia.
units.tr: The Jews indeed take refuge in certain other defences, but of such a kind that they cannot hold up, and they never satisfy our objections, especially this one drawn from Jeremiah.

units.la: Habent verò in promptu quosdam locos Scripturæ qui videntur sonare legem ipsorum debere durare in æternum: propter quos contenderunt nonnulli initio reuelatæ Euangelij, simul cum Euangelio seruandam legem: atque in hunc diem pertinaciter legi suæ addicti sunt.
units.tr: They have ready at hand, however, certain passages of Scripture which seem to sound that their law ought to endure for ever. On account of these some, at the beginning of the revealed gospel, contended that the law was to be kept together with the gospel; and to this day they are stubbornly devoted to their law.

units.la: Hi sunt huiusmodi: Genef.17. de circumcisione. Eritq; pactum meum in carne vestra in sœdus æternum. Exodi 12. de esu agni pascalis, Habebitis diem hunc in monimentum, & celebrabitis eum solennem Domino in generationibus vestris cultu sempiterno. Ibidem eadem de re, Custodi verbum istud legitimum tibi & filijs tuis usque in æternum. Exodi 31. de custodiendo sabbato.
units.tr: These are passages of this kind: Genesis 17, concerning circumcision: "And my covenant shall be in your flesh for an everlasting covenant." Exodus 12, concerning the eating of the Passover lamb: "You shall keep this day as a memorial, and you shall celebrate it as a feast to the Lord throughout your generations, with an everlasting observance." In the same place, on the same matter: "Keep this statute for you and your sons for ever." Exodus 31, concerning the keeping of the sabbath.

units.la: Item in Leuitico præcepta de offerendis primitijs frugum alijsque oblationibus & sacrificijs: item de solennitate pentecostes, de die propitiationis, de panibus propositionis, & similibus.
units.tr: Likewise in Leviticus the precepts concerning the offering of the first fruits of the harvest and other oblations and sacrifices; likewise concerning the solemnity of Pentecost, the day of atonement, the showbread, and similar things.

units.la: Hæc igitur præcepta feré semper adiunctum habent, quòd debeant in æternum seruari. Atque hisce locutionibus potissimum innituntur Iudæi. Sed facile est omnia ista diluere. Negare non posunt Iudæi, vocem לעולם (quam vertunt nostri in æternum) non semper significare tempus perpetuò duraturum, siue non habens finem: sed subindè etiam significat tempus bene longum & determinatum, quemadmodum ipsorum Rabini crebrò interpretantur, & necessitas sententiæ nonnunquàm cogit: ut Deuter.15. de seruo nolente donari libertate anno septimo: Si dixerit, nolo egredi, quòd diligat te & domum tuam, & bene sibi apud te esse sentiat, assumes subulam, & perforabis aurem eius in ianua domus tuæ, & seruiet tibi vsque in æternum. Quo loco manifestum est, non posse manere seruum in aeternum: Ergo necessum est accipi pro tepore vitae ipsius. Item 1. Regum 1. Mater Samuelis nolens cum marito Helcana proficisci Hierosolymam ait, non vadam, donec ablactetur infans, & ducam eum, ut appareat ante conspectum Domini, ut maneat ibi iugiter: vbi etiam habetur in Hebraeo עד-עולם in seculum, quod reddunt, in aeternum: cum interea Leuitae non ministrabant nisi quinquaginta annis: ut habemus Numeror. 18. Et Rabi Kimhi Esaiae 40. diserte exponit, ונעל subinde significare tempus longum quidem, sed determinatum, & aliquando finiendum. Quin etiam cum proprie significat, quod nobis aeternum est, & sine fine, tum fere semper ei addi particulam, עד, id est, & vltra: quando videlicet sermo est de re, quae aliàs finem habitura iudicatur. Quamobrem etiam saepè vertunt nomine, seculi, quae vox etiam nobis longum quidem, sed tamen finitum tempus significat. Cyrillus lib. 4. in Leuiticum, dicit, legem & sacrificia dici aeterna, quatenus intelligitur lex, &c. Ex his liquet, quam infirmum sit Iudaeorum fundamentum, & quod illa testimonia non satis euincant, legem ipsorum (loquimur potissimum de ceremonialibus) debere in aeternum durare. Nos hic aperte habemus apud Hieremiam de nouo testamento constituendo, & aliis multis in locis de abrogatione ceremoniarum occurrunt vaticinia: cuiusmodi quaedam Apostolus citat, & adhuc citabit, ut capite decimo, Sacrificium & oblationem noluisti, &c.
units.tr: These precepts almost always carry the qualification that they are to be observed for ever, and the Jews rely chiefly on these expressions. But all of this is easily refuted. The Jews cannot deny that the word לעולם (which our translators render "for ever") does not always mean a time that will last perpetually, or without end. It also often means a fairly long but determinate time, as their own rabbis frequently explain, and the sense of a passage sometimes requires it. Take Deut. 15, concerning the servant who does not want to be freed in the seventh year: "If he says, I will not go out, because he loves you and your house, and feels well with you, you shall take an awl and pierce his ear at your door, and he shall serve you for ever [לעולם]." Here it is plain that the servant cannot remain for ever, so the word must be understood as the length of his own life. Likewise in 1 Sam. 1, Samuel's mother, unwilling to go up with her husband Elkanah to Jerusalem, says: "I will not go until the child is weaned, and I will bring him, that he may appear before the Lord and remain there for ever [עד-עולם]." In the Hebrew there is עד-עולם, "unto the age," which they render "for ever," although the Levites ministered only until fifty years of age, as we have it in Num. 18. Rabbi Kimchi, too, expressly explains on Isa. 40 that ולעולם sometimes signifies a long but determinate time, one that will at some point come to an end. Indeed, even where it properly signifies what is eternal for us and without end, it is nearly always joined with the particle עד, that is, "and beyond," namely when the subject is something judged otherwise destined to have an end. For this reason the translators often render it by the word "age," which in our usage also denotes a long but nevertheless finite time. Cyril, in book 4 on Leviticus, says that the law and the sacrifices are called eternal insofar as the law is understood, and so on. From these points it is clear how weak is the foundation of the Jews, and that those testimonies do not sufficiently prove that their law (we speak chiefly of the ceremonial law) must endure for ever. We have here plainly in Jeremiah the promise of establishing a new covenant, and in many other places prophecies of the abrogation of the ceremonies occur. The Apostle cites some of these, and will cite more, as in chapter ten: "Sacrifice and offering you did not desire," and so on.

units.la: CAPUT NONUM.
units.tr: CHAPTER NINE.

units.la: Igitur habebat quidem etiam prius illud iustificationes, cultus, ac sanctum mundanum: siquidem tabernaculum factum fuit primum, in quo erant lucerna, & mensa, & propositio panum, quam vocant, sancta. Post secundum autem velum erat tabernaculum, quod vocatur Sanctum Sanctorum, aureum habens thuribulum, & arcam testamenti vndique circumtectam auro, in qua vrna aurea habens manna & virga Aaron, quae germinauerat, & tabulae testamenti. Supra hanc autem Cherubim gloriae, obumbrantia propitiatorium, de quibus non est nunc dicendum singulatim. His autem ad hunc ordinatis modum, in prius quidem tabernaculum semper ingrediuntur sacerdotes, qui sacrorum ritus peragant: in secundum autem semel quotannis solus pontifex non sine sanguine, quem offert pro seipso, & populi ignorantiis, illud significante spiritu Sancto, nondum manifestatam esse sanctorum viam, adhuc priore tabernaculo consistente. Quae erat similitudo pro tempore tum praesente, in quo dona sacrificiaq; offeruntur, quae non possint iuxta conscientiam perfectum reddere cultorem, in cibis duntaxat & potionibus, & diuersis ablutionibus ac iustificationibus carnis usque ad tempus correctionis impositia. At Christus accedens pontifex futurorum bonorum, per maius & perfectius tabernaculum, non manu factum hoc est, non huius structurae, neque per sanguinem hircorum ac vitulorum, sed per proprium sanguinem ingressus est semel in sancta, aeterna redemptione reperta.
units.tr: Then indeed the first covenant also had ordinances of divine service, and a worldly sanctuary. For there was a tabernacle made, the first, wherein was the candlestick, and the table, and the shewbread, which is called the sanctuary. And after the second veil, the tabernacle which is called the Holiest of all; which had the golden censer, and the ark of the covenant overlaid round about with gold, wherein was the golden pot that had the manna, and Aaron's rod that budded, and the tables of the covenant; and over it the cherubims of glory shadowing the mercyseat; of which we cannot now speak particularly. Now when these things were thus ordained, the priests went always into the first tabernacle, accomplishing the service of God. But into the second went the high priest alone once every year, not without blood, which he offered for himself, and for the errors of the people; the Holy Ghost this signifying, that the way into the holiest of all was not yet made manifest, while as the first tabernacle was yet standing. Which was a figure for the time then present, in which were offered both gifts and sacrifices, that could not make him that did the service perfect, as pertaining to the conscience; which stood only in meats and drinks, and divers washings, and carnal ordinances, imposed on them until the time of reformation. But Christ being come an high priest of good things to come, by a greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with hands, that is to say, not of this building; neither by the blood of goats and calves, but by his own blood he entered in once into the holy place, having obtained eternal redemption.

units.la: Am descendit ad exprimendum, quodnam fuerit excellentissimum Christi sacrificium. Sunt autem, ut perspicuam & integram habeamus sententiam, omnia haec ab initio capitis ad illum usque locum, Nam si sanguis taurorum, &c. coniungenda. Atq; ut breuiter explicemus Apostoli mentem, nos vna periodo, omnia quae necessaria sunt ad absoluendam sententiam, comprehendemus, neglectis iis, quae omitti commode possunt, etiamsi nihil otiose fit additum. Sic ergo respiciens ad id, quod Paulo ante dixerat, videlicet, sacerdotium legale in terra deseruire exemplari atq; umbrae coelestium (quod dictum vna cum probatione adhibita admonuimus quasi fundamentum esse & basin multorum, quae in hac secunda parte disputationis proferuntur, ideoq; diligenter obseruandum) de sacrificio Christi pergit apertius differere, huiusmodi penè verbis incipiens.
units.tr: Now he descends to explain what was the most excellent sacrifice of Christ. In order to have a clear and complete understanding, all of these things, from the beginning of the chapter down to that place, "For if the blood of bulls," etc., must be joined together. And so that we may briefly explain the mind of the Apostle, we shall comprehend in one period everything that is necessary to complete the sentence, setting aside those things which can conveniently be omitted, even though nothing superfluous has been added. Thus, looking back to what he had said a little earlier, namely that the legal priesthood served in earth as a copy and shadow of heavenly things (which we pointed out, together with the proof given, as the foundation and base of many things brought forward in this second part of the disputation, and therefore to be carefully noted), he goes on to discuss the sacrifice of Christ more openly, beginning in almost these words.

units.la: Quando igitur his ita constitutis, quod nimirum sacerdotium legale in terra deseruient exemplari atque umbrae rerum Euangelicarum seu coelestium: quemadmodum in priori testamento tabernaculum habebatur magnificentissimè apparatum, ut in eo certus locus appellatus sancta sanctorum, quem semel quotannis solus pontifex ingrediebatur, non sine sanguine tamen, quem pro populi ignorantijs offerebat: ita & Christus accedens pontifex noui testamenti & futurorum bonorum etiam ingressus est semel in tabernaculum quoddam & in eo etiam Sancta Sanctorum: praeterea non sine sanguine, quem pro peccatis populi obtulit. His inquam paucis ad hunc modum seorsum congestis sententia Apostoli absoluitur. Apostolus simpliciter confert typum siue vmbram cum re ipsa, sequens id, quod pro fundamento supra posuerat: ac prius quidem vsitato more collationum seu similitudinum vmbrá proponit, mox addit rem ipsam de Christo, & in Christo vere adimpletam. Quomodo obsecro potuisset tantundem dici facilius aut crassius? Hoc iterum notandum, quod Apostolus posteriorem partem effert quadam contentionis forma, ita ut eadem opera clare & nominet tabernaculum, quod Christus semel ingressus est: item sacrificium, quod obtulit, (quod alioqui postea debuisset seorsim plenius facere) & significet pariter ista multis parasangis excellentiora esse, qua fuerint illa in veteri testamento. Quod reuera artificiosissime factum est, ac dignitatem sacrificij statim valde illustrat.
units.tr: Therefore, when these things have been established, namely that the legal priesthood served in earth as a copy and shadow of evangelical or heavenly realities: just as in the former covenant the tabernacle was furnished most magnificently, having a certain place called the Holy of Holies, which only the high priest entered once a year, yet not without blood, which he offered for the ignorances of the people; so Christ, coming as high priest of the new covenant and of good things to come, also entered once into a certain tabernacle and, in it, into the Holy of Holies; moreover not without blood, which he offered for the sins of the people. With these few things, I say, gathered together in this way apart, the Apostle's sentence is completed. The Apostle simply compares the type or shadow with the reality itself, following what he had laid down as the foundation: and first, in the usual manner of comparisons or likenesses, he sets forth the shadow, and then presently adds the reality itself, truly fulfilled concerning Christ and in Christ. How, I ask you, could the same thing have been said more easily or more plainly? This again is to be noted, that the Apostle expresses the latter part in a certain form of contrast, so that at the same time he clearly names the tabernacle which Christ entered once, and likewise the sacrifice which he offered (which otherwise he would afterwards have had to treat separately and more fully), and at the same time signifies that these things are many parasangs more excellent than those in the Old Testament. This has indeed been done most skilfully, and it immediately sets off the dignity of the sacrifice very strongly.

units.la: Caeterum omnia illa, quae in priori parte collationis sunt adiecta, quibus describitur tabernaculi in duas partes diuisio, & recensentur, quae eo loco, quem Sancto Sanctorum appellabant, fuerint dispositae ac seruata: praeterea, quod eundem locum non quouis tempore, nec quiuis sacerdotes soliti sint ingredi: hoc consilio admixta esse apparet: partim, vt tabernaculi legalis amplitudo ac splendor hoc modo nihil amplificetur: ex hac autem amplificatione postea intendatur etiam praestantia tabernaculi noui testamenti, quod Christus est ingressus, quod mox coelos ipsos interpretatur, quibus nihil magnificentius excogitari queat: partim, ut animi auditorum in illa omnia, quauis alias in specie praeclara, intuentes, cogitarent tamen typica tantum esse, & leuiter adumbrare quaedam per Christum peragenda, quemadmodum ipse quoq; insinuans se velle per auditores ita fieri in caeteris, interpretationem elegantem interserit, eius, quod sacerdotes reliqui quotidie quidem ingrederentur priorem tabernaculi partem, at sancta sanctorum nunquam.
units.tr: Moreover, all those things which are added in the first part of the comparison, by which the division of the tabernacle into two parts is described, and the things that were placed and kept in the place which they called the Holy of Holies are recounted, and besides that, the fact that the priests were not accustomed to enter that same place at any time nor by any priest at all: these appear to have been mixed in with this purpose: partly, so that the greatness and splendour of the legal tabernacle might in this way be nothing enlarged; and from this enlargement afterwards the pre-eminence of the tabernacle of the new covenant, which Christ entered, which he immediately interprets as the heavens themselves, than which nothing more magnificent can be imagined, might be heightened: partly, so that the minds of the hearers, looking at all those things, however otherwise remarkable in their kind, might nevertheless think them to be merely typical, and only faintly to foreshadow certain things to be accomplished through Christ; just as he himself, hinting that he wishes this to be done by his hearers in the other things too, inserts an elegant explanation of the fact that the other priests indeed entered the first part of the tabernacle daily, but never the Holy of Holies.

units.la: Tertio, ut vbi ostenderet, etiam plura in veteri testamento fuisse, quae res Christi praefigurarint, tanto melius fidem faceret, per vnicam oblationem sanguinis in sancta sanctorum, praefignificatum vnicum Christi sacrificium. Proinde nos in explicando totum hunc locum hoc progrediemur ordine. Primum nostro more explicabimus partes, atque in his tabernaculi descriptionem luculentam ob oculos ponemus. Post, inuitati occasione eorum, quae scripta cernimus ab ipso Apostolo, etiam typice exponemus vniuersam tabernaculi descriptionem. Hinc, si quae grauior quaestio notatu digna: item, si doctrina aut consolatio occurrerit breuiter adijciemus.
units.tr: Thirdly, so that where he shows that there were also many more things in the Old Testament which prefigured the things of Christ, he might make the case all the better, the one offering of blood into the Holy of Holies prefigured the one sacrifice of Christ. Accordingly, in explaining this whole passage we shall proceed in the following order. First, in our customary manner, we shall explain the parts, and set before the eyes a clear description of the tabernacle in these. Afterwards, prompted by the occasion of those things which we see written by the Apostle himself, we shall also expound the whole description of the tabernacle typically. Then, if any weightier question worth noting arises, likewise if any doctrine or consolation presents itself, we shall add it briefly.

units.la: Igitur habebat quidem etiam prius illud, iustificationes, cultus, ac sanctum mundanum.
units.tr: Therefore the former covenant also had justifications, worship, and the worldly sanctuary.

units.la: Particula ἂν videtur parere obscuritatem, quia, cum fit fere semper illatiua, non satis videtur, quid hic inferat, aut colligat praecedentibus. Sed considerandum est, Apostolum respicere ad id, quod posuerat pro fundamento huius partis de sacrificio Christi, nempe, omnia quae in veteri lege fiebant in sacerdotio & per sacerdotium, fuisse typos atque umbras rerum coelestium, & succedentib. praestantioribus, quae sunt noui testamenti, abolerì vmbratica illa, quę sunt testameti veteris. His ergo sit pro hypothesi constitutis, ac demonstratis quando iam aggreditur explicationem sacrificij Christi, & conferre vult typum veteris testamenti cum re noui testamenti, recte per hanc particulam exorditur, dicens: Habebat igitur & prius illud iustificationes. Sunt autem haec verba propositionis vice, ad plenius explicandum, quod sacrificium Christi fuerit, per sacrificium veteris testamenti adumbratum.
units.tr: The particle ἂν seems to cause obscurity, because, though it is almost always inferential, it does not seem clear what it infers or concludes from what precedes. But we must consider that the Apostle is looking back to what he had laid down as the foundation of this part, concerning the sacrifice of Christ: namely, that all the things done in the old law, in the priesthood and through the priesthood, were types and shadows of heavenly things, and that those shadowy things of the old covenant were abolished by the more excellent things that follow, which belong to the new covenant. So, with this hypothesis set up and demonstrated, when he now takes up the explanation of Christ's sacrifice, and wants to compare the type of the old covenant with the reality of the new, he rightly begins with this particle, saying: "Therefore the former covenant also had justifications." These words serve as a proposition, to explain more fully what Christ's sacrifice was, which was foreshadowed by the sacrifice of the old covenant.

units.la: Prius illud) Supple, testamentum: Ita enim πρῶτη refert Διαθήκη. Iamq; sumpta est haec distinguendi formula, qua distinguuntur testamenta, vt vnum dicatur prius seu vetus, alterum vero posterius seu nouum, & praecedenti testimonio Hieremiae: vnde deinde liberius utitur hisce loquendi formulis. Habebat, inquit Chrysostomus, tanquam nunc non habeat: atque ita ostendit vetus illud a modo cessasse.
units.tr: "The former") Supply "covenant", for the Greek πρώτη [first] refers to διαθήκη [covenant]. This formula of distinction, by which the covenants are distinguished, so that one is called the former or old and the other the latter or new, has now been adopted, and by the preceding testimony of Jeremiah; hence he uses these forms of speech more freely from here on. "He had," says Chrysostom, "as if he did not now have it": and thus he shows that the old covenant has ceased to be in use.

units.la: Iustificationes, cultus, ac sanctum mundanum) His tribus vocibus comprehendit omnia, quę ad religionem in veteri testamento pertinebant, quae causas omnes sacrorum continent, nempe, causam finalem, formalem, & locum, in quo sacra fiebant: vel, quaestiones has, quare, qualiter, ubi.
units.tr: "Justifications, worship, and the worldly sanctuary") By these three words he comprehends everything that pertained to religion in the old covenant, which contain all the causes of the sacred rites: namely the final cause, the formal cause, and the place in which the sacred rites were performed. Or, they answer these questions: why, how, and where.

units.la: Iustificationes sunt veluti effectus eorum, quae in sacris fiunt, hoc est, reputatio iustitiae coram hominib. vel coram Deo, sicut vocabulum Δικαιώματα plane forese est, ut iustificari ide sit, atque iustum fustum & immunem à peccato pronunciari: Hinc verò talis pronunciatio seu reputatio.
units.tr: Justifications are, as it were, the effects of the things done in the sacred rites, that is, the reckoning of righteousness before men or before God; the word δικαιώματα [justifications] is plainly a forensic term, so that to be justified means the same as to be pronounced just and free from sin, and such a pronouncement or reckoning follows from this.

units.la: Porrò in scripturis pasim vsurpatur vocabulum iustificationis, duplici significatu: altero, vt significet iustitiam externam coram hominibus, & in externis rebus sitam: quomodo Apostolus etiam paulo post vocat iustitiam externam, quae contingit propter observationem externarum ceremoniarum, iustificationes carnis vsque ad tempus correctionis impositas. Et sic saepe inuenitur sumptum in libris legalibus, item omnibus locis apud prophetas, vbi de iustitia legali & externa agitur.
units.tr: Moreover, in the Scriptures the word justification is used everywhere in a twofold sense. The first is to signify external righteousness before men, resting in external things: as the Apostle also calls it a little later "justifications of the flesh, imposed until the time of correction," which come about through the observance of external ceremonies. It is often found used in this sense in the books of the law, and likewise in all the places among the prophets where legal and external righteousness is treated.

units.la: Alio modo iustificatio significat iustitiam internam & spiritualem coram Deo, quae contingit, non propter obseruationem legis aut ceremoniarum, sed propter solum Christum: quomodo passim in scriptis Apostolorum, & inprimis Pauli: deinde etiam apud Prophetas, vbi habentur promissiones de Christo, vsurpatur. Vt Esaiae 53. de Christo: In cognitione sui iustificabit ipse iustus seruus meus multos, quorum iniquitates ipse portabit. Et Apostolus hoc ipso capite significationem eandem exprimere volens vocat purgationem conscientiae, profligationem peccati.
units.tr: In another way, justification signifies internal and spiritual righteousness before God, which comes about not through the observance of the law or of ceremonies, but through Christ alone. This is used everywhere in the writings of the Apostles, and especially of Paul; and also among the Prophets, where promises about Christ are found. As in Isaiah 53, about Christ: "By his knowledge my righteous servant shall justify many, and he shall bear their iniquities." And the Apostle, in this very chapter, wanting to express the same meaning, calls it "the purging of conscience" and "the putting away of sin."

units.la: Caeterum Apostolus hic loquitur de iustificationibus prioris generis, quae veteri testamento erant vsitatae, cum, quae posterioris generis sunt, tantum noua testamento conueniant. Iam vocabulum cultus potius significat causam formalem, & res eas, quae fiuntad Dei honorem, vtque Deo sunt acceptae: cuiusmodi sunt omnia fere ceremonialia, sacrificia, oblationes, &c. quae fiebant ad inducendos homines in agnitionem & confessionem peccati, implorationem misericordiae, gratiarum actionem, & huiusmodi: quae hac ratione, quòd tenderent ad gloriam Dei, rectè cultus Dei appellantur. Caeterum etiam dupliciter vocabulum cultus in scripturis accipitur: Primò, vt significet externa illa legis praecepta, potissimum ceremonialia, quae facta sunt ad honorandum Deum, & ad parandum externam iustitiam coram hominibus: quomodo Exodi 18. Iethro ad Mosen: Esto tu populo in his, quae ad Deum pertinent, vt referas, quae dicuntur ad eum, ostendasque populo ceremonias, & ritum colendi, viamq;, per quam ingredi debeant, & opus quod facere debeant. Quae & facta sunt, quia ea tanquam ad cultum Dei proprie pertinentia lex praecipiebat. Secundò, vt significet quaecunq; bona opera ex fide proficiscentia, quibus honoratur Deus, & iuuatur proximus: De quibus Christus ait, Misericordiam volo, & non sacrificium, Matthaei 9. ex Osea 6 & alia passim huiusmodi, quae vocantur sacrificia grata & accepta Deo, vt Roman. 12. & praesentis epistolae capite decimo: quae fiunt impulsu Spiritus, & quae fides, quandoquidem non potest esse otiosa, semper profert: Et proprie sunt illa, quibus Deus colitur in Euangelio; quaeque Deo prae omni veteris testamenti externo cultu grata sunt. Proinde Apostolus etiam hic loquitur de cultibus prioris generis. Ac prodest animaduertere hoc discrimen iustificationum & cultuum, vt intelligatur ratio ac dignitas eorum, quae proprie sunt in Euangelio exhibita, praeillis, quae habebantur sub lege, In hunc enim finem Apostolus ita loquitur, vt omnes intelligant, quòd lex vetus etiam habuerit suas iustificationes, suos item cultus, sed multum diuersos, & longe inferiores, ab ijs, quae sunt in Euangelio. Sic enim ipse postea distinguit iustificationes carnis à iustificasionibus conscientiarum. Item, cultus in cibis, potionibus, ac lotionibus, ab opere Christi, quo seipsum Deo patri pro nobis obtulit.
units.tr: Moreover, the Apostle here speaks of justifications of the first kind, which were customary under the old covenant, whereas those of the second kind belong only to the new covenant. Now the word worship (cultus) rather signifies the formal cause, and those things which are done to the honour of God and are accepted by him: such as almost all the ceremonial things, sacrifices, offerings, and so on, which were done to lead men to the acknowledgment and confession of sin, the imploring of mercy, thanksgiving, and the like. Because these tend to the glory of God, they are rightly called the worship of God. The word worship is also taken in Scripture in two ways. First, to signify those external precepts of the law, chiefly the ceremonial ones, which were enacted to honour God and to procure external righteousness before men: as in Exodus 18, where Jethro says to Moses: "Be you for the people in those things which pertain to God, that you may bring before him the things said to him, and show the people the ceremonies and the rite of worship, and the way in which they ought to walk, and the work which they ought to do." These were also done because the law commanded them as belonging properly to the worship of God. Second, to signify all good works proceeding from faith, by which God is honoured and the neighbour is helped. Of these Christ says, "I desire mercy and not sacrifice" (Matthew 9, from Hosea 6), and elsewhere in similar passages. These are called sacrifices pleasing and acceptable to God, as in Romans 12 and in chapter ten of this letter. They are done by the impulse of the Spirit, and faith, since it cannot be idle, always brings them forth. These are properly the things by which God is worshipped in the Gospel, and they are pleasing to God beyond all the external worship of the old covenant. Therefore the Apostle here also speaks of worship of the first kind. It is useful to note this distinction between justifications and worship, so that the reason and dignity of those things which are properly presented in the Gospel may be understood in comparison with those which were held under the law. For to this end the Apostle speaks in such a way that everyone understands that the old law also had its justifications and likewise its worship, but very different from, and far inferior to, those which are in the Gospel. For he himself afterwards distinguishes in this way justifications of the flesh from justifications of the conscience; likewise worship in foods, drinks, and washings from the work of Christ, by which he offered himself to God the Father for us.

units.la: Tertiò, dicit, quod prius illud testamentum, habuit etiam sanctū: tertia pars ad religionem pertinens: vt sit sententia, habuit vetus illud testamentum iustificationes, cultus, & in summa quicquid ad sanctimoniam pertinet neque quicquam huiusmodi ei defuit. Quod vero additum est, mundanum, id accipio ad extenuationem omnium illorum, quae in veteri testamento fiebant quasi per interpretationem esse appositum, vt significetur vniuersum illud sanctum in iustificationibus & cultibus situm, quamlibet in speciem praeclarum fuerit, tamem mundanum duntaxat, id est, externum, temporale, caruale, & nequaquàm spirituale fuisse: inquam sententiam etiam dicuntur iustificationes carnis: vel, vt sanctum accipiatur pro tabernaculo, quod ita appellatum est, quodque Apostolus mox describit. Atque his tribus omnia comprehenduntur legis ceremonialia, valdeque notanda est haec distinctio, quia in altera parte collationis etiam obseruanda venit.
units.tr: Thirdly, he says that the former covenant also had a sanctuary, the third part pertaining to religion. So the sense is: the old covenant had justifications and worship, and in sum whatever pertains to holiness, and nothing of this kind was lacking to it. But what is added, "worldly," I take as a qualifier for all those things which were done in the old covenant, placed here as if by way of explanation. It is signified that all that holiness lying in justifications and worship, however splendid it may have looked, was yet only worldly, that is, external, temporal, fleshly, and by no means spiritual; in this sense justifications are also called "of the flesh." Or the sanctuary may be taken for the tabernacle, which was so called, and which the Apostle is about to describe. By these three terms all the ceremonial things of the law are comprehended. This distinction is to be carefully noted, because it will also need to be observed in the other part of the comparison.

units.la: Coram mundo quidem per externas illas res parabatur ibi sanctitas, at nequaquam coram Deo, haec paranda adhuc erat in Euangelio per Christum, ad quem vnum omnes etiam in cultibus illis versantes debebant respicere quicunque vere sancti esse cupiebant. Facit etiam, vt huiusmodi emphasin subesse intelligam, articulus τό, quasi dicatur, & totum illud sanctum muudanum: & prope finem huius capitis, quae sub Euangelio sunt, vocantur coelestia. Et ipsa lex ad Galatas quarto, Colossens. 2. vocatur
units.tr: Before the world, holiness was indeed prepared there through external things, but by no means before God. This was still to be prepared in the Gospel through Christ, to whom alone all, even those engaged in those rites, ought to look if they truly desired to be holy. The article τό [the] also makes me understand that an emphasis lies here, as if it were said "that whole worldly sanctuary." And near the end of this chapter, what is under the Gospel is called heavenly. The law itself is called in Galatians 4 and Colossians 2

units.la: Elementa mundi, κοσμος: & vocabulum mundi subinde pro rebus externis, caducis, nequaquam spiritualibus accipitur: quomodo Ioannes 1. epistolae cap. 4. dicit, Pseudoprophetas e mundo loqui, id est, traditiones & legales ceremonias, & id genus obtrudere, in quibus nihil est spiritus.
units.tr: "the elements of the world" [κόσμος]. And the word world is at times taken for external, perishable things, by no means spiritual, as in 1 John, chapter 4, where John says that false prophets speak "from the world," that is, they impose traditions, legal ceremonies, and that kind of thing, in which there is nothing of the Spirit.

units.la: Scio quidem, Chrysostomum explicare sanctum mundanum, pro loco, seu parte anteriore templi, quam omnes citra discrimen ingrediebantur, quales vulgo vocant seculares, veluti Iudaei quicunque, proselyti, gentiles, Nazaraei. Unde quidam moti, ea quae sequuntur, de templo Solomonis omnia sunt interpretati: Sed quid attinet de templo multa hic proferre, quando diserte promissum est illud ad Mosen dictum, Fac omnia secundum exemplar, quod tibi in monte ostensum est) Ex quo manifestum fit, de tabernaculo, quod Moses secundum illud exemplar extruxit? Et quando pro typo adferuntur ea, quae in prima legis institutione sunt facta, & ostenditur, ea ipsa pulcherrime quadrare cum ijs, quae per Christum sunt peracta, id magis, appositum est, & instituto conueniens. Alijs placet ... significare splendidum apparatum & omne instrumentum sacrorum, tabernaculum, altaria, vestes, & id genus, eo pacto, quo & mundum sive ornatum muliebrem dicimus. Nonnulli interpretati sunt sanctum seculare, id est, ad certum tempus, veluti seculum, aut aliquot secula duraturum. Sed gracae voci no satis respodet. Magis placet nobis interpretatio, qua primo loco posuimus.
units.tr: I know indeed that Chrysostom explains the worldly sanctuary as the outer part of the temple, which everyone entered without distinction, such as those commonly called profane: Jews of every kind, proselytes, Gentiles, Nazarenes. Some, moved by this, have interpreted all that follows as about the temple of Solomon. But what is the point of bringing many things about the temple here, when it is plainly promised by the saying spoken to Moses, "Make all things according to the pattern that was shown you on the mountain"? From this it is clear that the passage is about the tabernacle, which Moses built according to that pattern. And when those things which were done at the first institution of the law are brought forward as a type, and it is shown that these very things agree most beautifully with those accomplished through Christ, this is more fitting and suited to the purpose. Others prefer to take it as signifying the splendid apparatus and every instrument of the sacred rites: the tabernacle, altars, vestments, and that kind of thing, in the way we also speak of women's adornment as "mundus." Some have interpreted the worldly sanctuary as a sanctuary lasting for a certain age, or for some ages. But this does not correspond well to the Greek word. The interpretation we placed first pleases us more.

units.la: Siquidem tabernaculum factum fuit primum, in quo erant lucerna, & mensa, & propositio panum, quae vocatur sancta. Post secundum autem velum erat tabernaculum, quod vocatur sanctum sanctorum, aureum habens thuribulum, & arcam testamenti undiq; circumtectam auro, in qua urna aurea habens manna, & virga Aaron, quae germinauerat, & tabulae testamenti. Supra hanc autem Cherubim gloria, obumbrantia propitiatorium, de quibus non est nunc dicendum singulatim.
units.tr: For the tabernacle was made first, in which were the lampstand, the table, and the setting out of the loaves, which is called the holy place. But behind the second veil was the tabernacle called the Holy of Holies, having the golden censer and the ark of the covenant covered on every side with gold, in which were a golden pot holding the manna, and Aaron's rod that had budded, and the tables of the covenant. Above it were the cherubim of glory overshadowing the mercy seat, of which we need not speak particularly now.

units.la: Exponit siue probat, quod vetus testamentum habuerit iustificationes, cultus, ac sanctum mundanum: Ac primum describendo ipsum tabernaculum, siue loci dispositionem, in quo sacra fiebant, ostendit, quale sanctum ibi fuerit. Sed dicat aliquis, quando tantum agitur de sacrificio Christi, atque istud figuratum fuit per unicam in anno oblationem sanguinis in sancta sanctorum, quorsum attinet, ista tam multa de tabernaculo, & solitis in eo fieri, proferri in medium? Satius fuisset paucis illud de sanguine semel in anno oblato attingere. Respondendum: Si tantum de oblato sanguine sermonem fecisset, facile potuisset typus reijci, tanquam non satis aptus & longius petitus. Nunc autem quando addit de tabernaculo, atq; ostendit etiam conuenire rebus Christi, docens videlicet, Christum quoq; vt verum, summum, pontificem ingressum in tabernaculum, item semel ingressum, ac tum ibi sanguinem obtulisse, melius fidem facit, per unicam oblationem sanguinis sacrificium Christi praesignificatum.
units.tr: He sets out, or proves, that the Old Testament had justifications, worship, and an earthly sanctuary. He first describes the tabernacle itself, or the arrangement of the place in which the sacred rites were performed, and so shows what kind of sanctuary it was there. But someone may say: since the discussion is only about the sacrifice of Christ, and that was foreshadowed by the single offering of blood once a year in the Holy of Holies, why bring forward so much about the tabernacle and what was done there customarily? It would have been better to touch briefly on the blood offered once a year. The answer is this: had he spoken only of the blood offered, the type could easily have been rejected as not apt enough and fetched from too far off. But now that he adds about the tabernacle, and shows that it also fits the things of Christ, teaching that Christ too, as true high priest, entered the tabernacle, likewise once, and then offered blood there, he gives better assurance that the sacrifice of Christ was foreshadowed by the one offering of blood.

units.la: Hac igitur de causa conueniebat hic plura addi, ut omittamus causas supra a nobis reddias. Iudaei potuissent multa cauillari, & dicere, ibi nihil esse, quod seruiat instituto.
units.tr: For this reason, therefore, it was fitting to add more here, so that we may leave aside the reasons already given by us above. The Jews could have raised many objections and said that there was nothing there that served the purpose.

units.la: Caeterum, ut plenius & clarius ista omnia intelligantur, operae faciemus pretium, si, quomodo Deus vniuersum tabernaculum extrui iusserit, & quibus locis omnia, praesertim quae hic nominantur, fuerint dispositia, ex libro Exodi repetamus, idq;, quam fieri potest faciemus crassissime, quasi architectorum morem in delineando obseruantes.
units.tr: However, so that all these things may be understood more fully and clearly, we shall take the trouble, if we recall from the book of Exodus how God commanded the whole tabernacle to be built and in what places everything was arranged, especially what is named here. We shall do this as roughly as possible, following the custom of architects in their outlines.

units.la: Primum ergo in lectissima area in medio castrorum, iussit Dominus erigi atrium, adeoq; ambitum totius tabernaculi, cuius longitudo ex altera parte ad Australem plagam, altera ad Septentrionem, erant centum cubitorum, latitudo ad orientem & occidentem quinquaginta cubitorum.
units.tr: First, then, in the most select open space in the middle of the camp, the Lord ordered that a court be set up, and so the enclosure of the whole tabernacle: its length, from one side toward the south and from the other toward the north, was a hundred cubits, and its breadth toward the east and west was fifty cubits.

units.la: Atque in longitudine quidem iustis interuallis dispositae erant columnae viginti, in latitudine columnae decem. Omnes autem columnae obductae argenteis laminis, capita habentes argentea, bases vero aeneas: atque altitudo columnarum habebat quinque cubitos. Ab his columnis omni ex parte pendebant aulaea seu tapetes ex bysso retorta, ad terram usque demissae, quinque cubitorum altitudine. Sic vero diuisae tapetes, ut singulae essent longitudine quindecim cubitorum, & tres columnas occuparent, atque ita ex vnoquoque latere in longitudine, septem penderent.
units.tr: Along the length, twenty pillars were set at fitting intervals, and along the breadth ten pillars. All the pillars were overlaid with silver plates, having silver capitals and bronze bases, and the height of the pillars was five cubits. From these pillars hangings, or curtains, of fine-twined linen were hung on every side, reaching down to the ground, five cubits high. The curtains were so divided that each was fifteen cubits long and covered three pillars, and so seven hung along each side in length.

units.la: Sed in porta fine ingressu atrij, id est, ad occidentalem plagam, ad medium latitudinis, vnum erat velum multo praestantissimum viginti cubitorum, ex hyacintho, & purpura, & vermiculo cocci, & bysso retorta, opere acupictoris, a quatuor columnis suspensum.
units.tr: But at the gate, which was the entrance to the court, that is, on the western side, at the middle of the breadth, there was one veil, far more excellent, twenty cubits long, of hyacinth, purple, scarlet, and fine-twined linen, the work of an embroiderer, hung from four pillars.

units.la: Haec est descriptio totius ambitus.
units.tr: This is the description of the whole enclosure.

units.la: Post hoc ad orientalem plagam huius atrij tam spatiosi, erigebatur tabernaculum in hunc modum, Ad latus Austrinum, similiter ad Aquilonem, erigebantur viginti tabulae siue afferes: ad orientem verò singulis lateribus octo tabulæ, singulæ altitudine decem cubitorum, latitudine verò cubiti & dimidij. Quare longitudinem totius tabernaculi licet colligere fuisse cubitorum triginta, latitudinem verò cubitorum duodecim, altitudinem verò decem. Singulæ verò bases habebant duas bases argenteas eleganter fabrefactas, quibus infigebantur tabulæ per duos dentes. Vectibus item prælongis, & annulis tabulæ coniungebantur ac sustentabantur. Ipsæ autem tabulæ ex lignis erant Sittim, auro tamen vestitæ, sicut & vectes ex eadem materia, atque annuli ex auro. Præterea anteriori parte tabernaculi, hoc est, occidentem versus, velum ex hyacinthino serico, purpureo, coccino bis tincto, & byssò torta, cum pictura Cherubim opere textorio, quod è quatuor columnis ex lignis Sittim auro opertis suspendebatur, quarum capita erant aurea, bases argenteæ. Atque hoc velum distinguebat, inter sanctum, & inter sanctum sanctorum. Etiamsi aliud velum erat non admodum dissimile, quo operiebatur ostium tabernaculi, quod pendebat ex quinque columnis de lignis Sittim, opertis auro, quorum & capita aurea, bases æneæ.
units.tr: Behind this, toward the east side of this so spacious court, the tabernacle was erected in this way. On the southern side, and likewise on the north, twenty boards or planks were set up; on the west, however, there were eight boards on each side, each ten cubits high and a cubit and a half broad. Hence the length of the whole tabernacle may be gathered to have been thirty cubits, its breadth twelve cubits, and its height ten cubits. Each board had two silver bases, elegantly wrought, into which the boards were fixed by two tenons. They were also joined and held together by very long bars and rings. The boards themselves were of acacia (Sittim) wood, yet overlaid with gold, and the bars likewise of the same material, and the rings of gold. Moreover, at the front part of the tabernacle, that is, facing west, there was a veil of hyacinth silk, purple, scarlet dyed twice, and fine-twined linen, with a picture of cherubim worked in weaving, which was hung from four pillars of acacia wood overlaid with gold, having golden capitals and silver bases. This veil divided the holy place from the Holy of Holies. There was also another veil, not much unlike it, by which the door of the tabernacle was covered, which hung from five pillars of acacia wood overlaid with gold, whose capitals were also gold and bases bronze.

units.la: Neque hoc tebernaculum carebat tecto: Nam ad tegendum ipsum erant primum aulæa vndecim, singula longitudine triginta cubitorum, latitudine quatuor cubitorum. Secundum tegumentum ex pellibus arietum rubris: tertium ex pellibus thaforum siue melium. Habemus nunc erectum tabernaculum: non difficile erit explicare, quid in vnoquoque loco fuerit constitutum.
units.tr: Nor was this tabernacle without a roof. For to cover it there were first eleven curtains, each thirty cubits long and four cubits broad. The second covering was of red ram skins; the third of tahash skins, or melim. We now have the tabernacle erected; it will not be difficult to explain what was placed in each location.

units.la: Primum, in ingressu atrij erectum est altare holocausti (Exodi 27.) ex lignis Sittim, tectum ære, quinque cubitos longum, totidem latum, tres altum, concauum, cuius media concauitate pensile ex quatuor anulis rete æneum, cui hostiæ sunt impositæ igne substrato. Accreditur, in latere altaris, quod orientem spectabat, ostiolum fuisse, per quod ligna ingererentur struendo igni, & cineres rursus ac carbones egererentur, sicut sentit Cassiodorus in enarratione super psalmos, referente Rabano. Item ad latera annulos cum vectibus, vt gestari posset. Iam ollæ fuscinulæ, crateres, forcipes, & id genus, ex ære etiam formabantur, præterea paulò altius ac propius ad tabernaculum erectum est aliud altare, appellatum thimiamatis siue incensi, ex lignis Sittim, totum tectum auro, coronam habens aueam per circuitum, duos item annulos aureos infra coronam in duobus angulis eius, cum traiectis vectibus, quibus deportarentur, ijsdemque ex lignis Sittim & auro opertis, altitudine duorum cubitorum, latitudine vnius, & longitudine pariter: ad solum suffitum faciendum quotidie mane & vesperi fuit fabrefactum.
units.tr: First, at the entrance of the court, the altar of burnt offering was set up (Exodus 27), made of acacia wood, covered with bronze, five cubits long, as many broad, three high, hollow; in the middle of its hollow hung a bronze grate from four rings, on which the victims were laid with fire kindled beneath. It is believed that on the side of the altar facing east there was a little door, through which wood was thrust in to feed the fire, and ashes and coals were carried out again, as Cassiodorus holds in his commentary on the Psalms, as reported by Rabanus. Likewise, there were rings with bars on the sides, so that it could be carried. Pots, fire-forks, bowls, tongs, and the like were also fashioned of bronze. Moreover, a little higher and nearer to the tabernacle, another altar was set up, called the altar of incense, made of acacia wood, wholly covered with gold, having a golden crown round about, likewise two golden rings below the crown at its two corners, with the bars passed through them by which it might be carried, also of acacia wood and covered with gold, two cubits high, one cubit broad, and equally long. It was made solely for offering incense every morning and evening.

units.la: Inter hoc altare & velum tabernaculi erat labrum æneum cum basi ænea, cui aqua inerat, qua manus ac pedes lauarent sacerdotes, quotiescunque in tabernaculum testimonij vellent ingredi.
units.tr: Between this altar and the veil of the tabernacle stood a bronze laver with a bronze base, containing water with which the priests washed their hands and feet whenever they wished to enter the tabernacle of testimony.

units.la: Hinc non procul item à tabernaculo, ad Aquilonarem plagam erat Mensa panum propositionis ex lignis Sittim inauratis, cum corona aurea per circuitum, longitudine duorum cubitorum, latitudine vnius, altitudine verò vnius & dimidiati. Ad quatuor eius angulos, sub corona quatuor annuli, cum vectibus inauratis. Et huic sua instrumenta, acetabula, inquam, cochlearia, phialæ, & similia ex auro.
units.tr: Not far from the tabernacle, toward the northern side, stood the table of the showbread, of acacia wood overlaid with gold, with a golden crown round about, two cubits long, one cubit broad, and a cubit and a half high. At its four corners, under the crown, were four rings with gilded bars. And to it belonged its own utensils: dishes, I mean, spoons, bowls, and the like, all of gold.

units.la: E regione ad plagam Austrinam candelabrum aureum, medio stipite erecto, è quo calami deinde consurgunt ex vnoquoq; latere tres, vt superius imponi posint septem lucernæ. Talento auri constabat, numerando emunctoria & vascula, quibus emunctæ extinguebantur. Hæc omnia hoc ordine extra tabernaculum.
units.tr: Opposite, toward the southern side, was the golden lampstand, with a central upright shaft, from which branches rose on each side, three to each side, so that seven lamps could be placed on top. It weighed a talent of gold, counting the snuffers and the little vessels in which the wicks were put out. All these were set in this order outside the tabernacle.

units.la: Intra tabernaculum erat arca testimonij, cum propitiatorio, eaque sic fabrefacta. Arca erat ex lignis Sittim, auro intus & foris vestita, longa duos cubitos & dimidiatum, lata vnum & dimidiatum, alta tantundem, torohaun habens auream in circuitu. Et ad angulos quatuor, quatuor annuli aurei, pro duobus inauratis vectibus, quibus gestari posset. Huic arcæ imponebatur testimonium, id est, tabulæ legis, & quædam alia. Superponebatur verò ei propitiatorium: id erat ex auro mundissimo, eiusdem longitudinis & latitudinis: sed præterea habens ad latera duos Cherubim aureos, sic constitutos, quasi sese mutuò vultibus intuerentur, atque alas ita expandentes, vt propitiatorium quasi tegerent. Ex eo verò loco Deus promittebat sese daturum responsa, ut licet Exodi 25. animaduertere. Atque hæc omnia eiusdem libri Exodi 25.26.27.30.40. manifesta fiunt. Sed iuuerit etiam hic conferre ea, quæ habentur libro 3. regum, & 2. Paralipomemon, vbi describitur ædificium templi cum omni apparatu per Solomonem erectum.
units.tr: Inside the tabernacle was the ark of the testimony, with the mercy seat, made in this manner. The ark was of acacia wood, overlaid with gold within and without, two and a half cubits long, a cubit and a half broad, and as high; it had a gold moulding round about. At its four corners were four golden rings, for the two gilded bars by which it could be carried. On this ark was placed the testimony, that is, the tables of the law, and certain other things. Above it was the mercy seat, of the purest gold, of the same length and breadth; and moreover it had at its sides two golden cherubim, so set that they looked at one another with their faces, and spread out their wings so as to cover the mercy seat. From that place God promised that He would give answers, as may be noted in Exodus 25. And all these things are made clear in the same book of Exodus, chapters 25, 26, 27, 30, and 40. But it will also be helpful to compare here what is found in 3 Kings and 2 Chronicles, where the building of the temple with all its furnishings, erected by Solomon, is described.

units.la: Oriens latitudo 50. cubitorum
units.tr: East: breadth 50 cubits

units.la: latitudo 12. cubitorum
units.tr: breadth 12 cubits

units.la: Longitudo 50. cubitorum
units.tr: Length 50 cubits

units.la: Longitudo 100. cubitorum
units.tr: Length 100 cubits

units.la: Auster.
units.tr: South.

units.la: Aquilo
units.tr: North

units.la: Occidens Ex his iam facile intelligemus verba Apostoli, Siquidem tabernaculum factum fuit primum, in quo erant & lucernæ, & mensa, & propositio panum, quæ uocatur sancta. Post secundum autem uelum erat tabernaculum, quod uocatur sanctum sanctorum.
units.tr: West. From these things we shall now easily understand the words of the Apostle: For there was a tabernacle made; the first, wherein was the candlestick, and the table, and the shewbread, which is called the Sanctuary. And after the second veil, the tabernacle which is called the Holiest of all.

units.la: Sic loquitur Apostolus, quasi duo essent tabernacula, cum tamen in Scriptura omnia simul vnius tabernaculi nomine comprehendantur: quanquam distinguitur tabernaculum in duas partes, quarum altera & patentior appellata est nomine atrij: altera minor & suis iterum septis conclusa, tabernaculum testimonij, atque, vt ipse hic ait, pars ista appellata est sancta sanctorum; illa simpliciter sancta: quæ distinctio etiam habetur Exodi vigesimo sexto, vbi dicitur, velum preciosissimum ad quatuor columnas suspendum, ad ingressum tabernaculi, quo sanctum, & sanctum sanctorum diuiderentur.
units.tr: The Apostle speaks as if there were two tabernacles, though in Scripture everything is included under the one name of tabernacle. Still, the tabernacle is divided into two parts: the larger and more open part is called the court, and the smaller part, enclosed by its own walls, is called the tabernacle of testimony. As the Apostle here says, the inner part is called the Holy of Holies and the outer part simply the Holy. This distinction is also found in Exodus 26, where it is said that a most precious veil was hung from four pillars at the entrance of the tabernacle, to divide the Holy from the Holy of Holies.

units.la: Voluit autem Deus tabernaculum siue σκηνὴν sibi erigi, ad ostendendum, quòd vellet populo suo adesse & habitare in medio eorum, sicut Dominus ipse ait Exodi vigesimo quinto, Tabernaculum vero rectius, quàm domum, vel huiusmodi, sicut patres in tabernaculis vixisse leguntur, quæ transferri hinc inde facile poterant: Item in eremo agentibus & subinde locum mutantibus quid magis conuenisset? Præterea tabernaculum sic transferibile satis significabat Dei potentiam, & nihilominus quòd alibi quoque esset, ac loco nequaquam concluderetur.
