units.tr: God willed that a tabernacle, or skēnē [σκηνὴν], be set up for himself, to show that he wished to be present with his people and to dwell in their midst, as the Lord himself says in Exodus 25. Indeed a tabernacle rather than a house, or something of that kind, is more fitting, since the fathers are read to have lived in tents, which could easily be moved from place to place. Moreover, for people living in the wilderness and changing their place from time to time, what would have been more suitable? Besides, a portable tabernacle signified well enough the power of God, and at the same time that he was present everywhere and was in no way confined to one place.

units.la: Cæterum in ea parte anteriori constitutas fuisse lucernas, siue candelabrum, constat ex ijs, quæ diximus.
units.tr: Moreover, that the lampstands, or the candelabrum, stood in that front part is clear from what we have said.

units.la: Præterea de mensa, in qua panes propositionis siue panes propositi, sic appellati, quòd ibi per totam hebdomadem essent publicè propositi, cum thure, in vasculis, siue acerris, vt dicitur 2. Paralipomen. 13. Vnde, cùm in conspectu & coram facie essent, etiam panes facierum dicti sunt.
units.tr: Next, concerning the table on which the loaves of the proposition, or set-out loaves, were placed, so called because they were publicly set out there for the whole week, with incense in little dishes or censers, as is said in 2 Chronicles 13. Hence, since they were in the sight and before the face of God, they were also called the loaves of the faces.

units.la: Quod autem dicit propositione panum, non panes propositionis, sicut alias per Hebraismum, videri queat hypallage esse, sicut dicunt, dare clasibus austros. Cùm verò dicit Apostolus, Post secundum autem uelum, erat tabernaculum, μετὰ δὲ τὸ δεύτερον καταπέτασμα σκηνὴ, quidam annotant ibi esse συγχύσιν, id est, confusionem ac vocum perturbationem, vt τὸ δεύτερον cum σκηνὴ, debeat construi, non cum καταπετάσματος, sitque sensus: Post velum autem erat secundum tabernaculum, vt dicatur tabernaculum secundum, ad distinctionem prioris, quomodo prius diximus; & Apostolus iterum subijcit, dicens, quòd in primum tabernaculum semper ingrediuntur sacerdotes, in secundum autem solus pontifex semel quotannis. Alias, si duo vela hic constituas, tùm erit triplex distinctio locorum siue tabernaculorum, ita vt vnum spacium sit sumendum inter duo vela, & rursus vnum ab altera parte alterius veli: quod non est, licet apud Iosephum simile quiddam legatur, adeò veritati consentaneum: nisi certè quis vsque adeò disitá esse velit ab inuicem, velum illud, quo discernitur sanctum à sancto sanctorum, & pendet ex quatuor columnis, vt habetur Exodi 25. ab altero, quod ibidem ad finem capitis statim describitur suspendum ad quinque columnas, quod septuaginta differentiæ causa vocant ἐπιοὐσιον, quòd videlicet segregetac disiungat locum à loco, vt annotauit Vulgarius. Aut certè secundum velum dicetur respectu alterius, quod in ingressu atrij suspensum erat, longitudine viginti cubitorum. Quomodocunque sit, de secundo tabernaculo res agitur, satisque est intelligere, à primo tabernaculo, quod vocatum est, Sancta, ventum esse ad secundum tabernaculum, vocatum, Sancta Sanctorum, quæ duo solo velo ab inuicem disiuncta sunt.
units.tr: As for the words propositione panum, not panes propositionis as elsewhere, this may be a hypallage, as they say, giving south winds to the fleets. When the Apostle says, Post secundum autem uelum, erat tabernaculum [μετὰ δὲ τὸ δεύτερον καταπέτασμα σκηνή], some note that there is here a synchysis, that is, a confusion and disturbance of the words, so that tò deuteron [τὸ δεύτερον] should be construed with skēnē [σκηνή], not with katapetasma, and the sense would be: after the veil there was a second tabernacle, so that the tabernacle is called the second, to distinguish it from the first, as we said before. The Apostle then adds that the priests always entered the first tabernacle, but only the high priest entered the second, and that once a year. Otherwise, if you posit two veils here, there would be a threefold division of places or tabernacles, so that one space would have to be taken between the two veils and another on the far side of the second veil. This is not so, although something similar is read in Josephus, and it agrees so well with the truth; unless indeed someone wishes to separate so far the veil which divides the Holy from the Holy of Holies, and hangs from four pillars, as Exodus 25 has it, from the other veil, which is described in the same chapter, at its end, as hung from five pillars. The Seventy, to make a distinction, call this epiousion [ἐπιοὐσιον], because it separates and divides one place from another, as Vulgarius noted. Or else the second veil will be called second in relation to the other, which hung at the entrance of the court and was twenty cubits long. However that may be, the matter concerns the second tabernacle, and it is enough to understand that from the first tabernacle, called the Holy, one comes to the second tabernacle, called the Holy of Holies, and these two are separated from one another by a single veil.

units.la: Notabis interea, eiusmodi duplicationes, Sancta Sanctorum, Hebræis significare excellentiam, & superlatiuum gradum in comparationibus sic exprimi, vt Sancta Sanctorum tantundem fit, atque si dicatur, inter ea, quæ sancta sunt, omnium sanctissima.
units.tr: Meanwhile you will note that such doublings as Holy of Holies signify excellence for the Hebrews, and that the superlative degree is expressed in comparisons in such a way that Holy of Holies amounts to the same as saying the most holy among holy things.

units.la: Iam videamus, quid in hoc secundo tabernaculo fuisse scribat: Aureum, inquit, habens thuribulum, & arcam testamenti undiq; circumtectam auro: De arca testamenti sic appellata, quòd tabulas legis, quæ erant tabulæ continentes conditiones fœderis, inclusas haberet, nulla est ambiguitas: Nam aperte habetur Exodi 25. quòd Dominus imponi eas iusserit, & ita factum legitur Exodi 40. Sed de thuribulo posito in tabernaculo testimonij, & quibusdam alijs, quæ mox dicit etiam in arca fuisse repositia, dubitatur.
units.tr: Now let us see what he writes was in this second tabernacle: having a golden censer, he says, and the ark of the testament covered round about with gold. That the ark of the testament was so called because it contained the tables of the law, which were the tables containing the conditions of the covenant, there is no doubt; for it is plainly stated in Exodus 25 that the Lord ordered them to be placed there, and it is read in Exodus 40 that this was done. But there is doubt about the censer being placed in the tabernacle of testimony, and about certain other things which he next says were also kept in the ark.

units.la: Vnde quidam ausi sunt contendere, hanc epistolam non esse scriptam ab homine rerum hebraicarum perito, tantum abest, vt à Paulo concedant profectam.
units.tr: Hence some have dared to contend that this epistle was not written by a man skilled in Hebrew matters, so far are they from conceding that it came from Paul.

units.la: Vt de thuribulo breuiter agamus, cùm græcè legatur χρυσοῦν θυμιατήριον: vox autem hæc significat & thuribulum, & locum atque etiam aram, in qua suffitus fit, quidam vertent, altare aureum, intelligentes altare incensi, quod ex lignis Sittim fiebat, atque autem vestiebatur. Sed manifestum est, istud intra velum tabernaculi non fuisse positum, sed potius extra quandoquidem Exodi 30. dicitur, Aaron quotidie adoleret illi thymiama, mane & vesperi, post reparatas lucernas: quod certè non fuisset factum, si intra tabernaculum testimonij fuisset collocatum. Proinde accipiemus θυμιατήριον pro thuribulo, qualia multa ex auro facta sunt Exodi 37. &c, cum Leuitici 16. pluribus verbis describatur, quomodo summus pontifex semel in anno intrabat in sancta, cum thuribulo incendens aromata, ut nebula eorum & vapor operiat oraculum, quod est supra testimonium, & non moriatur, accipiemus ita describi, uti sacerdos solet cum apparatu illud ingredi, sicut mox dicet, ingredi solitum cum sanguine. Fortasis autem, cùm multa fuerint thuribula, unum aliquod in hunc vsum proprie destinatum erat, atque ita istud dicit haberi in secundo tabernaculo, quod verosimile est id ibi seruari solitum. Neque est absurdum dicere, ibi thuribulum fuisse seruatum, quod non licuisset cuiquam ingredi ad reponendum vel educendum illud, cum dubium non sit, quin alias quoque licuerit sacerdotibus ingredi tabernaculum, videlicet si aliquid fractum fuisset, vel, si quid concidisset, ut illud erigerent, vel, si mouenda essent castra, sicut Num. 4. diserte exprimitur. Sed non poterat quisquam intrare, ad adolendum, vel ad offerendum sanguinem, aut aliquid huiusmodi, quod erat solius summi pontificis semel in anno facere. Tantum de thuribulo, quod Apostolus ait fuisse in secundo tabernaculo: neque est, quod praeterea imperitus rerum Hebraicarum videatur. Iam addit Apostolus, quid in arca fuerit repositum: In qua urna aurea habuit manna. An in arca fuerit reposita huiusmodi urna, in scripturis haud satis exprimitur: certè in tabernaculo asseruatam ad rerum gestarum memoriam, clarum est. Sic enim de reseruando Manna praecepit Dominus Exod. 16. Dixit Moses, sicut praeceperat Dominus, ad Aaron: Sume vas unum, & mitte ibi Man, quantum potest capere Gomor, & repone coram Domino ad seruandum in generationes vestras, sicut praeceperat Dominus Mosi, posuitque illud Aaron in tabernaculo conseruandum. Sequitur: Et virga Aaron, quae germinauerat: De hac Numer. 17. quomodo posita in tabernaculo foederis coram testimonio per Mosen, cum duodecim aliis virgis, singulis è singulis tribubus, sola floruerit, Deo sic declarante, quòd tribus Leuiticam, & in hac domum Aaronis elegisset ad munus sacerdotale: & postea subijcitur: dixitq; Dominus ad Mosen, Refer virgam Aaron in tabernaculum testimonij, vt seruetur ibi in signum rebellium filiorum Israel, & quiescat querelae eorum à me, ne moriantur. En ergo virgam Aaron in tabernaculo seruatam.
units.tr: To deal briefly with the censer: the Greek reads chrysoun thymiatērion [χρυσοῦν θυμιατήριον], but this word means both a censer and the place, and even the altar, on which the incense is burned. Some translate it "the golden altar," understanding the altar of incense, which was made of acacia wood and covered with gold. But it is clear that this did not stand within the veil of the tabernacle but rather outside it, since Exodus 30 says that Aaron burned incense on it every morning and evening, after the lamps had been trimmed; which certainly would not have been done if it had been placed inside the tabernacle of testimony. Therefore we shall take thymiatērion [θυμιατήριον] to mean a censer, of which many were made of gold, as in Exodus 37 and following. Since Leviticus 16 describes at greater length how the high priest entered the holy places once a year with a censer burning spices, so that the cloud and vapour of them might cover the mercy seat which is above the testimony, and that he might not die, we shall take it that the censer is described in the way the priest usually carried it in with its equipment, just as he is soon to say that it was customary to enter with the blood. Perhaps, since there were many censers, one particular one was set aside for this purpose, and so he says it was kept in the second tabernacle; which is likely, since it was usual for it to be kept there. Nor is it absurd to say that the censer was kept there, so that no one but the priest could enter to put it away or to take it out, though there is no doubt that priests were at other times allowed to enter the tabernacle, namely if something had been broken, or if something had fallen and had to be set up again, or if the camp had to be moved, as Numbers 4 expressly states. But no one could enter to burn incense, or to offer blood, or anything of that kind, which was the work of the high priest alone, once a year. So much for the censer, which the Apostle says was in the second tabernacle; nor is there reason to think him ignorant of Hebrew matters on that account. Now the Apostle adds what was placed in the ark: in which was the golden pot that had the manna. Whether such a pot was placed in the ark is not sufficiently stated in the Scriptures; that it was kept in the tabernacle as a memorial of the things done is clear. For the Lord thus commanded concerning keeping the manna, Exodus 16: Moses said, as the Lord had commanded, to Aaron: Take one vessel, and put in it a homer of manna, and lay it up before the Lord, to be kept for your generations, as the Lord commanded Moses; and Aaron laid it up in the tabernacle to be kept. There follows: and Aaron's rod that budded. Of this, Numbers 17 says that when it was placed before the testimony in the tabernacle of the covenant by Moses, along with twelve other rods, one from each tribe, it alone flowered, God thus declaring that he had chosen the Levitical tribe, and in it the house of Aaron, for the priestly office; and afterwards it is added: And the Lord said to Moses, Bring back the rod of Aaron into the tabernacle of testimony, to be kept there as a sign against the rebellious sons of Israel, and that their murmurings against me may cease, lest they die. Behold, then, Aaron's rod kept in the tabernacle.

units.la: Et tabulae testamenti) Has repositas fuisse in arca, non est dubitatio, quia clarè id praecipitur, & factum esse inuenitur Exodi 25. & 40. Sed de prioribus plurimi vocantin dubium, idque eo magis, quòd non commemorentur apertè reposita in arcam, sed in tabernaculum: Deinde 3. Reg. 8. & 2. Paralipomen. 5. expressè dicitur, nihil fuisse in arca, praeter duas tabulas lapideas, quas posuerat Moses in Horeb, quando legem dedit Dominus filiis Israel egredientibus ex Aegypto. Ad istam obiectionem variè respondent. Primùm Theophylactus ait, Apostolum ita accepisse ex maiorum traditionibus, qui forte narrarint ita factum, videlicet ista quoque, vnam, inquam, & virgam impositas arcae, nondum quidem Solomonis temporibus, sed longè post, necessitatibus diuersis vrgentibus, veluti cum esset necesse Hieremiae prophetae temporibus etiam arcam ipsam occultari: additque, Hebraeos plurimos ita sensisse, maximeq; pharisaeos, inter quos edoctus erat Apostolus. Quidam dicunt exclusiuam κιβωτὸν, quae apud septuaginta legitur, non haberi in Hebraeo. Alijs placet per Synecdochen dictum esse, in ea tantùm tabulas haberi, vt alia subintelligantur, & illud solum exprimatur, vnde ipsa arca trahit appellationem. Potest & illud addi, hic in verbis Apostoli, οὐ ἡ, non tàm referre κιβωτὸν, arcam, quam σκηνήν, id est, tabernaculum: & sic erit sententia, haec omnia fuisse in tabernaculo, quod scriptura passim apertissimè memorat. Neque verò rixandum morosius est propter huiusmodi dictum: multo minus propterea contemnetur Apostolus quasi rerum Hebraicarum imperitus.
units.tr: And the tables of the covenant.) That these were placed in the ark there is no doubt, since this is clearly commanded and is found to have been done (Exod. 25 and 40). But many call the former into doubt, the more so because they are not plainly said to have been placed in the ark but in the tabernacle. Moreover, in 3 Kings 8 and 2 Chronicles 5 it is expressly said that there was nothing in the ark except the two stone tables which Moses had put there at Horeb, when the Lord gave the law to the sons of Israel coming out of Egypt. To this objection there are various answers. First, Theophylact says that the Apostle received it thus from the traditions of the elders, who perhaps reported that it happened so: namely, that these other things as well, the urn and the rod, were placed in the ark, not indeed in Solomon's time but long afterwards, when different necessities pressed, as when in the time of the prophet Jeremiah it was necessary to hide the ark itself. He adds that many Hebrews thought so, especially the Pharisees, among whom the Apostle had been taught. Some say that the exclusive kibōtos [κιβωτὸν], which is read in the Septuagint, is not found in the Hebrew. Others think it is said by synecdoche: only the tables are mentioned in the ark, so that the rest is understood, and only that is expressed from which the ark itself takes its name. It may also be added that here, in the Apostle's words, [οὐ ἡ], "in which," refers not so much to [κιβωτὸν], the ark, as to [σκηνήν], that is, the tabernacle; and so the sense will be that all these things were in the tabernacle, which Scripture everywhere most plainly records. Nor should one wrangle stubbornly over such an expression; much less should the Apostle be despised as if he were ignorant of Hebrew matters.

units.la: Supra hanc autem Cherubim gloriae obumbrantia propitiatorium) Iosephus Cherubim ait animalia fuisse volatili figura, cuiusmodi nullus unquàm viderit mortalium: Sed Moses ita se vidisse figurata ad sedem Dei referebat. Et conueniebat, quae nunquàm visa sunt in rerum natura, proponi, vt talium rerum conspectu animus res maximas conciperet, & ad apprehendendum diuinam maiestatem, quae nulla figura delineari poterat, in sede vacua euehteretur. Quomodo verò ita constituti Cherubim, vt obumbrarint alijs suis propiciatorium, licet colligere ex descriptione, quae habetur Exodi 25.
units.tr: Above this, the cherubim of glory overshadowing the mercy seat.) Josephus says that the cherubim were living creatures of a winged form, of a kind no mortal has ever seen; but Moses, he reports, saw them thus depicted as the seat of God. It was fitting that things never seen in nature should be set forth, so that by looking at such things the mind might conceive great matters, and be lifted up to the empty seat to grasp the divine majesty, which no figure could portray. How the cherubim were so arranged that they overshadowed the mercy seat with their wings may be gathered from the description given in Exodus 25.

units.la: De quibus non est nunc dicendum singulatim) Reijcit Apostolus pleniorem earum rerum descriptionem, atque interpretationem, tum quòd haec sufficiant, ad demonstrandum, quòd vetus testamentum habuerit suum sanctum: tum, quòd explicare, quomodo ea omnia typus fuerint Christi, & rerum per eundem gerendarum, longum, nec admodū operæ foret precium: quod tamen per lectores posse, & merito debere fieri, satis indicat, quando, quæ principaliter ad causam præsentem de sacrificio Christi attinent, elegantissimè mox exponit. Et profecto quorsum opus fuisset, omnia typicè statim exponere, quà do prolixitas attulisset tædium, & non magno negotio quiuis alius id posset? Et tacitè reprehendit quorundam curiositatem. Erat ergo ad causam principalem festinandum. Nos tamen, vbi quæ ad partes attinent, exposuerimus, etiam typicè, quomodo quæ in tabernaculo erant, Christum adumbrarint, exponemus, vt auido lectori aliquo modo satisfiat: aut, si id non dabitur, certè occasio præbeatur meliora cogitandi & proferendi.
units.tr: Of which things there is no need to speak individually now.) The Apostle sets aside a fuller description and interpretation of those things, partly because what he has said suffices to show that the old covenant had its holy place, and partly because to explain how all these things were types of Christ and of the things he would accomplish would be long, and not really worth the effort. That this can and rightly should be done by the readers, the Apostle sufficiently indicates, since he presently expounds most elegantly what pertains chiefly to the present cause, the sacrifice of Christ. And indeed, why would it have been necessary to expound everything typologically at once, when the length would have brought weariness, and anyone could do it without great trouble? He also tacitly rebukes the curiosity of some. He had therefore to hasten on to the main cause. We, however, when we have expounded what concerns the parts, will also expound, even typologically, how the things in the tabernacle prefigured Christ, so that the eager reader is in some measure satisfied; or, if that is not granted, at least an occasion is provided for thinking and proposing better things.

units.la: His autem ad hūc ordinatis modum in prius quidem tabernaculū semper ingrediūtur sacerdotes, qui sacrorum ritus peragant: in secundum autem semel quotānis solus pontifex non sine sanguine, quē offert pro seipso, & pro populi ignorantiis, illud signifi cante spiritu sancto, nondum manifestatam esse sanctorum viam adhuc priore tabernaculo consistente. Quod erat similitudo pro tempore tum præsente, in quo dona sacrificiaque offeruntur, quæ non possunt iuxta conscientiam perfectum reddere culiorem, in cibis duntaxat, & potionibus, & diuersis ablutionibus, ac iustificationibus carnis, vsque ad temporis correctionis impositā.
units.tr: Now these things having been thus ordained, the priests always go into the first tabernacle to perform the rites of worship; but into the second only the high priest, once a year, and not without blood, which he offers for himself and for the sins of ignorance of the people; the Holy Spirit signifying this, that the way into the holy places was not yet made manifest while the first tabernacle still stood. This was a figure for the present time, in which gifts and sacrifices are offered which cannot make the worshipper perfect as to conscience, consisting only in meats and drinks, and various washings, and ordinances of the flesh, imposed until the time of reformation. (Heb. 9:6–10)

units.la: Iam describit, quid in tabernaculo agatur, eademque opera exponit, siue probat, quæ ad cultus pertinent: quando nimirum ait, ibi sacerdotes esse, qui sacrorum ritus peragāt, dona & sacrificia offerant: Deinde verò etiam quæ ad iustificationes pertinent, dicens, nequaquam perfectos ibi reddi iuxta cōscientiam, sed tantum prouenire iustificationes carnis: atque ita non solum cultus & iustificationes, sed etiam, quales hi fuerint, ostendit. Vtitur verò appositissimis verbis, ad transeundum ad id, quod maximè conuenit institutæ causæ. Nam istud reuera, quòd videlicet, cùm omnib. liceret ingredi quouis tempore in sancta, tamen in Sancta Sanctorum solum ingredi summum sacerdotem, idque semel in anno, maximè ad causam de sacrificio Christi pertinet: quæ præmissa sunt, ad cō firmandum & illustrandum sunt præmissa, & quodámodo præparationis loco: quod aūt nunc sequitur, maximè est necessarium: cum dicit, τὰς λατρείας ἐπιτελοῦντες, id est, cultus perficiētes, clarè videre possumus, eum hic explicare, quales cultus fuerint in veteri testamento, & quòd cultus, sicut suprà exposuimus, formâ seu causam formalem ritui significet. Tantum hoc demonstrandum est ex Scripturis, quòd sacerdotibus reliquis licitum fuerit quotidie ingredi Sancta. Primum Leuitici sexto, ubi de lege holocausti & singulorum sacrificiorum, ac de igne perpetuo præcipitur: Holocaustum, inquit, cremabitur in altari tota nocte usque mane: ignis ex eodem altari erit. Et paulo pòst: ignis autem in altari semper ardebit, quem nutriet sacerdos subijciens ligna mane per singulos dies, & impositio holocausto desuper adolebit adipes pacificorum. Ignis est iste perpetuus, qui nunquam deficiet in altari.
units.tr: Now he describes what is done in the tabernacle, and in the same breath explains, or establishes, what pertains to worship: namely, when he says that there are priests there who perform the rites of worship and offer gifts and sacrifices. Then he also treats what pertains to justifications, saying that the worshippers are by no means made perfect there as to conscience, but only justifications of the flesh arise. Thus he shows not only the worship and the justifications, but also what kind they were. He uses most fitting words in order to pass on to what most suits the cause in hand. For the fact that, while everyone was permitted to enter the holy places at any time, only the high priest entered the Holy of Holies, and that once a year, pertains most of all to the matter of Christ's sacrifice. What has been set out before is set out to confirm and illuminate it, and serves in a way as preparation. What follows now is most necessary: when he says performing the services [τὰς λατρείας ἐπιτελοῦντες], that is, completing the worship, we can clearly see that he is here explaining what sort of worship there was under the old covenant, and that worship, as we explained above, signifies the rite by its form or formal cause. Only this must be shown from the Scriptures: that the other priests were permitted to enter the holy place every day. First, Leviticus 6, where, concerning the law of the burnt offering and of each sacrifice, and concerning the perpetual fire, it is commanded: "The burnt offering," he says, "shall be burned on the altar all night until morning; the fire of the same altar shall be kept burning." And a little later: "But the fire on the altar shall always burn, which the priest shall feed, laying wood on it every morning, day by day; and when the burnt offering is set in order upon it, he shall burn on it the fat of the peace offerings. This is the perpetual fire, which shall never go out on the altar."

units.la: Certum est, omnia ista non esse facta per solum summum pontificem, sed potius per reliquos sacerdotes & Leuitas. Exodi.30. de quotidiana compositione Lucernarū vesperi & mane atque toties adolendo thymiamate, licet id per Aaronem potissimum dicatur fieri: sicut & Leuitici 24. de Lucernis & panibus propositionis. Item libro Numerorum passim multa de ministerio Leuitarum ingredientium tabernaculum: clarissimè verò, Numeror. 28. ubi sacrificia describuntur quorumcunque temporum & festiuitatum, & inter alia præcipitur, quotidie offerri duos agnos anniculos immaculatos. Non dubium, quin ad ista ministeria reliqui sacerdotes cooperati sint quotidie, propter hæc ingredientes anterius tabernaculum.
units.tr: It is certain that all these things were not done by the high priest alone, but rather by the other priests and the Levites. Exodus 30 speaks of the daily trimming of the lamps evening and morning and of the frequent burning of incense, although this is said to be done chiefly by Aaron; likewise Leviticus 24 concerning the lamps and the loaves of the presence. Likewise in the book of Numbers, in many places, much is said about the ministry of the Levites entering the tabernacle; most clearly in Numbers 28, where the sacrifices for all the times and festivals are described, and among other things it is commanded that two yearling lambs without blemish be offered every day. There is no doubt that the other priests cooperated daily in these ministries, entering the outer part of the tabernacle for that purpose.

units.la: Iam, quòd in secundū semel quotannis solus pontifex, non sine sanguine, quem offert pro se ipso & populi ignorantijs, ingrediebatur, id pluribus describitur Leuitici 16. præcepit Dominus Mosi dicens, Loquere ad Aaron fratrem tuum, ne omni tempore ingrediatur sanctuarium, quod est intra velum coram propitiatorio, quo tegitur arca, ut non moriatur, quia in nube apparebo super oraculum, nisi hæc antè fecerit. Vitulum pro peccato offeret, & arietem in holocaustum.
units.tr: Now, that the high priest alone entered the second part once a year, not without blood, which he offers for himself and for the sins of the people, is described more fully in Leviticus 16. The Lord commanded Moses, saying: "Speak to Aaron your brother, that he not enter at all times the sanctuary which is within the veil before the mercy seat, which covers the ark, lest he die; for I will appear in the cloud over the oracle, unless he first does these things. He shall offer a calf for sin and a ram for a burnt offering."

units.la: Tunica linea vestietur: fœminalibus lineis verenda celabit: Accingetur zona linea, cydarin lineam imponit capiti. Hæc enim vestimēta sunt sancta, quibus cunctis, cùm lotus fuerit, induetur, suscipietque ab vniuersa multitudine filiorum Israel duos hircos pro peccato, & vnum arietem in holocaustum: Cùmque obtulerit vitulum & orauerit pro se, & pro domo sua, duos hircos statuet coram Domino in ostio tabernaculi testimonii, mittensque super vtrumque sortem, vnam Domino, & alteram capro emissario, cuius exierit sors, Domino offeret illum pro peccato: cuius autem in caprum emissarium, statuet eum viuum coram Domino, ut fundat preces super eo, & emittet eum in solitudinem. His ita celebratis offeret vitulum, & rogans pro se & pro domo sua, immolabit eum: assumptoq; thuribulo, quod de prunis altaris impleuerit, & hauriens manu compositum thymiama in incensum, ultra velum intrabit in sancta, ut positis super ignem aromatib. nebula eorum & vapor operiat oraculum, quod est supra testimonium, & non moriatur. Tollet quoq; de sanguine vituli, & asperget digito septies contra propitiatorium ad Orientem: cumq; mactauerit hircum pro peccato populi, inferet sanguinem eius intra velum, sicut praeceptum est de sanguine vituli, ut aspergat e regione oraculi, & expiet sanctuarium ab immunditiis filiorum Israel, & a praevaricationibus eorum, cunctisq; peccatis. Haec cibi, ex quibus omnia ista manifesta. Vbi multa typica etiam de Christo, qui figuratur ibi per vitulum, per hircum, sicut & per pontificem. Quod autem dicit, pro populi ignorantiis, supra initio capitis quinti ostendimus, qualia dicantur in lege peccata per ignorantiam commissa, quae septuaginta vocant ἀκουσίως, id est, non sponte, inuito animo perpetrata. De anima, quae per ignorantiam peccauerit, lege Numer. 15. Leuit. 4. Theophylactus notat, ignorantias dici, vel ad ostendendum hoc discriminis inter sacrificia legalia, & sacrificium Christi, quod illa remittunt tantum peccata per ignorantiam commissa: istud vero ea etiam, quae a scientibus & volentibus perpetrantur: vel ad tacite arguendum omnis generis homines, quorum nulli sunt, qui non sint, saltem peccatis per ignorantiam admissis obnoxij, ac proinde rei coram Domino. Sequitur:
units.tr: "He shall be clothed in a linen tunic; he shall cover his nakedness with linen breeches; he shall be girded with a linen belt, and wear a linen mitre on his head. For these are holy garments, and when he has washed, he shall put on all of them. He shall receive from the whole congregation of the sons of Israel two goats for sin and one ram for a burnt offering. When he has offered the calf and prayed for himself and his house, he shall set the two goats before the Lord at the door of the tabernacle of the testimony, and cast lots over them, one lot for the Lord and the other for the scapegoat. The goat on which the lot for the Lord falls he shall offer for sin; but the goat on which the lot for the scapegoat falls he shall set alive before the Lord, that he may make prayer over it, and send it away into the wilderness. When these things have been done, he shall offer the calf, and praying for himself and his house, he shall slaughter it. Taking a censer full of coals from the altar, and taking compounded incense in his hand, he shall put it on the incense before the Lord, and he shall go within the veil into the holy places, so that the cloud and vapour of the spices placed on the fire may cover the oracle which is above the testimony, and he may not die. He shall also take some of the blood of the calf and sprinkle it with his finger seven times toward the mercy seat on the east side; and when he has slain the goat for the sin of the people, he shall bring its blood within the veil, as was commanded concerning the blood of the calf, and sprinkle it toward the mercy seat, and make atonement for the sanctuary, because of the uncleanness of the sons of Israel and their transgressions, all their sins." In these things all this is made plain. Here much that is typical is found, also concerning Christ, who is prefigured in the calf, in the goat, and likewise in the high priest. As for what he says, for the ignorances of the people, we showed above at the beginning of chapter 5 what sort of sins committed through ignorance the law speaks of, which the Seventy call akousiōs [ἀκουσίως], that is, not willingly, committed against the will. Concerning a soul that has sinned through ignorance, see Numbers 15 and Leviticus 4. Theophylact notes that they are called ignorances either to show this difference between the legal sacrifices and the sacrifice of Christ, that the former remit only sins committed in ignorance, whereas the latter also remit those committed by people who know and will what they do; or to tacitly accuse all kinds of men, of whom there is none who is not, at least through sins committed in ignorance, liable and therefore guilty before the Lord. It follows:

units.la: Illud significante Spiritu Sancto, nondum manifestatam esse sanctorum viam, adhuc priore tabernaculo consistente) Prudenter interponit typicam interpretationem hanc, tum ut, quemadmodum supra attigimus, excitet animos ad ita interpretandum caetera, quae de tabernaculo sunt dicta: tum ut ostendendo, non illud tantum de summo pontifice semel ingrediente in sancta Sanctorum, verum etiam caetera omnia commode posse de rebus per Christum gerendis explicari, fidem faciat, non posse reijci, quod ipse per typum de Christi sacrificio adducit.
units.tr: The Holy Spirit signifying this, that the way of the saints was not yet made manifest while the former tabernacle still stood. He wisely inserts this typical interpretation, first, as we touched on above, to rouse minds to interpret in the same way the other things said about the tabernacle; and second, by showing that not only the entry of the high priest once into the Holy of Holies but all the other things can fitly be explained of the works accomplished through Christ, to make it clear that what he adduces from the type concerning Christ's sacrifice cannot be rejected.

units.la: Hac enim ratione obturat os aduersarijs, qui fortasis dicturi erant, illud de vnica in anno oblatione, Christo non recte aptari, quando reliquae partes historiae nullo pacto rebus per Christum gestis aptari possent. Verum ipse vna hac interpretatione etiam in caeteris omnibus Christum esse adumbratum non obscure indicat. Dixit autem magna Emphasi, ita significasse spiritum Sanctum: Neque enim tanquam suam interpretationem proponit, quae ob contemptum personae, & ob humanam fragilitatem, ut humanum commentum facile potuisset reijci: sed, ut profectam a spiritu Sancto: sicut reuera spiritu Sancto afflati locuti sunt sancti homines: & quae ibi decreta sunt, cum lex daretur, caeteraq; legalia constituerentur, non tantum a Deo patre profecta sunt, verum etiam a filio & a spiritu Sancto: sicut supra de Christo ostendimus cap. 3. vbi Christus dicitur eandem domum administrasse, quam administrarat Moses: de spiritu Sancto autem eodem capite, vbi dicitur, Quapropter sicut dicit spiritus ille Sanctus.
units.tr: For in this way he stops the mouths of opponents who might perhaps have said that the single offering in the year does not fittingly apply to Christ, when the remaining parts of the account could in no way be applied to the things done through Christ. But by this one interpretation he also indicates plainly that Christ is foreshadowed in all the other things as well. He said, moreover, with great emphasis, that the Holy Spirit signified it in this way. For he does not put it forward as his own interpretation, which, because of the lowliness of the person and human frailty, could easily have been rejected as a human invention; rather, he presents it as coming from the Holy Spirit, just as holy men truly spoke when inspired by the Holy Spirit. And the things decreed there, when the law was given and the other legal institutions were established, came not only from God the Father but also from the Son and the Holy Spirit, as we showed above in chapter 3, where Christ is said to have administered the same house that Moses administered; and concerning the Holy Spirit in the same chapter, where it is said, "Wherefore, as that Holy Spirit says."

units.la: Nondum manifestatam esse sanctorum viam adhuc priore tabernaculo consistente) Quod caeteri sacerdotes non ingrediebantur Sancta Sanctorum, significatum est ea re, quod stante priore tabernaculo, id est, lege ac sacrificijs, via nondum fuerit manifestata in sancta, id est, in caelos. Quando enim Christus ipse nondum fuit in caelos oblatione sanguinis sui ingressus, reuera nec aliis sanctis hominibus eo licuit ingredi. Christus via & ostiu in sancta sanctorum, & ipse prius in ea debebat ingredi, quam aliis ingressus pateret. Nonnulli quidem interpretantur viam sanctorum modum sanctificationis hominum, qui modus declarandus erat aduentu ipsius Christi, qui sanguinem suum pro sanctificatione seu iustificatione hominum offerret. Neq; id prorsus inepte. Sed magis quadrat, si τὰ ἅγια accipiamus neutro genere potius quam masculino, sicut in historia tota ponitur, ut de loco, non de personis sermo est, & per sancta intelligamus caelos, quemadmodum Apostolus ipse post interpretatur. Atq; ita Chrysostomus & Theophylactus. Porro tabernaculum anterius respectu interioris, quod ipse interpretatur caelos, nos habita ratione antitheseos interpretaremur ecclesiam in terris adhuc constitutam: verum Apostolus ita loquitur, ut per tabernaculum anterius significet potius legem ad id temporis durantem, & suas habentem vires. Sed sciendum est, interius tabernaculum recte significare & caelos, & Euangelium per Christum reuelatum: eodemq; modo tabernaculum exterius pariter significare & ecclesiam constitutam in terris, & ipsam legem, seu tempus legis. Proinde praesenti loco rectius interpretatur de lege, quam de ecclesia, illationis ratione ita poscente. Nam de ecclesia dicere, quod in ea perstante non fuisset manifestata via in caelos, id profecto non fuisset verum consentaneum.
units.tr: That the way of the saints was not yet made manifest while the former tabernacle still stood. The fact that the other priests did not enter the Holy of Holies is signified by this: that while the former tabernacle, that is, the law and the sacrifices, still stood, the way into the holy places, that is, into heaven, had not yet been made manifest. For since Christ himself had not yet entered into heaven by the offering of his own blood, in truth it was not lawful for other holy men to enter there either. Christ is the way and the door into the holy of holies, and he himself had to enter there first before the entrance was opened to others. Some indeed interpret "the way of the saints" as the manner of sanctifying men, which manner was to be declared by the coming of Christ himself, who would offer his blood for the sanctification or justification of men. And this is not altogether absurd. But it fits better if we take "the holy things" [τὰ ἅγια] in the neuter rather than the masculine gender, as it is used throughout the whole account, so that the discourse concerns a place and not persons, and we understand by "the holy places" the heavens, as the Apostle himself afterwards explains. So also Chrysostom and Theophylact. Moreover, if we took the outer tabernacle in relation to the inner, which he himself interprets as the heavens, by the reasoning of contrast we would interpret it as the church still established on earth. But the Apostle speaks in such a way that by the outer tabernacle he signifies rather the law, which lasted at that time and had its own force. But it must be known that the inner tabernacle rightly signifies both heaven and the gospel revealed through Christ; and in the same way the outer tabernacle equally signifies both the church established on earth and the law itself, or the time of the law. Therefore in the present passage it is more rightly interpreted of the law than of the church, as the logic of the inference requires. For to say of the church that while it stood the way into heaven had not been made manifest would certainly not have been true or consistent.

units.la: Quadoquidem, cum ecclesia semper fuerit, & semper maneat, & semper fuerint in ea aliqui viri sancti ab initio inde mundi conditi, certè in ea patet ingressus in coelos, & maximè post Christum manifestatum, & in coelos ingressum. Sed eo tempore ecclesiae, quo ad huc durabat lex cum suis sacrificijs, reuera non fuit manifestata via in coelos, aut non nisi per typos & figuras vtrunque adumbrata. Itaque respectu certi temporis in ecclesia, & quatum ad modu docendi, verum est, quòd in ecclesia non fuit manifestata via in sancta sanctorum, siue in coelos.
units.tr: Since, indeed, the church has always been and always remains, and there have always been some holy men in it from the beginning of the created world, certainly in the church the entrance into heaven lies open, and especially since Christ has been manifested and has entered into heaven. But at that time of the church, when the law with its sacrifices still lasted, the way into heaven truly had not been made manifest, or else it was foreshadowed only through types and figures. Therefore, with respect to a certain time in the church, and as to the manner of teaching, it is true that in the church the way into the Holy of Holies, or into heaven, had not been made manifest.

units.la: Quae erat (vel potius quod, scilicet tabernaculum) similitudo pro tempore tum praesente: latet hic ratio, quare ibi non potuerit manifestari uia Sanctorum, sumpta ex eo, quòd initio huius partis de sacrificio Christi dictu est, omnia videlicet, quae in veteri sacerdotio fiebant, umbrae tantum atque exemplari seruiuisse coelestium longe post accipiendorum.
units.tr: What was (or rather, what, namely the tabernacle) was a likeness for the time then present. Here lies the reason why the way of the saints could not have been made manifest there, drawn from the fact that at the beginning of this part it was said concerning the sacrifice of Christ that all the things done in the old priesthood served only as a shadow and pattern of the heavenly things to be received long afterwards.

units.la: Similitudinem siue parabolam vocat vetus testanentum, quia non res vera, sed similitudo tantum perfectionis in eo est exhibita: sed in Euangelio similitudo omnis euacuata est, rebus ipsis sese in apertum proferetibus. Vox autem παραβολὴς, hebraeis בשנ in sacris literis, & similitudinem seu illationem significat, & sermonem obscurum. Similitudine, ut Marci 13. A' ficu vero discite similitudinem, μάθετε τὴν παραβολήν, cùm ramus eius iam tener fuerit, produxeritque folia, scitis quòd prope sit aestas: sic & vos cùm videritis haec fieri, scitote, quòd prope sit in foribus. Sermonem autem obscurum Matthaei 13. Haec omnia locutus est Iesus per parabolas ad turbas, & sine parabola nihil locutus est illis, ut compleretur, quod dictum fuerat per prophetam, qui ait (Psalmo 77) Aperiam in parabolis os meum, eructabo abscondita a constitutione mundi. Et ibidem propter obscuritatem dicebant discipuli, Explica nobis parabolam zizaniorum agri. Vtram autem accipias significationem, ea conuenit & legi, in qua & Similitudo tantum, & obscuritas siue vmbra rerum futurarum. Nec vero simpliciter dicit Similitudinem, sed pro tempore tum instante quod videlicet erat ante Christum mundo manifestatum. Propterea tempus, quo hic reuelatus est, vocatur plenitudo temporis, uel tepus adimpletum, quo praesenti illa quoque similitudo euanescit, & obscuritas clara redditur.
units.tr: The Old Testament calls it a likeness or parable, because in it there is not the true thing but only a likeness of perfection is displayed; but in the Gospel every likeness is emptied out, the things themselves coming forth into the open. The word παραβολή [mashal], which in the Hebrew of the sacred writings is [משל], signifies both a likeness or comparison and an obscure discourse. As a likeness, as in Mark 13: "From the fig tree learn the parable [μάθετε τὴν παραβολήν]: when its branch is now tender and has put forth leaves, you know that summer is near; so also you, when you see these things happening, know that it is near, at the doors." And as an obscure discourse, Matthew 13: "Jesus spoke all these things in parables to the crowds, and without a parable he spoke nothing to them, so that what was spoken through the prophet might be fulfilled, who says (Psalm 77), 'I will open my mouth in parables, I will utter things hidden from the foundation of the world.'" And in the same place, because of the obscurity, the disciples said, "Explain to us the parable of the tares of the field." Whichever of these meanings you take, it agrees with the law, in which there is both mere likeness and obscurity, or the shadow of things to come. Nor does he speak simply of a likeness, but of one for the time then present, that is, the time before Christ was manifested to the world. Therefore the time in which he was revealed is called the fullness of time, or the time fulfilled, when that likeness also vanishes away in the present, and the obscurity is rendered clear.

units.la: In quo dona sacrificiaque offeruntur.
units.tr: In which gifts and sacrifices are offered.

units.la: In tabernaculo istud fieri solitum satis est manifestum, & sepius iam dictum est proprieque ad cultus pertinet. Apparet autem, plurali numero ista poni, ut, cùm multa sint & varia, & tamen ex ijs non sequatur iustificatio, post crescat dignitas vnici sacrificij Christi, quod vnum ad redemptionem vniuersalem parandam sufficiens praedicatur.
units.tr: That these things were customarily done in the tabernacle is quite plain, as has been said often already, and they properly pertain to worship. But it appears that these things are put in the plural, so that, although there are many and various things, and yet justification does not follow from them, the dignity of the one sacrifice of Christ may then increase, since that one sacrifice is declared sufficient to procure universal redemption.

units.la: Quae non possint iuxta conscientiam perfectum reddere cultorem) Dum aperit, quales sint legis iustificationes, simul plenius confirmat, quod dixerat, uiam sanctorum nondum fuisse durante priore tabernaculo manifestatam. Sic enim fere argumentatur: ut aliqui ingrederentur in Sancta, oportebat eos esse perfectos & iustificatos iuxta conscientiam:
units.tr: "Which cannot make the worshipper perfect as regards conscience." While he sets out what the justifications of the law are, he at the same time more fully confirms what he had said, namely that the way of the saints had not yet been revealed while the earlier tabernacle endured. For he argues roughly like this: in order for some to enter into the holy places, they had to be perfect and justified as regards conscience;

units.la: Atqui per sacrificia prioris tabernaculi, non perficiebantur seu iustificabantur aliqui iuxta conscientiam.
units.tr: but through the sacrifices of the earlier tabernacle, none were made perfect or justified as regards conscience.

units.la: Ergo perstiftente illo tabernaculo cum suis sacrificijs nulli in Sancta Sanctorum, id est, coelos ingredi poterant.
units.tr: Therefore, while that tabernacle with its sacrifices remained, none could enter into the Holy of Holies, that is, heaven.

units.la: Itanamque recte sequitur, si non potuerunt ibi iustificari conscientiae, nec potuit uia in coelos aperiri. Certum enim est, immundos & pollutos in Sancta Sanctorum, id est, coelos, non potuisse ingredi, id quod labrum aeneum ante Sancta Sanctorum positum indicabat: item sacrificia & oblationes & tot praeparationes, quae per ipsum summum sacerdotem fieri debebant, quando ipse Sancta Sanctorum erat ingressurus. Et si non poterat Sancto Sacrorum ingredi locum illum terrenum & typicum, nisi prius multis modis & studiosissime purgati: quanto minus ingredientur in vera Sancta Sanctorum, id est, coelos, qui purgati prius non fuerint? Itaq; maior per se est manifesta. Minore probat ipse per contrarium, dices: In cibis duntaxat, & potionibus, & diuersis ablutionibus ac iustificationibus carnis: quasi summatim diceret: Perfectio omnis seu iustificatio, quae paratur in lege, sita est in obseruatione ciborum, potuum, item in ablutionibus, ideoque tantum externa est & carnalis. Sed, conscientia, in qua haeret peccatum, est res in aeterna & spiritualis. Ergo per illa nequaquam perficiuntur conscientiae, nequaquam a peccatis purgantur. Vult autem prudenter discerni conscientiam seu animam a corpore, intelligiq; secundum earum rerum diuersitate etiam longe diuersas esse perfectiones seu iustificationes: sicut duplex peccatum seu inquinatio, quaedam, qua inquinabantur corpora, ut, contactus mortui, vel rei secundum lege pro immunda iudicatae, sumptus cibus vel potus lege vetitus, temporum uel dierum negligentia, certorum locorum ingressus: quaedam vero, qua inquinabatur anima seu conscientia, ut sunt peccata, quae nos quoq; nunc censemus inquinare, quae Christus dixit prodire de corde hominis, inuidia, inquam, adulterium, homicidium, &c. Ita duplex quoque purgatio seu iustificatio debet intelligi, sicut & supra diximus, altera secundum corpus, altera secundum
units.tr: And so it follows rightly: if consciences could not be justified there, neither could the way into heaven be opened. For it is certain that the unclean and defiled could not enter into the Holy of Holies, that is, heaven, as the bronze laver placed before the Holy of Holies indicated; likewise the sacrifices, the offerings and the many preparations that had to be made by the high priest himself when he was about to enter the Holy of Holies. And if he could not enter that earthly and typical holy place unless he had first been purified in many ways and with the utmost care, how much less will those enter the true Holy of Holies, that is, heaven, who have not first been purified? So the major premise is plain in itself. The minor he proves by the contrary, saying: "in foods only, and drinks, and various washings and justifications of the flesh." It is as if he were saying in brief: all the perfection or justification that is provided in the law consists in the observance of foods and drinks, and likewise in washings, and is therefore only external and carnal. But conscience, in which sin clings, is an eternal and spiritual thing. Therefore those things by no means perfect consciences or cleanse them from sins. He wisely wishes conscience or soul to be distinguished from the body, and it is to be understood that, according to the diversity of these things, the perfections or justifications are also far different. Just as there is a twofold sin or pollution: one by which bodies were polluted, as by contact with a dead body or with a thing the law judged unclean, eating or drinking what the law forbade, neglect of times or days, entry into certain places; and another by which the soul or conscience was polluted, such as the sins which we too now judge to defile, which Christ said come forth from the heart of man: envy, I mean, adultery, murder, and so on. So a twofold purification or justification should likewise be understood, as we also said above: one according to the body, the other according to

units.la: animam seu conscientiam: è quibus prior illa quidè paratur & perficitur per sacrificia le galia, ita ut offerentes pro talib. peccatis sacrificia præscripta, iam essent mundi & perfecti ierum coram Deo. Sed posterior nullo modo potest ex illis sacrificijs contingere, sed solum per vnicum sacrificium Christi paratur credentib. Vnde & Prophetę sepissimè ea de re concionabantur: ut Esaiæ 1. Ne offeratis vltrà sacrificiũ frustrà. Hierem. 11. Nunquid cat nes sanctę auferūt à te iniquitates tuas? Micheę 6. Nunquid placari potest Deus in millib. arietum, aut in millib. hircorum pinguium? Et Apostolus paulò pòst, potissimumq; initio capitis decimi idè exponit, probatq; multò clarissimè. Quicunq; verò ibi perfecti inuenti sunt & iustificati, quales multos fuisse inter sanctos patres constat, ij iustificati sunt non propter sacrificia, vel quæcunq; opera legis, sed per fidè in Christum: sicut per fidem iustificatum Abrahamum probatur Rom. 4. Et de multis alijs idè ostenditur cap. 10. 11. 2. huius epistolæ. Atq; in eiusdem rei argumentum legimus plerunq;, vbi de sacrificijs offerendis agitur, subiectum: Orabitq; pro eo sacerdos, & dimittetur ei. Leuit. 5. Quod non aliam ob cau-sam factum, quàm ad ostendendum, quòd non per sacrificia iustificarentur conscientiæ, sed potius per fidem, quæ in oratione exercetur. Igitur propter obseruationes legales, itè propter sacrificia, tantum carnalis, externa, & coram mundo parabatur iustitia, & nequa quàm purgabantur conscientiæ. Porrò de iustitia legali ex cibis habes Leuit. 11. De potionib. Leuit. 10. vbi vacaturis orationi, aut sacrificio interdicitur potus vini & omnis liquoris inebriantis. De diuersis ablutionib. Leuit. 15. Num. 8. Deut. 23. Ergo hac enumeratione omnia coplexus est, quæcunq; in lege existimabantur ad purgationem seu iustificationem factę: & aptissimè dicit, in omnibus illis: quandoquidem carnalia tantùm erant, etiâ non nisi carnalem iustitiam parantia. Vnde magnam Emphasin habet vocabulũ carnis, ita voci iustificationis adiectum, vtpote valde necessariũ & aptum præsenti caussæ. Sic verò & alibi caro pro rebus externis & carnalib. quales in lege erant propositæ. Galat. 3. Adeò stultì estis, cùm Spiritu cœperitis, nunc carne consummamini. Philip. 3. Si quisquam alius videtur fiduciam habere in carne, ego magis habeo. Et supra cap. 7. Christus sacerdos describitur, non secundum legem mandati carnalis, sed iuxta potentiam vitæ indissolubilis. Huc iam confer, quæ de cibis, potu, &c. habentur Colof. 2. & alibi, de inani ista iustitia carnali, quæ ex operib. legis parabatur. Vsq; ad tempus correctionis imposita. Interpretatur, quid sibi voluerit supra dicens, tabernaculum fuisse similitudinem pro tempore. Quanquá & gravissima occupatione istud adiectum videtur. Nam cũ ita asseritur, legalia illa tantùm con duxisse adiustificationem carnis, nihilq; valere ad perfectionem conscientiarum, obijcere poterant quidam, omnia igitur illa videri frustrà à Deo ordinata atq; præcepta, quando non maior vtilitas inde sequeretur. Respondet ergo, illa utiliter pro tempore fuisse imposita, ac durare debuisse, dum adesset tempus correctionis, quo videlicet præstantiora & vtilia per Christum proferrentur, per quem iustificatio conscientiarum perficeretur, ac via in cœlos patefieret. Rectissimè autem tempus Euangelij vocat tempus correctionis. Corriguntur, quæ aut, cùm vitij aliquid habet, emendantur, aut, cùm ijs aliquid deest, perficiuntur. Quare & legis potestas extenuatur ea voce, & Euangelij dignitas mirificè amplificatur: atq; Euangelio iustissimè tribuitur, quòd lege corrigat perficiatq;. Sic enim Christus ipse ait: Non veni soluere legem, sed adimplere: &, Audistis, quia dictum est antiquis, Non concupisces: Ego autem dico vobis, &c. Item de dente pro dente, seu lege talionis: itè de libello repudij, &c. Rom. 8. Quod lex præstare non potuit, ea parte, qua imbecillis erat per carnem, hoc Deus proprio filio suo misso sub specie carnis peccato obnoxiæ præstitit. Galat. 4. Nos cum essemus pueri, sub elementis mundi eramus in seruitute adaćti: at vbi venit plenitudo temporis, &c. Et supra dixit, legem non potuisse ad perfectionem adducere: quare erat perficienda corrigendaq;: item in locum corporaliũ surroganda spiritualia. Igitur tempus, quo Christus in mundum veniens propalauit suũ Euangeliũ, tempus correctionis recte dicitur. Ac valde prodest ista præmitti, quibus tantopere extenuantur & cultus, & sacrificia testameti veteris. Hac enim ratione mirũ in modũ crescit, atq; amplificat dignitas sacrificij, in nouo testamento per Christũ oblati. Adeò nihil sine certo et graui cõsi lio p Apostolũ hũc est positũ, neq; sine caussa priore collationis parte tot verbis cõtexuit.
units.tr: the soul or conscience. Of these, the former is indeed prepared and perfected through the legal sacrifices, so that those who offered the prescribed sacrifices for such sins were already clean and perfect before God. But the latter can in no way come from those sacrifices; it is granted to believers only through the one sacrifice of Christ. Hence the prophets also preached very often on this matter, as in Esai. 1: "Bring no more vain sacrifice." Hierem. 11: "Can holy flesh take away your iniquities from you?" Mich. 6: "Can God be appeased with thousands of rams, or with thousands of fat goats?" And the Apostle, a little later and especially at the beginning of chapter ten, explains this and proves it far more clearly. But whoever were found perfect and justified there, and it is established that there were many such among the holy fathers, those were justified not because of sacrifices or any works of the law, but through faith in Christ, as Abraham, justified through faith, is shown in Rom. 4. And the same is shown of many others in chapters 10, 11 and 12 of this epistle. And as evidence of the same matter we often read, where the sacrifices to be offered are treated, the words: "The priest shall pray for him, and it shall be forgiven him," Levit. 5. This was done for no other reason than to show that consciences were justified not through sacrifices, but rather through faith, which is exercised in prayer. Therefore, on account of the legal observances, and likewise on account of the sacrifices, only a carnal and external righteousness was procured, one that counts before the world, and consciences were by no means cleansed. Moreover, concerning legal righteousness in foods, see Levit. 11; concerning drinks, Levit. 10, where drinking wine and every intoxicating liquor is forbidden to those about to devote themselves to prayer or sacrifice; concerning the various washings, Levit. 15, Num. 8, Deut. 23. Therefore by this enumeration he has embraced everything that was thought in the law to be done for purification or justification; and he says most aptly "in all those," since they were only carnal and could produce only carnal righteousness. Hence the word "flesh," added to the word "justification," carries great emphasis, being very necessary and apt for the present argument. And so elsewhere too "flesh" is used for external and carnal things, such as were set forth in the law. Galat. 3: "Are you so foolish? Having begun in the Spirit, are you now being perfected in the flesh?" Philip. 3: "If anyone else seems to have confidence in the flesh, I have more." And above, in chapter 7, Christ the priest is described not according to the law of a carnal command, but according to the power of an indissoluble life. Now compare with this what is said about foods, drink and so on in Coloss. 2 and elsewhere, about that empty carnal righteousness which was produced by the works of the law, "imposed until the time of correction." He explains what he meant when he said above that the tabernacle was a figure for the time. Yet this addition also seems to be a matter of great weight. For when it is asserted that those legal things only led to justification of the flesh and were worth nothing for the perfection of consciences, some might object: then all those things seem to have been ordained and commanded by God in vain, since no greater usefulness followed from them. He answers, therefore, that they were usefully imposed for the time, and ought to have lasted while the time of correction was at hand, when the more excellent and useful things would be brought forward through Christ, through whom the justification of consciences would be perfected and the way into heaven opened. Moreover, he rightly calls the time of the gospel the time of correction. Things are corrected when, if they have some fault, they are amended, or, if something is lacking in them, they are perfected. Hence the power of the law is diminished by that word, and the dignity of the gospel is wonderfully enhanced; and it is most justly attributed to the gospel that it corrects and perfects the law. For Christ himself says: "I came not to destroy the law, but to fulfil it"; and "You have heard that it was said to the ancients, You shall not covet; but I say to you," and so on. Likewise concerning "an eye for an eye, or the law of retaliation," and likewise concerning the bill of divorce, and so on. Rom. 8: "What the law could not do, in that it was weak through the flesh, God did by sending his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh, which is subject to sin." Galat. 4: "When we were children, we were held in bondage under the elements of the world; but when the fullness of time came," and so on. And above he said that the law could not bring anything to perfection; therefore it had to be perfected and corrected, and spiritual things were to be substituted in place of bodily ones. Therefore the time in which Christ, coming into the world, made known his gospel is rightly called the time of correction. And it is very profitable to premise these things, by which both the worship and the sacrifices of the old covenant are so greatly diminished. For by this reasoning the dignity of the sacrifice offered in the new covenant through Christ increases and is magnified in a wonderful way. So nothing has been set down here by the Apostle without a certain and grave purpose, and not without cause has he woven so many words into the first part of his comparison.

units.la: Dignitas sacrificij.
units.tr: The dignity of the sacrifice.

units.la: At Christus accedens pontifex futurorum bonorum per maius & perfectius tabernaculum, non manu factum, hoc est, non huius structurę, neq; per sanguinem hircorum ac vitulorum, sed per proprium sanguinem ingressus est semel in sancta, æterna redemptione reperta.
units.tr: But Christ, coming as high priest of the good things to come, through the greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with hands, that is, not of this construction, and not through the blood of goats and calves, but through his own blood, entered once for all into the holy places, having obtained eternal redemption.

units.la: Altera pars collationis de sacrificio Christi, breuiter quidem, sed sic artificiosè reddita, ut nouo quoq; testamento non minus, quà veteri, suum sanctũ seu potius sancta sancto-rum, suos item cultus, tuasq; iustificationes esse, luculenter ostendat. Sanctum enim describit, ubi ait, Christum ingressum in Sacta æterna, & per maius ac perfectius tabernaculum, non manu factum. Cultus vero, ubi ait, eum obtulisse sanguinem, non hircorum aut vitulorum, sed proprium. Iustificationes denique, ubi ait, per Christū repertam redemptionem. Neque omisit, quæ ad partium amplificationem conducunt. Siue enim spectes personam offerentem, id est, Christum, siue sanctum, siue cultus, siue iustificationes, sunt omnia certè elegati orationis forma illustrata amplificataq;, ut quiuis clarè intelligere queat, hæc multo præstantiora ijs; quæ in veteri testamento habebantur, licet hæc alias admodum splendida extiterint. Quæ omnia clariora euadent, si partes singulas breui ter expendamus.
units.tr: The second part of the comparison, concerning the sacrifice of Christ, is set out briefly but so skilfully that it clearly shows that the New Testament, no less than the Old, has its sanctuary (or rather its holy of holies), its own forms of worship, and its own ordinances of justification. For it describes the sanctuary where it says that Christ entered the eternal holy places, through the greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with hands. It describes the worship where it says that he offered his own blood, not the blood of goats or calves. And it describes the justification where it speaks of the redemption obtained through Christ. Nor has it omitted what serves to amplify each part. For whether you look at the person offering, that is Christ, or at the sanctuary, the worship, or the justification, all are certainly illustrated and magnified by an elegant form of expression, so that anyone can clearly understand that these things are far more excellent than those that were held in the Old Testament, although those were in other respects very splendid. All of this will become clearer if we weigh the individual parts briefly.

units.la: At Christus, inquit, accedens) cum græcè habeatur παραγινόμενος, quod non inepte vertatur γενόμενος. assistens, Namen quia statim additur de ipsius ingressu, & non admodum conueniret constituere, Christū prius assistente & interpellante, quàm ingressus esset, ideo aptius dicitur accedens. Depingit autem hæc vox Christū veluti cum magnifico apparatu sese componentem ad suum sacrificium offerendum, ut cum iam quasi oculis putes te cernere ingredientem suum tabernaculum. Vel, ut Chrysostomus iudicat, adueniens, non factus, quia nō nunc primùm factus pontifex, sed nunc primùm prodiens & mundo exhibitus. Vocat Christum pontificem futurorum bonorum, id est, cœlestium & post hanc vitam expectandorum, ad ostendendum eius excellentiam præ sacerdotibus legalibus, qui erant tantùm pontifices rerum pro tempore illo habentium suam æstimationem. Futura dixit pro cœlestibus, tum quòd supra dixit; ea, quæ fiebant in veteri testamento fuisse umbras & exemplaria, sicut & mox initio capitis decimi dicet, legem obtinere umbram futurorum bonorum: tum quòd proximè dixerit, prius tabernaculum siue legem fuisse similitudinem pro tempore tum præsente: itaq; ijs quæ illo tempore habebant suum vigore, opponuntur iam bona futura. Vel, futura dicuntur spiritualia quæcunque bona, quæ hic etiam tempore Euangelij revelati obtinentur: quę quidem futura dicuntur respectu temporalium, quæ sub lege habebantur pro tempore tùm præsente.
units.tr: "But Christ," he says, "coming" [παραγινόμενος], which may fairly be rendered "becoming" [γενόμενος], "standing by." Since the statement about his entering follows at once, and it would not fit well to place Christ standing by and interceding before he entered, the word "coming" is the more apt. This word portrays Christ as it were preparing himself with a splendid array to offer his sacrifice, so that you might almost seem to see him with your own eyes entering his tabernacle. Or, as Chrysostom judges, "arriving," not "made," because he was not now first made high priest, but now first came forth and was shown to the world. He calls Christ "high priest of the good things to come," that is, of the heavenly good things which are to be expected after this life, to show his excellence above the legal priests, who were only high priests of the things that had value for the time then present. He says "to come" instead of "heavenly," both because he has said above that the things done in the Old Testament were shadows and copies, as he will say soon at the beginning of chapter ten, that the law holds a shadow of the good things to come, and because he has just said that the earlier tabernacle, or law, was a likeness for the time then present; so the good things to come are set against those which had their force at that time. Or, the good things are called "to come" in the sense that they are spiritual goods which are now obtained even in the time of the revealed Gospel; these are called "to come" in respect of the temporal goods which were held under the law for the time then present.

units.la: Per maius & perfectius tabernaculū, non manu factū, hoc est, non huius structuræ) Nonnulli, ut Chrysostomus, & hunc secutus Theophylactus, hic interpretantur priustabernaculum carne, quam Christus induit, secundū verò diuinitate Christi, quæ quasi velo ab altera discernatur. Sed nihil opus hoc loco huiusmodi interpretationibus allegoricis, consistamus simpliciter in typica interpretatione, eamque ampletamur, quam ipse Apostolus proponit.
units.tr: Through the greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with hands, that is, not of this construction) Some, like Chrysostom, and after him Theophylact, interpret here that the first tabernacle is the flesh which Christ put on, and the second is the divinity of Christ, which is distinguished from the other as by a veil. But there is no need here for allegorical interpretations of this kind. Let us simply keep to the typical interpretation, and develop it as the Apostle himself sets it out.

units.la: Secundum hanc verò Sancta Sanctorum typus fuit cœlorum, quos Christus semel ingressus est, sanguinem suum patri offerens, sicut postea clarius exponitur per apostolum, cuius respectu anterius tabernaculū rectè dici posset ecclesia in tabernaculo constituto, sicut etiam quidam hic interpretantur: quandoquidem hic dicitur Christus ingressus per tabernaculum in sancta, ut duo distincta loca aperte significetur. Ergo sententia est, quòd vbi legales pontifices ingresi sunt per tabernaculum materiale, manibus hominum paratum, in sancta sanctorum itidem materialia & manibus hominum parata, Christus ingressus est etiam per tabernaculum multò excellentius, in sancta etiam longè præstantiora, nempe cœlos ipsos. Itaq; de huiusmodi tabernaculo loquens, merito dicit Christum ingressum per tabernaculū multo amplius & perfectius in sancta. Reuera maius est tabernaculū, per quod Christus ingressus est, quàm erat vetus illud, quia latius patet tota multitudo & amplitudo credentium, quibus constat ecclesia; quàm angustum illud è tentorijs confectum tabernaculū. Præterea multò perfectius, quia lex, ut dictum est capite septimo, nihil ad perfectionem adducebat: item sicut iamiam dicebatur, dona sacrificiaq; in tabernaculo legali oblata non poterat perfectum reddere cultorem iuxta conscientia. Tertiò addit, non manu factum: tabernaculum legale cum omni apparatu fuit humana opera atque arte construction: at ecclesia non nisi per Deum ipsum & spiritum Sanctum colligitur: & propterea rectè subijcitur, summatim & uniuersaliter enunciando, eam nullo modo esse huius structuræ, id est, materialis, externæ, carnalis, temporalis, & non diu duraturæ. Ita particula ταῦτης demonstrat opinor, quicquid in mundo hoc fabricari excellens possit, ut sit sententia: Nullo pacto esse mudanum istud sanctum, sicut supra dictū vetus testamentū habuisse sanctum mundanū: sic etiam de cœlis 2. Corinth. 5. habemus domicilium non manu factū, sed æternū in cœlis. Per huiusmodi igitur tabernaculū ingressus est Christus in sancta, in secundū tabernaculum, videlicet cœlos. Proinde satis liquet, istas antitheses valde eleganter positas, ad amplificandam dignitatem tabernaculi, per quod Christus ingressus est, neque opus est prolixiore oratione demonstremus descriptiones istas ecclesiæ optimè conuenire.
units.tr: According to this, the Holy of Holies was a type of the heavens, into which Christ entered once, offering his blood to the Father, as is later explained more clearly by the Apostle. In relation to this, the earlier tabernacle could rightly be called the Church set up in the tabernacle, as some also interpret here, since it is said that Christ entered through the tabernacle into the holy places, so that two distinct places are clearly signified. The sense, then, is this: where the legal high priests entered through the material tabernacle, prepared by human hands, into the holy of holies, likewise material and prepared by human hands, Christ entered through a far more excellent tabernacle, into holy places also far more outstanding, namely the heavens themselves. So, speaking of this kind of tabernacle, he rightly says that Christ entered through a tabernacle much greater and more perfect into the holy places. Indeed the tabernacle through which Christ entered is greater than that old one, because the whole multitude and breadth of believers, of whom the Church consists, extends more widely than that narrow tabernacle made of tents. Moreover it is far more perfect, because the law, as was said in chapter seven, brought nothing to perfection; and likewise, as was just said, the gifts and sacrifices offered in the legal tabernacle could not make the worshipper perfect as to conscience. Thirdly he adds, "not made with hands": the legal tabernacle, with all its equipment, was constructed by human work and art, but the Church is gathered only by God himself and the Holy Spirit. Therefore it is rightly added, stating it briefly and generally, that it is in no way of this construction, that is, material, external, carnal, temporal, and not lasting long. Thus the particle "this" [ταύτης], I think, points to whatever excellent thing can be made in this world, so that the sense is: that holy place is in no way of this world, just as the Old Testament, as said above, had a worldly holy place. So also concerning the heavens, in 2 Corinthians 5 we have a dwelling not made with hands, but eternal, in the heavens. Through such a tabernacle, then, Christ entered into the holy places, into the second tabernacle, namely the heavens. Hence it is quite clear that these antitheses are set very elegantly, to amplify the dignity of the tabernacle through which Christ entered, and there is no need for a longer discourse to show that these descriptions fit the Church very well.

units.la: Neq; per sanguinem hircorum aut vitulorum, sed per proprium sanguinem De sanguine vituli, & de sanguine hirci inferedo in sancta supra exposuimus, quantum satis est, producto loco ex Leuitic. 16.
units.tr: "Nor through the blood of goats and calves, but through his own blood." Concerning the blood of the calf and of the goat carried into the holy places, we have explained above as much as is enough, citing the passage from Leviticus 16.

units.la: Leuitic. 16. Apparet plurali numero dixisse hircorum ac vitulorum, partim contemptu quodam (sic enim per contemptum dicimus, quid mihi commemoras Marios, Catilinas, Syllas?) partim ad ostendendum tacitè, quòd, quamlibet multa eiusmodi offerrentur, tamen nulla essent respectu sanguinis Christi, nihilq; prorsus illa per se efficere. Habet autem Emphasin vox proprium, sicut alias solent inculcare, tradidit Christus semetipsum, suum corpus, ac mirificè commendatur ea voce sacrificij Christi excellentia, quòd videlicet non alienum, sed proprium sanguinem obtulerit. Praeterea Christi insignis charitas, iuxta illud Ioan. 15. Maiore hac dilectionem nemo habet, ut quis animam suam ponat pro amicis suis. Semel, opponitur ei, quod dictum est, pontifice semel in anno ingressum: Christus dicitur semel in vniuersum ingressus: quandoquidem non potuit nisi semel ingredi, sicut ad finem huius capitis ostenditur. Sic vero 1. Petri 3. & Roman. 6. Christus semel mortuus est pro peccatis nostris.
units.tr: Leviticus 16. He says "of goats and calves" in the plural, partly with a certain contempt (for so we speak contemptuously: "why do you mention to me Marius, Catiline, Sulla?"), and partly to show tacitly that however many such things were offered, they would still be nothing compared with the blood of Christ, and could accomplish nothing at all by themselves. The word own carries emphasis, as they are accustomed to stress elsewhere: Christ "gave himself up, his own body"; and the excellence of Christ's sacrifice is remarkably commended by this word, namely that he offered not another's blood but his own. Also, there is Christ's remarkable love, according to John 15: "Greater love has no one than this, that someone lay down his life for his friends." Once is set against what was said, that the high priest entered once a year: Christ is said to have entered once for all, since he could enter only once, as is shown at the end of this chapter. Thus also 1 Peter 3 and Romans 6: Christ died once for our sins.

units.la: Aeterna redemptione reperta) Ecce hic effectus illius sanguinis, siue iustificatio sequens ex tali cultu longè praestantior omnibus iustificationib. carnis. Quod dicit redemptione (λύτρωσις redemptio est & precium redemptionis) omninò plus notat, quàm si diceret iustificatione: quodq; addit aeternam, maius est, quàm iustificatio carnis. Notat autem voce redemptionis omninò maximam vim sanguinis Christi, nempe quòd per eum qui captiui ac serui erant, fuerint iterum in libertatem restituti: quae figura sermonis passim occurritin explicando mysterio salutis humanae per Christum partae, sumptaque est ab ijs, qui vel depositum, vel amissum quid precio recuperant. Matth. 20 & Marci 10. Filius hominis non venit, ut sibi ministraretur, sed ut ipse ministraret, utq; daret animam suam redemptione pro multis. 1. Corinth. 1. Factus est nobis sapientia à Deo, iustitiaq; & sanctificatio, & redemptio. Hanc porrò redemptionem cū dicit aeternam, manifestum est, spiritualem esse, quae post hac quoq; vitâ retineat suam uim: igitur & haec vox amplificat. Quod deniq; dicitur hanc redemptionem repertam, siue quòd Christus eam inuenerit, pulchrè notatur, iustificationem nostram esse gratuitâ, nullis nostris meritis vel viribus comparatâ, sed solius Dei bono consilio atq; ordinationi asscribendam. Sumpta est forma loquendi à deliberatibus, & qui in variis cōsilijs vnum aliquod inueniunt cōmodius, idq; eligunt. Sic enim & Deus è multis modis, quibus potuisset humanum genus liberare, iudicauit omnium expedientissimum, ut per mortem filij id fieret, sicut capite secundo huius epistolae dictum est, Decebat enim ut, &c. Itaq; omnia haec posita mirabiliter illustrant id, quod per Christum in nouo testamento factum est, & nulla propè vox est, quae non amplificationem aliquam in se habeat. Atq; haec quidem satis pro partium explicatione. Iam quae ad doctrinam vel consolationem ex his colligenda sunt, operaeq; precium est breuiter ostendamus, necnon &plenius exponamus typicè de Christo, ea quae in tabernaculo legali visa sunt. Primùm quando in veteri testamento dicitur cultus, iustificationes, et sanctum fuisse: & in secunda parte collationis adiectum est, eadem omnia haberi in nouo testamento, sed multò praestantiora: habemus hic & comprehensa omnia, quae in veteri lege sunt summa. Secundò vero illud ad doctrinam nobis notandum est, quia locus tabernaculi priore fui parte vocatur Sanctum, posteriore verò parte sancta sanctorum, non ita accipienda esse, quasi loco ulli per se insit sanctitas, vel ex loco posit sanctitas parari, sed sancta sanctorum dicuntur à sanctis operibus, quae ibi fiunt: alias vbicunque quis sit, locus sanctus est, quatenus ipse, quod sanctū est, facit. A Deo quidem, qui omnia implet, & vbiq; est, omnis locus sanctus est: caeterum ubi nos quoq; bene agimus, videlicet peccata confitendo, Deū inuocando audiendo verbū Dei, is locus singulariter pro sancto apud nos agnoscitur. Ideo Solomō aedificaturus templum hoc praefabatur 1. Reg. 8. quòd domus illa non posset eum capere, cùm nec coeli coelorum eum caperent. Interea tamen Deus electo illi populo voluit tandem locum prescribere, quo adorari vellet: non quidem, quòd vno loco potius ageret, quàm alio: sed partim ut testimonii externum haberetur de voluntate Dei erga populū illum, quòd videlicet apud eum maximè coli vellet: partim ut populus, pro ut rudis erat & rebus externis erudientibus, tanto magis moueretur ad vnius Dei cultum: partim ut hac ratione auocarentur ab idololatria & ritu erigendi passim altaria, vel excogitandi dimersos cultus, sicut ante legem latâ homines passim incipiebant (si enim vno loco cultus praescriptus esset, profuturū istud erat ad continendum omnes in religionis vnitate: quo licet aliquid videre Iosuae 22.) Hinc legimus Deute. 12 praecepta de non offerendo alibi, quàm in loco electo. Ad arcâ Dei quasi sedè Dei omnes oraturi se couertebât, post verò Hierosolymam se conferebant, deportata nimirum eò arca Dei: ad eundem locum oculos detorserunt oraturi in captiuitate Babylonica, id quod ex Danielis historia liquet.
units.tr: Having found eternal redemption: Here is the effect of that blood, or the justification that follows from such worship, which is far more excellent than all the justifications of the flesh. The word redemption (λύτρωσις [lytrōsis], meaning redemption and also the price of redemption) signifies far more than if he had said justification. Calling it eternal adds still more, since it exceeds the justification of the flesh.
