units.tr: Moreover, here we learn, first, that we must remain in our calling and firmly determine that God will be with us in all things, provided we ourselves are not idle. Thus we see Moses did, who did not reject his calling, although at first his successes seemed unhappy. All fine and excellent things are difficult at the start; and God sometimes wishes to see the faith and diligence of his people, and in a manner to test them. But if he sees them steadfast and using his gifts rightly, dispensing their talents well, he increases those gifts and multiplies them, according to the promises of the Gospel, Matt. 25.

units.la: Secundò, discimus non metuenda pericula, quæ à tyrannis impendent. Simus vigiles in nostra vocatione, certum est, Deus dabit media, per quæ omnia in nobis complebuntur, quæ ipse ad suam gloriam debere perfici ordinauit. Siue velit fuga, siue immutatione cordis tyrannorum, siue alia ratione, siue etiam morte nostra, ipse nobis & gloriæ suę consulet.
units.tr: Second, we learn not to fear the dangers that threaten from tyrants. Let us be watchful in our calling; it is certain that God will provide the means by which all those things will be accomplished in us which he has ordained should be carried out for his glory. Whether he wills flight, or a change of heart in tyrants, or some other way, or even our death, he will provide for us and for his own glory.

units.la: Hoc sciuit Moses noster, hoc sciuit Elias sub Achab & Iezabel. Primo libro Regum decimoōctauo & decimonono, &c.
units.tr: Our Moses knew this, and Elijah knew it under Ahab and Jezebel. In the first book of Kings, chapters eighteen and nineteen, etc.

units.la: Per fidem fecit Pascha, & effusionem sanguinis, ne is, qui perimebat primogenita, tangeret ipsos.
units.tr: By faith he kept the Passover and the sprinkling of blood, so that the one who destroyed the firstborn would not touch them.

units.la: Quarta probatio fidei Mosi, à ritu celebrati paschatis, in quo illud erat mirabile exercitium fidei, quòd, vbi sanguis agni foret illitus postibus, ibi primogenita ab angelo percutiente non læderentur.
units.tr: The fourth proof of Moses' faith is taken from the rite of celebrating the Passover, in which there was that wonderful exercise of faith: where the blood of the lamb had been smeared on the doorposts, the firstborn were not harmed by the destroying angel.

units.la: Nota est historia Exodi vndecimo: Moses iussu Domini annunciat Pharaoni, futurum, vt ni dimittat populum, interficiatur omne primogenitum tam hominum, quàm iumentorum in terra Aegypti: Israelitarum autem primogenita fore tuta à periculo. Cumque Pharao ne hac quidem ratione moueretur ad dimittendum populum, Dominus ordinauit signum, quo notarentur aedes Israelitarum, distinguerenturque ab aedibus Aegyptiorum: quo item certi omnes redderentur de sua liberatione. Instituitur, per singulas familias mactari agnum immaculatum, anniculum: huius sanguinem fasciculo hyssopi asper gi ad domorum postes in foribus: tum accinctos & habentes baculos in manibus, stantesque eo agno asso vesci, vt mox abituros: se interea lustraturum vniuersam Aegyptu, & per singulas domos interfecturum primogenita: quo malo permoti Aegyptij itatim vltrò iuberent, rogarentque Israelitas, ut cum omnibus suis & pecudibus, & aliis rebus discederent, imò adderent etiam lubenter vasa & vestes, & quicquid huiusmodi petirent. Praecipue autem spectanda verba in eo capite sunt haec: sic comedetis illum: Renes vestros accingetis, & calciamenta habebitis in pedibus, tenentes baculos in manibus, & comedetis festinantes. Est enim Pascha, id est, transitus Domini. Nam transibo per terram Aegypti in nocte illa, & percutiam omne primogenitum in terra Aegypti, ab homine vsq; ad iumentum, & in cunctis Diis Aegypti faciam iudicia, ego Dominus. Quoniam igitur primùm Moses ipse credidit hisce verbis Domini, statuitque hac ratione, per sanguinem videlicet agni notandas aedes, vt forent tutae: deinde mox etiam liberandū populum: merito fides eius hic praedicatur: & quando ipse Moses alijs quoque eadem annunciauit, omnis populus etiam iure credidit verbis Domini. Ac Dominus quoq; quod dixerat, impleuit opere. Nam sequitur eodem capite: Factum est, in noctis medio percussit Dominus omne primogenitum in terra Aegypti, à primogenito Pharaonis, qui in solio eius sedebat, vsque ad primogenitum captiuae, quae erat in carcere, & omne primogenitum iumentorum. Surrexitq; Pharao nocte, & omnes serui eius, cunctaq; Aegyptus, & ortus est clamor magnus in Aegypto: neq; enim erat domus, in qua non iaceret mortuus. Vocatisq; Pharao Mose & Aaraone nocte, iussit eos cum omnibus suis egredi, & cum gregibus, & armentis: populusque etiam vrgebat: necnon vasa aurea, argentea, item vestes lubenter accommodabant: atque ita eo ipso die statim egressi sunt filij Israel sexcenta fere milia peditum virorum, absque mulieribus & paruulis, & innumerabili & iam vulgo, quòd se illis adiunxit: postquam quadringentos triginta annos in Aegypto filij Israel vixissent. Recte igitur Mosi fides praedicatur, quòd ita credens verbis Domini pascha celebrarit, euentumque talem expectarit.
units.tr: The story is well known from Exodus chapter 11. At the Lord's command, Moses announces to Pharaoh that, unless he lets the people go, all the firstborn, both of men and of cattle, in the land of Egypt will be killed, but the firstborn of the Israelites will be safe from danger. When Pharaoh was still not moved to let the people go even by this, the Lord ordained a sign by which the houses of the Israelites were marked and distinguished from the houses of the Egyptians, and by which all would be assured of their deliverance. It was instituted that each family should slaughter a lamb without blemish, a yearling, and sprinkle its blood with a bunch of hyssop on the doorposts and lintels of the houses. Then, girded, with staves in their hands, they were to eat the roasted lamb standing, as those about to depart at once, while he himself would pass through all Egypt and strike the firstborn in every house. Moved by this calamity, the Egyptians would at once willingly urge and beg the Israelites to leave with all their people, flocks and other goods, and would even gladly add vessels, garments and whatever else of this kind they asked for. The words in that chapter especially to be noted are these: "Thus you shall eat it: you shall gird up your loins, and have your shoes on your feet, holding staves in your hands, and you shall eat in haste. For it is the Passover, that is, the passing over of the Lord. For I will pass through the land of Egypt in that night, and will strike every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from man to beast, and against all the gods of Egypt I will execute judgments: I am the Lord." Since Moses himself first believed these words of the Lord, and in this way established that the houses were to be marked with the blood of the lamb so that they would be safe, and then soon also that the people would be freed, his faith is rightly praised here. And since Moses announced the same things to others as well, the whole people also rightly believed the words of the Lord. The Lord too fulfilled in deed what he had said. For it follows in the same chapter: "It came to pass at midnight that the Lord struck every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh who sat on his throne to the firstborn of the captive who was in the prison, and every firstborn of the cattle. Pharaoh rose up in the night, and all his servants, and all Egypt; and a great cry arose in Egypt, for there was no house in which there was not a dead man." Pharaoh then called Moses and Aaron by night and ordered them to go out with all their people, with flocks and herds. The people also pressed them, and the Egyptians willingly lent gold and silver vessels and garments. So on that very day the children of Israel set out, about six hundred thousand men on foot, besides women and little ones, and a countless mixed multitude that joined them, after the children of Israel had lived in Egypt four hundred and thirty years. Rightly, then, Moses' faith is praised, in that, believing the words of the Lord, he celebrated the Passover and awaited such an outcome.

units.la: Quauis statuere debemus, Mosen & reliquos omnes non vsque adeò defixos fuisse hde sua in nudum illud signum, de notandis sanguine agni aedibus: sicut neque sanguinis ipsi feruandi vim tribuerunt: sed potius speculasse per fidem in rem significatam, hoc est, in veram & spiritualem liberationem, pertinentem ad salutem animarum, nempe eä qnae perficienda erat in posterum per sanguinem immaculati agni Christi, per quem omnes credentes ex Aegypto in terrā promissam, id est, è uita nostra aerumnosa & peccatis obnoxia, ad vitam coelestem & aeternā erant ducendi.
units.tr: Yet we may suppose that Moses and all the others were not so fixed on that bare sign, on the marking of the houses with the blood of the lamb, any more than they attributed to the blood itself the power to save. Rather, through faith they looked on the thing signified, that is, the true and spiritual deliverance pertaining to the salvation of souls, namely that which was to be accomplished in time to come through the blood of the immaculate Lamb, Christ, through whom all believers were to be led out of Egypt into the promised land, that is, from our troubled life, subject to sins, into the heavenly and eternal life.

units.la: Itaq; ingens sacramentum latens in esu agni paschatis, percusione Aegyptiorum, & liberatione Israelitarum latebat: & patres sine dubio per fidem cōtemplati iunt spiritualia, quae per Christum postea sunt adimpleta. Sic autem Ioannes euangelista cap. 19. & Apostolus 1. Cor. 5. agnum illum typum fuisse Christi clarè docet, & patribus omnia in figura contigisse, 1. Cor. 10. Ac possemus nos etiam latius explicare, quomodo, quae in illo agno paschali considerantur, etiam in Christo sint adimpleta: sed nos aliàs fere id ostendimus, & res per se ipsam non adeò difficilis. Item de signis, & natura signorum tam in veteri, quàm in nouo testamento, possent hic multa dici.
units.tr: Thus a great sacrament lay hidden in the eating of the Passover lamb, in the striking of the Egyptians and the deliverance of the Israelites. The fathers, undoubtedly contemplating these spiritual things by faith, saw them afterwards fulfilled through Christ. John the evangelist in chapter 19, and the Apostle in 1 Cor. 5, clearly teach that that lamb was a type of Christ, and 1 Cor. 10 teaches that all things happened to the fathers in figure. We could also explain more fully how the things considered in that Passover lamb have been fulfilled in Christ, but we have shown this nearly enough elsewhere, and the matter is not in itself very difficult. Likewise, much could be said here about signs and the nature of signs, both in the Old and in the New Testament.

units.la: Discimus hic, quod credere debeamus, Deum nos liberaturum ex particulis Aegyptiacis, etiam illis medijs, de quibus minimè suspicamur. Item, quòd Deus dum percutit impios, pios seruat etiam in medio impiorum.
units.tr: We learn here that we ought to believe that God will deliver us from the Egyptian plagues, even from those intermediate ones of which we least suspect. We learn too that while God strikes down the wicked, he preserves the godly even in the midst of the wicked.

units.la: Iam discimus, gratias agere Deo, & memores esse nostrae liberationis, sicut illud pascha erat illis commissum celebrandum in monimentum, in sempiternum.
units.tr: Further, we learn to give thanks to God and to remember our deliverance, just as that Passover was committed to them to be celebrated as a memorial for ever.

units.la: Per fidem transierunt mare rubrum, veluti per siccam terram, quod cum tentaf- sent Aegyptij, absorpti sunt.
units.tr: Through faith they passed through the Red Sea as though on dry land, but when the Egyptians attempted it, they were swallowed up.

units.la: Quinta probatio fidei Mose, ab eo, quod credidit, viam sibi aperiendam, vbi nulla ratione id fieri posse apparebat, & vbi caeteri omnes plane desperabant: vt clare scribitur Exodi 14. Ita vero hic praedicatur fides Mosi, vt tamen ad alios quoque communis latus redeat, eorundemque fides simul praedicetur, qui Mosi nomine Dei certum promittenti auxilium lubenter crediderunt. Et conueniebat ita alios coniungi ipsi Mosi, quando in re adeo magna, & nullo modo secundum humanam rationem expectanda simul graui simis exercitati sunt tentationibus & in fide pariter confirmati. Nota est historia Exo. 14. vbi Israelitae, qui Deo duce & autore ex Aegypto egresi fuerat, ad mare rubrum pe- uenissent, & Pharaone cum exercitu insectante, in summas angustias essent redacti, & neque regredi, neque progredi possent, clamauerunt ad Deum, dixerunt-que ad Mosen: An, quod non essent sepulchra in Misraim, tulisti nos, ut moreremur in deserto? quid hoc fecisti nobis, vt educeres nos ex Misraim? Nonne hoc ipsum est, quod dicebamus tibi in Misraim, dicentes: Cessa a nobis, vt seruiamus Aegyptijs? Nam melius erat nobis, seruire Aegyptijs, quàm mori in deserto.
units.tr: The fifth proof of Moses' faith is that he believed a way would be opened for him where, by no reasoning, it could seem possible, and where all the others utterly despaired, as is plainly written in Exodus 14. Yet the faith of Moses is set forth in such a way that it also extends to the others who shared his lot, and their faith is praised at the same time: those who gladly believed that the help Moses promised in God's name was certain. It was fitting that others be joined to Moses in this way, since in a matter so great, and not to be expected by any human reckoning, they were together exercised by very severe temptations and likewise strengthened in faith. The story is well known from Exodus 14. When the Israelites, who had come out of Egypt under God as their leader and author, had reached the Red Sea, and Pharaoh with his army was pursuing them, they were brought into the greatest distress. They could neither go back nor go forward. They cried out to God and said to Moses: "Did you take us away to die in the wilderness because there were no graves in Misraim? What have you done to us, leading us out of Misraim? Is this not what we said to you in Misraim, when we said: 'Leave us alone, that we may serve the Egyptians'? For it was better for us to serve the Egyptians than to die in the wilderness."

units.la: Et ibidem Dominus ad Mosen: Eleua virgam tuam, & extende manum tuam super mare, & scinde illud, & ingrediantur filij Israel intra mare per aridâ. Et paulo post, Et extendit Moseh manum suam super mare, & recedere fecit Iehouah mare vento orientali vehementi tota nocte, posuitque mare in siccum, & iam scissae erant aquae. Ingresi sunt igitur filij Israel inter mare, per aridam, & aquae eius erant murus à dextera & à sinistra eorum. Haec historia est transitus per mare rubrum, cuius etiam mentio fit, psalm. 78 & 114. Iosuae 4.1. Corinth. 10.
units.tr: And there the Lord said to Moses: "Lift up your rod and stretch out your hand over the sea, and divide it, and let the children of Israel go into the sea on dry ground." And a little later: "Then Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and Iehovah caused the sea to recede by a strong east wind all night, and made the sea dry land, and the waters were divided." So the children of Israel went into the midst of the sea on dry ground, and its waters were a wall to them on their right hand and on their left. This story of the passage through the Red Sea is also mentioned in Psalms 78 and 114, Joshua 4 and 1 Corinthians 10.

units.la: Aclicet aliqua ex parte incredulitatis Israelitę hic insimulantur, quando metu periculi instantis ad Aegyptum respexerunt, ibique mori se maluisse dixerunt: attamen imbecillitas haec fidei non derogat verbis apostoli, dicentis, per fidem transiisse patres per mare rubrum, velut per siccam terram. Ἀλγονιγία haec fuit Israelitarum, antequam ex verbo Dei, per Mosen, & Angelum castra praecedentem essent corroborati: Audita autem Dei promissione & visa columna nubis, quae profectionis diuinae certissimum erat signum, audacter & magna animi fiducia alueu maris sunt ingresi, non diffidentes, quin Deus patrum potenti sua manu ipsos esset educturus. Pertinet huc, quod apostolus 1. Corint. 10. de Israelitis hisce refert, quòd sub nube fuerint, per mare transierint, & eandem esca spiritualem comederint, & omnes eúdem potum spirituale biberint: bibebant n. inquit, de spirituali, comitanti petra, petra verò erat Christus. Ex quo patet, multos eorum fide habuisse, licet plures illorum Deus non approbarit. Patet hinc, quomodo sancti & electi Dei pericula effugere, & Dei ope ductuque emergere possint. Fit hoc nimirum ope & gratia Dei, quę per fidem est apprehendenda. Exempla plura vide in historia Noahi, Lothi, Dauidis. Item Actor. 12. & in historia euangelica, aliisque locis innumeris.
units.tr: Although in some respect the Israelites are here charged with unbelief, when in fear of the imminent danger they looked back toward Egypt and said that they would rather die there, this weakness of faith does not detract from the apostle's words, which say that the fathers passed through the Red Sea as though on dry land by faith. This despondency [ἀθυμία] was the Israelites' before they were strengthened by the word of God through Moses and by the angel going before the camp. But when they had heard God's promise and seen the pillar of cloud, which was the most certain sign of the divine going forth, they entered the bed of the sea boldly and with great confidence of spirit, not doubting that God would lead them out by his mighty hand, as he had done for their fathers. To this belongs what the apostle reports in 1 Corinthians 10 about these same Israelites: that they were under the cloud, that they passed through the sea, that they all ate the same spiritual food and all drank the same spiritual drink. For, he says, they drank of the spiritual rock that followed them, and the rock was Christ. From this it is clear that many of them had faith, although God did not approve of many of them. It is also clear how the saints and elect of God can escape dangers and emerge by God's help and guidance. This indeed happens by the help and grace of God, which is to be laid hold of through faith. See more examples in the histories of Noah, Lot and David, likewise in Acts 12, in the Gospel history, and in countless other places.

units.la: Quod cum tentassent Aegyptij, absorpti sunt) Illustrat fidem Israelitarum, per contentionem adijciendo euentum incredulorum Aegyptiorum. Hi enim cum insequeretur Israelitas, & pariter transituros se ad eadem putarent, fluctibus maris coeuntis sunt absorpti. Locus extat Exod. 14. Vbi inter alia sic legitur: Reuersae sunt aquae, & operuerunt currus & equites, vniuersum exercitu Pharoh, qui ingresus fuerat post eos in mare, non remansit ex eis usque ad vnum. At filij Israel ambulauerunt per siccum intra mare, & aquae eis erant murus à dextera & à sinistra eorum: et seruauit Iehouah die illo Israelem è manu Aegyptiorū: viditq; Israel Aegyptios mortuos ad littus maris. En diuersum facinus Dei, alios videlicet, qui vocanti credunt & obediunt, seruantis & mirabiliter à periculo ecclesiam liberantis: incredulos verò & reprobos hostes opprimentis. Interitus calamitosus hoc loco depingitur omnium hostium & persecutorum ecclesiae. Omnes tyranni & impij hanc fortem subire coguntur. At licet interdum in terris Dominus illis parcat, perunt tamen aeternum. Sic Antiochus Epiphanes à Deo prosternatur, dum à Hierosolymitanorum & templi excidium cursu contendit. Exercitus numerosus Assyriorū ante moenia Hierosolymitana profligatur ab angelo Domini. Senacherib rex à filijs trucidatur. Saul graufisimus hostis ecclesiae à Philistaeis opprimitur, adeò vt sibi ipsi desperatas manus afferat. Achab in Syrorum manus traditur, domus eius penitus excinditur. Herodiana gens Christi ecclesiae semper infesta à Deo extirpatur. Pereunt illi à flamma ignis, qui socios Danielis in fornacem coniecerant, Dan. 3. Diluuio perit mundus improbus & genus Caini. Pereunt incendio coelitus Sodomitae: ita Deus semper & seruat ecclesiam. & & perdit hostes atq; inimicos suos.De quo plura lege in historijs sacris & libris propheticis atque apostolicis.
units.tr: "When the Egyptians attempted it, they were swallowed up." The author illustrates the faith of the Israelites by setting beside it, as a contrast, the outcome for the unbelieving Egyptians. For these, pursuing the Israelites and thinking that they too would cross over by the same way, were swallowed up by the waves of the sea as it closed in. The passage is found in Exodus 14, where among other things it is read thus: "The waters returned and covered the chariots and the horsemen, the whole army of Pharaoh that had gone into the sea after them; not one of them remained, not even one. But the children of Israel walked on dry ground in the midst of the sea, and the waters were a wall to them on their right hand and on their left. So Iehovah saved Israel that day out of the hand of the Egyptians, and Israel saw the Egyptians dead on the shore of the sea." Here we see the different outcome of God's deeds: on the one hand, those who believe and obey the one who calls them, whom he preserves and wonderfully rescues from danger, the church; on the other hand, the unbelieving and reprobate, whom he crushes as enemies. The calamitous destruction of all enemies and persecutors of the church is depicted in this place. All tyrants and wicked men are compelled to undergo this same lot. But although the Lord sometimes spares them on earth, they perish eternally. So Antiochus Epiphanes was overthrown by God while he hastened toward the destruction of Jerusalem and the temple. A numerous army of the Assyrians was routed before the walls of Jerusalem by the angel of the Lord. King Sennacherib was slain by his sons. Saul, the most grievous enemy of the church, was overwhelmed by the Philistines, so that he laid violent hands on himself in despair. Ahab was delivered into the hands of the Syrians, and his house was utterly cut off. The Herodian family, always hostile to the church of Christ, was rooted out by God. Those who had thrown Daniel's companions into the furnace perished by the flame of fire, Daniel 3. The wicked world and the race of Cain perished in the flood. The Sodomites perished by fire from heaven. Thus God always preserves the church and destroys its enemies and foes. Read more about this in the sacred histories and in the prophetic and apostolic books.

units.la: Per fidem mœnia Hiericho conciderunt circundata ad dies septem.
units.tr: By faith the walls of Jericho fell down, being compassed about for seven days.

units.la: Nonum exemplum de Iosua per fidem iustificato. Probatio sumpta est ab eo, quòd crediderit verbis Dei, promittentis nouum & inauditum genus victoriæ, ad occupandam munitissimam & quasi inexpugnabilem vrbem Hiericho.
units.tr: The ninth example, of Joshua, who was justified by faith. The proof is taken from the fact that he believed the words of God, who promised a new and unheard-of kind of victory for taking the very strong, and almost impregnable, city of Jericho.

units.la: Historia describitur Iosuæ 6. hisce verbis: Hiericho clausa erat atq; munita ob timorem filiorum Israel, & nullus egredi audebat aut ingredi. Dixitq; Dominus ad Iosue, Ecce, dedi in manus tuas Hiericho, & regem eius, omnesque fortes viros. Circuite vrbem cuncti bellatores, semel per diem, sic facietis sex diebus: septem autem sacerdotes tollent septem buccinas, tubas arietinas, precedentes arcam fœderis, & in die septimo circuibitis ciuitatem septem vicibus, clangentq; sacerdotes cum tubis. Et cum prolixiorem fecerint sonum cum cornu arietino, & vos audieritis vocem buccinæ, vociferabuntur omnes populi iubilo magno, & corruet murus ciuitatis subter eam, ascendentq; populi, qui isq; contra faciem suam. En, qualis modus obtinendæ victoriæ: certè quod ad clangorem cornuum conciderent muri, videtur æquè absurdum, atque si diceretur, Amphionis concurrisse lapides, coniunctosq; in Thebarum muros: de quibus Propertius libro tertio: Saxa Cytheronis Thebas agitata per artem Sponte sua in muri membra coiisse ferunt.
units.tr: The story is described in Joshua 6 in these words: "Jericho was shut up and fortified because of the children of Israel, and no one dared to go out or come in. And the Lord said to Joshua, 'See, I have given into your hand Jericho, and its king, and all its mighty men. Go round the city, all you fighting men, once a day; so you shall do for six days. But seven priests shall carry seven trumpets of rams' horns before the ark of the covenant, and on the seventh day you shall go round the city seven times, and the priests shall blow the trumpets. And when they make a long blast with the ram's horn, and you hear the sound of the trumpet, all the people shall shout with a great shout, and the wall of the city will fall down beneath them, and the people shall go up, every man straight before him.'" Behold what a manner of winning victory this is! Surely it seems as absurd that the walls should fall at the sound of horns as if one said that stones came together of their own accord and joined into the walls of Thebes, of which Propertius in his third book says: "They say the stones of Cithaeron, moved by art, came together of their own accord into the members of a wall of Thebes."

units.la: Et tamen quamlibet absurdum istud videbatur, & minimè conueniens, (quandoquidem multis aliis modis potuisset parari victoria, vbi tanta erat bellicosorum virorum copia, & tam consternati imbelles, hostes:) lubenter credidit Iehosua Deo promittenti, & iubenti fieri, statimq; opere est præceptum Dei executus.
units.tr: Yet however absurd that seemed, and quite unfitting (since victory could have been won by many other means, where there was such a multitude of warlike men and the enemy were so dismayed and unwarlike), Joshua gladly believed God, who promised and commanded it, and at once carried out the command of God in action.

units.la: Sic aut placuit Deo, inusitato modo victoriam suo populo concedere, vt hostes caeteri terrerentur, seseq; citius dederent: præcipuè autem ut Israelitæ in fide confirmantur. Videntes enim, quanta Dominus in gratiam populi stupenda signa ederet, merito debebant commoueri ad credendum, Deum semper velle erga ipsos misericordem, nec non promissa omnia adimplere. Quia ergo hic fides Iehosua in prima victoria ita emicuit, merito hinc arripitur occasio fidem eius celebrandi. Potuissent quidem & ex aliis præclaris actionibus Iehosuæ argumenta diuersa colligi, ad fidem ipsius comprobandam, veluti ex eo, quòd credebat, & prædicabat, Deum velle alueum Iordanis permeabilem reddere Iehosuæ 3. Item in capiunda vrbe Hai, vbi eleuando clypeum iussu Dei, certus factus est de victoria: Iosuæ 8. Item in expugnatione Gabaon, vbi ad votum eius steterunt sol & luna, donec vincerer, cap. 10.
units.tr: Thus it pleased God to grant victory to his people in an unusual manner, so that the other enemies might be terrified and surrender the sooner, but chiefly so that the Israelites might be confirmed in faith. For seeing what marvellous signs the Lord performed for the sake of his people, they ought rightly to be moved to believe that God always wishes to be merciful to them and to fulfil all his promises. Therefore, since Joshua's faith shone forth so clearly in this first victory, the occasion is rightly seized to celebrate his faith. Indeed, arguments to confirm his faith could have been drawn from his other notable deeds: for example, from the fact that he believed and proclaimed that God would make the channel of the Jordan passable (Joshua 3); likewise in taking the city of Ai, where, lifting the shield at God's command, he was made certain of victory (Joshua 8); likewise in the capture of Gibeon, where at his word the sun and moon stood still until he might conquer (ch. 10).

units.la: Sed istud reuera, quod Apostolus hoc loco commemorat, etiam valde excellens est, & ideo iustius prædicandum, quòd ad primam historiam pertinens ostendat, illum semper ab initio mirabili fide præditum. Deinde eiusmodi est, ut cætera ex eo secuta posint intelligi. Qui enim aduertit primam illam illustrem victoriam fidei attributam, idem pro tinus intelliget, reliquas quoque victorias fidei esse tribuedas. Etiam si addi potest, ideo quoque istud celebrari præ cæteris, quòd in hoc typum Christi Iosue gesserit clarissimum. Nam Hiericho, quæ vox significat lunam, rectè significat, mundum hunc instar lunæ varium & inconstantem, aliunde accipientem, si quid habet splendoris. Hic expugnandus est per Christum, sicut ipse dicit: Confidite, ego vici mundum: Sed, quomodo expugnatus? Non armis, aut sapientia humana, sed solo clangore cornuum atrietinorum, hoc est, prædicatione verbi, quod prædicarunt Apostoli 1. Corinth. 10. Arma nostra non sunt carnalia, &c.
units.tr: But that which the Apostle recalls in this place is truly most excellent, and therefore more rightly proclaimed, because, belonging to the first history, it shows that he was endowed with wonderful faith from the beginning. Moreover, it is of such a kind that the rest that followed from it may be understood. For whoever notices that this first illustrious victory is ascribed to faith will at once understand that the remaining victories are likewise to be ascribed to faith. It may also be added that this one is celebrated above the others because in it Joshua bore the clearest type of Christ. For Jericho, a word which means moon, rightly signifies this world, changeable and inconstant like the moon, receiving from elsewhere whatever splendour it has. It is to be conquered through Christ, as he himself says: "Be of good cheer, I have overcome the world." But how is it conquered? Not by arms or human wisdom, but by the sound of the ram's horns alone, that is, by the preaching of the word, which the apostles preached (2 Corinthians 10): "Our weapons are not carnal," etc.

units.la: Proinde est hic mirabilis effectus fidei, quòd per fidem obtinetur victoria in bello: sicut videmus Iosuæ obtinuisse. Et certè qui bella gerunt, præsertim iustis de causis suscepta, fide in Deum plus efficient, quàm omni sapientia & potentia humana. Exemplum habemus etiam 1. Samuel. 14. in Ionatha, qui dicebat armigero suo, Non est Domino difficile saluare vel in multis, vel in paucis. Et Iosaphat. 2. Paralipomen. 20. vbi exercitum instruxisset ad pugnam, Credite in Domino Deo vestro, & securi eritis, credite prophetis eius, & cuncta venient prosperà. Et pasim alibi extant eius modi exempla. Sed &nos, si quando certandum est, vt semper certandum est contra mundum, sataṅam: fide potissimum armabimur: 1. Ioan. 5. Hæc est victoria, quæ vincit mundum, fides nostra. Ephes. 6. Super omnia assumite scutum fidei, quo possitis omnia iacula ignita mali illius extinguere.
units.tr: Therefore this is a wonderful effect of faith, that victory in war is obtained through faith, as we see Joshua obtained it. And indeed those who wage war, especially wars undertaken for just causes, accomplish more by faith in God than by all human wisdom and power. We have an example also in 1 Samuel 14 in Jonathan, who said to his armour-bearer, "It is not difficult for the Lord to save, whether by many or by few." And in Jehoshaphat (2 Chronicles 20), who, when he had drawn up his army for battle, said: "Believe in the Lord your God, and you will be secure; believe his prophets, and all things will go well." Such examples are found everywhere else too. But we also, if ever we must contend, as we must always contend against the world and Satan, shall be armed chiefly with faith: "This is the victory that overcomes the world, our faith" (1 John 5). "Above all, take up the shield of faith, with which you can quench all the fiery darts of that evil one" (Ephesians 6).

units.la: Per fidem Rahab meretrix non periit, vnà cum his, qui non obedierant, cum excepisset hospitio exploratores pacificè.
units.tr: Through faith Rahab the harlot did not perish with those who had not obeyed, when she had received the spies peaceably into her house.

units.la: Decimum exemplum de Rahab meretrice per fidem iustificata: Probat autem fidem eius ab eo, quòd exploratores missos à Iosua exceperit hospitio pacificè, hoc est, cum quærequærerentur à ministris regijs, non prodiderit, sed suo etiam periculo seruarit, certò statuens & confitens, quòd Dominus populo suo traditurus esset terram Chanaan. Qua certè in re, ipsa fidem in ea, quæ de misericordia Dei erga populum Israeliticum narrari audierat, coniecit, atque etiam persuasum habebat, se posse per misericordiam Dei vnà cum populo illo seruari. Verba confessionis eius sic habent Iosue 2. Noui, quod Dominus tradiderit vobis terram: etenim irruit in nos terror vester, & elanguerunt omnes habitatores terræ. Audiuimus, quòd Dominus siccauerit aquas maris rubri ad vestrum introitum, quando egressi estis ex Aegypto, & quæ feceritis duobus regibus Amorrhæorum, qui erant trans Iordanem, Sihon & Og, quos interfecistis. Et hæc audientes perimuimus, & elanguit cor nostrum, nec remansit in nobis spiritus ad introitum vestrum. Dominus enim Deus vester, ipse est Deus in cœlo sursum, & in terra deorsum. Nunc ergo iurare mihi per Dominum, vt, quomodo ego misericordiam feci vobiscum, ita & vos faciatis cum domo patris mei, detisque mihi verum signum, vt saluetis patrem meum, & matrem, fratres ac sorores meas, & omnia quæ illorum sunt, & eruatis animas nostras à morte. Quibus verbis eleganter fides, eiusque ortus, officium, effectusque describuntur. Primùm, narrat, se audiuisse, quæ alibi gesta fuerant. Fides enim ex auditu. Deinde sequitur agnitio peccati, à timore & metu periculi, & ab exemplo aliorum punitorum. Accedit mox confessio: Dominus Deus uester ipse est Deus. Hinc ad fidem venitur, Iurate mihi per Dominum, &c. Et ipsa etiam suæ hdei effectus experta est: quamobrem Apostolus diserte addidit: Non periit vna cum his, qui non obedierant. Merito ergo fides Rahab celebratur, dignamque putauit apostolus, quam vna cum patribus celebraret. An autem meretrix fuerit & infamis mulier, in dubio est. Hebraicè habetur [?] quæ vox significat potius præparatricem ciborum, & hospitium aperientem mulierem: à verbo [?] vel [?] quod significat, cibauit: vnde & [?] item [?] cibus, esca, alimonia: septuaginta habent [?] scortum, quę vox ducta videtur à [?], id est, vędo, quòd hisce mulierculis pudor & libido venalis sit.
units.tr: The tenth example is of Rahab the harlot, justified by faith. The author proves her faith from the fact that she received the spies sent by Joshua peaceably into her house. That is, when they were sought by the king's servants, she did not betray them but, at her own risk, kept them safe, firmly resolving and confessing that the Lord would give the land of Canaan to his people. In this matter she had certainly drawn her faith from what she had heard about God's mercy towards the Israelite people, and she was persuaded that she could be saved together with that people through God's mercy. The words of her confession are as follows in Joshua 2: "I know that the Lord has given you the land, for terror of you has fallen upon us, and all the inhabitants of the land have melted away. We have heard how the Lord dried up the waters of the Red Sea for you when you came out of Egypt, and what you did to the two kings of the Amorites beyond the Jordan, Sihon and Og, whom you destroyed. Hearing these things, we were afraid, and our hearts melted, nor did any spirit remain in us because of your coming. For the Lord your God, he is God in heaven above and on earth beneath. Now therefore swear to me by the Lord that, as I have shown kindness to you, so you will do with my father's house, and give me a sure sign that you will save my father and mother, my brothers and sisters, and all that belongs to them, and deliver our souls from death." In these words faith, its origin, its duty and its effects are elegantly described. First, she says that she had heard what had been done elsewhere, for faith comes by hearing. Then follows the acknowledgement of sin, out of fear and dread of danger and from the example of others who were punished. Soon comes the confession: "the Lord your God is God." From this she comes to faith: "Swear to me by the Lord," and so on. She also experienced the effect of her faith, which is why the Apostle expressly added: "she did not perish with those who had not obeyed." Rightly, then, the faith of Rahab is celebrated, and the apostle thought her worthy to be celebrated along with the fathers. Whether she was a harlot and an infamous woman, however, is doubtful. The Hebrew word here signifies rather a preparer of food, and a woman who opens her house to guests. It comes from the verb meaning to feed, whence also the word for food, nourishment, sustenance. The Seventy render it by a word meaning a whore, which seems to be derived from the verb meaning to sell, because modesty and lust are for sale to such women.

units.la: Quanquā vox vendendi ad res honestas etiam referri potest, quarum vsus & contrarius minimè turpis est: sic meretricis & tabernæ meritoriæ phrasis non statim in deterius rapi debent. Meretrix enim dici ea potest, quæ pro ære vel mercede aliquid facit: tandem de iis vsurpatum est vocabulum, quæ ex corpore etiam mercedem & quæstum faciunt. Vt ut hoc sit, multa præclara in exemplo huius Rahab nobis & ad doctrinam & ad consolationem sunt præscripta.
units.tr: Yet the word for selling can also refer to honourable matters, whose use and opposite are by no means shameful; so the phrases for a harlot and a brothel should not be at once taken in the worse sense. For a harlot may be called anyone who does something for money or wages; and at last the word has been applied to those who make gain even from their bodies. However this may be, many excellent lessons are set before us for teaching and for comfort in the example of this Rahab.

units.la: Primùm discimus, tutissimam ac certissimam viam effugiendi iram Dei, & calamitates temporarias atque æternas, in fide esse positam: sic Noah mundi communem interitum declinauit, dum Deo credidit, & iuxta mandatum eius arcam extruxit. Qui verò increduli sunt & Deum tentant, in periculis hærent & infœlices exitus sortiuntur. Rahab seruatur: ciues eius pereunt. Noah protegitur in arca, incredulus mundus suffocatur. Loth ducitur ex Sodomis per fidem. Sodomitæ verò cœlitus delentur.
units.tr: First, we learn that the safest and most certain way of escaping the wrath of God, and both temporal and eternal calamities, lies in faith. Thus Noah escaped the common destruction of the world while he believed God and built the ark according to his command. But those who are unbelieving and tempt God remain in dangers and meet unhappy ends. Rahab is preserved; her fellow citizens perish. Noah is protected in the ark; the unbelieving world is suffocated. Lot is led out of Sodom by faith; the Sodomites are destroyed from heaven.

units.la: Secundò, ad effugiendi hanc viam pœnitentiæ & emendationis studium debet adiungi: nisi enim veteris fermenti sordibus eiectis noua creatura homo fiat, saluus fieri nequit. Id quod ex Ioannis Baptistæ, Christi, & apostolorum concionibus patet. Et memorabile est illud Matth. 3. vbi Ioannes Baptista ad Pharisæos & Saducæos, Progenies viperarum, quis vobis submonstrauit, vt fugeretis à ventura ira? Facite igitur fructus, qui deceant pœnitentiam, &c. Luc. 3. Ioan. 1. 3. Actor. 2. 3. 1. Cor. 5. & alibi loci ea de re extant quamplurimi. Impœnitentes verò iram Dei incurrunt. Matthæi vicesimo tertio, Luc. 13. 19. Roman. 11.
units.tr: Second, to this way of escape the pursuit of repentance and amendment must be joined. For unless man, with the leaven of the old sourness cast out, becomes a new creature, he cannot be saved. This is clear from the sermons of John the Baptist, of Christ and of the apostles. Memorable is that passage in Matthew 3, where John the Baptist says to the Pharisees and Sadducees: "You brood of vipers, who showed you how to flee from the coming wrath? Bring forth therefore fruits worthy of repentance," and so on. Luke 3; John 1; Acts 2 and 3; 1 Corinthians 5; and very many other places in Scripture speak of this matter. Those who do not repent, however, incur the wrath of God: Matthew 23; Luke 13; Romans 11.

units.la: Tertiò, Deus misericors est, & peccatores in gratiam recipit resipiscentes: non vult mortem peccatoris, sed vt conuertatur ac viuat. Sic Christus Ioan. 8. non condemnat mulierculam, quæ stuprum commiserat, sed uetat, ne pari siue eodem peccato iterum se polluat. Sic cum publicanis & peccatoribus conuersatus est, vt eos in via meliore reduceret. In veteri testamento quamplurima gratiæ diuinæ exempla occurrunt. Niniuitis resipiscentibus Deus parcit, quibus per Ionam prophetam interitum denunciarat. Iudaicam gentem resipiscentem ab exilio Babylonico reducit & veteri libertati restituit. Petrus resipiscens à Christo benigno vulto afficitur. Iudæis per resipiscentiam redit datur ad gratiam Dei, teste Petro Actor. 2. & 3. De misericordia Dei Scriptura sacra passim concionatur. Quapropter non opus est, de hac plura adiicere. Si enim meretrici genti fuit benignus per gratiam: quanto magis electis suis?
units.tr: Third, God is merciful, and receives repentant sinners into grace: he does not will the death of the sinner, but that he should turn and live. Thus Christ in John 8 does not condemn the woman who had committed adultery, but bids her not to defile herself again with the same or a like sin. Thus he associated with tax collectors and sinners, so as to lead them back into the better way. In the Old Testament very many examples of divine grace occur. God spared the Ninevites when they repented, though through the prophet Jonah he had announced their destruction. He brought back the Jewish nation, repenting, from the Babylonian exile and restored it to its former liberty. Peter, repenting, was received with a kind countenance by Christ. Access to the grace of God is given to the Jews through repentance, as Peter bears witness in Acts 2 and 3. Holy Scripture preaches everywhere of the mercy of God, so there is no need to add more on this. For if he was gracious to a harlot nation, how much more will he be to his elect?

units.la: Quarto, non est Deo respectus personarum, sed in quacunq; gente qui Deum timet, & operatur iustitiam, & credit verbo eius, acceptus & gratus est. Id quod elegater D. Petrus Act. 10. & Paulus Galat. 3. Coloss. 3. explicat.
units.tr: Fourth, there is no respect of persons with God, but in whatever nation the one who fears God, works righteousness and believes his word is acceptable and pleasing to him. Saint Peter in Acts 10 and Paul in Galatians 3 and Colossians 3 explain this admirably.

units.la: Neque hoc ita intelligendum, quasi inter pios & impios non fit Deo discrimen, cùm tamen iustus sit & seuerus iudex improborum, pios verò gratia sua complectatur: de peccatoribus in viam meliorem conuersis accipiendum est, quos Deus pater misericordiæ mirificè prosequitur, & expansis ulnis acipit, teste Christo, Lucæ decimoquinto in parabola de filio prodigo, & Matth.9.11. vbi medicum ægrotantium se profitetur, non robustorum.
units.tr: Nor is this to be understood as if there were no distinction with God between the godly and the ungodly, since he is a just and severe judge of the wicked, but he embraces the godly with his grace. It is to be taken of sinners converted into a better way, whom God the Father of mercies wonderfully pursues and receives with outstretched arms, as Christ testifies in Luke 15 in the parable of the prodigal son, and in Matthew 9:11–13, where he professes himself a physician of the sick, not of the strong.

units.la: 5. Exemplum & typus hic proponitur vocationis gentium, quas Deus aliquando per euangelium ad regnum erat inuitaturus: de qua vocatione plura sunt in prophetis & concionibus noui testamenti. Vide Esa. 2.42.49.52.60. Actor.13. Matth.21.8.Luc.10.1.Petr.2. Psalm.2.72.Luc.2.
units.tr: Fifth, this is set forth here as an example and type of the calling of the Gentiles, whom God was at some time to invite to his kingdom through the gospel. There are many things about this calling in the prophets and in the sermons of the New Testament. See Isaiah 2, 42, 49, 52, 60; Acts 13; Matthew 21:8; Luke 10:1; 1 Peter 2; Psalms 2, 72; Luke 2.

units.la: 6. Rahab confessionem edit de potentia & miraculis Dei, simul ac fidem suam in promissiones commendat. Ita & nos Christum per fidem ampleētemur, & confitebimur coram mundo hoc adultero. De quo plura Matth. duodecimo, Marci octauo, Romanorum decimo, &c.
units.tr: Sixth, Rahab makes a confession of the power and miracles of God, and at the same time commends her faith in the promises. So we too, through faith, shall embrace Christ, and confess him before this adulterous world. Of this more is said in Matthew 12, Mark 8, Romans 10, and so on.

units.la: Et quid praeterea loquor? Deficiet enim me tempus commemorantem de Gedeone, de Barac, & Samsone, & Iephthe, necnon Dauid, & Samuele ac prophetis: qui per fidem expugnauerunt regna, operati sunt iustitiam, assecuti sunt promissionem, occlu serunt ora leonum, extinxerunt vim ignis, effugerunt acies gladij, validi facti sunt ex imbecillitate, effecti sunt robusti in bello, incursiones auerterunt exterorum. Mulieres acceperunt, &c.
units.tr: And what more shall I say? For time would fail me if I told of Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, and also David and Samuel and the prophets: who through faith conquered kingdoms, worked righteousness, obtained the promise, stopped the mouths of lions, quenched the violence of fire, escaped the edge of the sword, were made strong out of weakness, became mighty in war, turned back the armies of foreigners. Women received their dead, and so on.

units.la: Inductionem institutam Apostolus absoluturus, quandoquidem iuxta dialecticorum præceptiones (ut videre est ad finem priorum Analyticorum Aristotelis:) oportet in ea enumerare omnia singularia, aut certè indicare, in omnibus singularibus similibus etiā, quæ non exprimuntur, eandem rationem considerari: significat iam, omnes alios quoq; sanctos patres quicunq; vnquam fuerunt, identidem per solam fidem iustificatos: ut hinc tandem inferat (quemadmodum & facit ad finem capitis) omnes homines quoque per fidem testimonium apud Deum consequi seu iustificari. Sic enim, ut initio quoque admonuimus, se tota habet hæc inductio. Abel est per fidem iustificatus. Enoch est per fidem iustificatus, Noe. Abraham. Sara. Isaac. Iacob. Ioseph. Moses. Iosue. Rahab.
units.tr: The Apostle, about to finish the induction he has set up, since according to the precepts of the dialecticians (as may be seen at the end of Aristotle's Prior Analytics) one must enumerate all the singulars in it, or at least indicate that the same reasoning is to be considered in all similar singulars, even those not expressed, now signifies that all the other holy fathers, whoever they have ever been, were likewise justified through faith alone; so that he may finally infer (as he also does at the end of the chapter) that all men too obtain testimony before God, or are justified, through faith. For the whole of this induction stands thus, as we also admonished at the beginning. Abel was justified through faith. Enoch was justified through faith. Noah. Abraham. Sarah. Isaac. Jacob. Joseph. Moses. Joshua. Rahab.

units.la: Et sic de omnibus aliis quoque patribus, vt Gedeone, Barac, Samsone, Iephthe, Dauide, Samuele, prophetis est iudicandum.
units.tr: And the same must be judged of all the other fathers too, such as Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, David, Samuel and the prophets.

units.la: Igitur omnes homines per fidem iustificantur.
units.tr: Therefore all men are justified through faith.

units.la: Sed apostolo non satis est, uti hac vsitata verborum forma, & sic de omnibus aliis est iudicandum: sed paulò illustrius & rhetorico feré artificio hanc comprehensionem omnium singularium enunciat. Et quid praeterea loquar, inquit, quasi diceret: Non opus est plures commemorare, sumantur quicunq; alij patres, & inuenientur ad vnum omnes eadem via, hoc est, per solam fidem iustificati. Atque iterum ut cupiens paucis omnia complecti, & festinans, patrum quorūdam illustrium recenset saltem nomina: de quibus & paucula commemorabimus, sicut Apostolus quoq; voluit paucis attingere, ne in re nō admodum necessaria, & alias iam satis manifesta auditorem fatigaret ac tædio afficeret.
units.tr: But it is not enough for the Apostle to use the customary form of words, "and the same must be judged of all the others." He sets out this inclusion of every individual in a somewhat more illustrious way, with an almost rhetorical art. "And what more shall I say?" he asks, as if to say: there is no need to recount more. Take any other fathers you like, and they will be found, all of them, by the same way, that is, justified through faith alone. Again, as one who wishes to embrace everything in few words and is hurrying on, he recounts at least the names of certain illustrious fathers. We too shall mention a few of them briefly, as the Apostle also wished to touch on them in few words, so as not to weary and bore the hearer with a matter that is not very necessary and is already sufficiently clear elsewhere.

units.la: De Gedeone) Est in primis & hoc loco obseruandum, quàm prudenter sequatur librorum ordinem: librum Iosua sequitur liber Iudicum, ex quo depromit exempla de Gedeone, Barac, Sampsone, Iephthe. Hunc librum sequuntur libri Samuelis & Regum. Quare de his protinus quoq; subiungit. Tum libri prophetarum, quorum itidem vna voce mentionem facit. Sciendum autem, alios etiam prædicari in libris Iudicum, quorum res extant præclarae per fidem gestae: sed Apostolo satis est, paucos & magis illustres, inque oculos positos obiter commemorare. Inter hos verò facile princeps extitit vnus Gedeō.
units.tr: Concerning Gideon: here too it must be observed how prudently he follows the order of the books. The book of Joshua is followed by the book of Judges, from which he draws his examples about Gideon, Barak, Samson and Jephthah. The books of Samuel and Kings follow that book, so he adds these immediately afterwards. Then come the books of the prophets, which he likewise mentions in a single word. It should be noted, however, that others too are praised in the book of Judges, whose notable deeds were done through faith. But it is enough for the Apostle to mention in passing a few of the more illustrious, placed before the eyes. Among these, Gideon easily stands out as the foremost.

units.la: De quo tametsi dici queat, quòd visus sit initio, cùm vocatus esset ad munus liberādi populum è seruitute Midianitarum, qui populum iam per septem annos grauissimè oppressé presserant, vacillare, petedo videlicet signum, primùm ab angelo in sacrificio, postea bis in vellere (sic autem solent animi etiam piorum primùm sentire luctas spirituales, & petere à Deo, vt dignetur ipsos confirmare) tamen in hoc emicuit valde insignis fides Gedonis, quòd verbis Domini sequentibus credidit & paruit. Cùm enim conuenissent ad triginta millia virorum, vt pugnarent contra Midianitas, Dominus iusit, vt domum remitteret omnes meticulosos & trepidantes: vnde manserunt duntaxat decem millia.
units.tr: Of him it can be said that at first he seemed to waver when he was called to the task of freeing the people from the servitude of the Midianites, who had for seven years heavily oppressed them. He asked, namely, for a sign: first from the angel at the sacrifice, and afterwards twice with the fleece. (For thus the minds even of the pious are wont first to feel spiritual struggles, and to ask God that he would deign to confirm them.) Nevertheless, the faith of Gideon shone out very remarkably in this, that he believed and obeyed the words of the Lord that followed. For when some thirty thousand men had assembled to fight against the Midianites, the Lord ordered that all who were fearful and trembling be sent home, and so only ten thousand remained.

units.la: Sed adhuc maius est, quod sequitur: Dominus iusit hos decem mille deduci ad aquas, ut biberent, atque ibi eos tantùm, qui manu haurientes aquam biberent, seligi ad expeditionem: hi autem visi sunt trecenti, cùm omnes reliqui ore suo prostrati aquas sorbe- rent. Hos autem trecentos adhuc eduxit tubas habentes, & complodentes lagenas, nec nō gestantes faces. Hoc novo genere armorum & pugnæ instructus Gedeo aulus media nocte aggredi innumerabilem (sicut arena maris) exercitum Madianitarum & Amalecytharum. Istud autem quomodo potuisset aggredi aut sperare, nisi amplissima fuisset fide præditus, qua statuere poterat, Deum sibi fore propitium, & daturum victoriam? Et in hoc exemplo tentationes credentium sunt propositæ: item auctus & incrementa fidei: denique & fidei mirabiles effectus.
units.tr: But what follows is greater still. The Lord ordered these ten thousand to be led down to the waters to drink, and that only those who drank the water by scooping it up in their hands should be chosen for the expedition. Three hundred were found, while all the rest, prostrate, drank the water with their mouths. These three hundred he then led out, holding trumpets and smashing jars, and also carrying torches. Equipped with this new kind of arms and fighting, Gideon dared to attack by night the innumerable army of the Midianites and Amalekites, like the sand of the sea. But how could he have undertaken this, or hoped for it, unless he had been endowed with the fullest faith, by which he could be confident that God would be propitious to him and would give him the victory? In this example the temptations of believers are set before us, likewise the growth and increase of faith, and finally the wonderful effects of faith.

units.la: Possemus autem totam hanc historiam victoriæ Gedeonis allegoricè, vel ethicè explicare, sed nequaquam opus est. Vide Oecolampadiū, item Primasium, & Augustinum tomo 10. valde copiosè. Est tamen minimè praetereunda quaestio, quam attingit hic Chrysostomus. Qui fit, quòd Apostolus hos celebret, quorum tamen constat plerosque turpiter lapsos. Veluti Gedeon peccauit toties signum petendo, & tentando Deum, sicut ipse fatebatur, se tentare Deum: Iudicum 6. item faciendo Ephod, in quo fornicatus est omnis Israel: Iudicum 8. Itè superhumerale seu cinctorium, cuius vsus erat in sacris: item Samson, qui interfecit semetipsum? Respondetur: Primùm merito ponit eos, quia ipsorum fides valde insignis fuit, & digna, quæ proponeretur in exemplum: sicut fides aliorum patrum. Secundò, licet vita eorum alicubi visa sit culpanda, tamen hic quæstio est de fide, non de vita. Neque ex vita vel operibus est iustitia, sed ex fide. Exempla sunt in Magdalena, Matthæo, Zachæo, Latrone, Petro, Paulo, &c. Et cùm etiam sancti aliquando ad tempus labantur, tamen rursus per fidem exiguntur, quemadmodū cernere licet in Davide. Tertiò, vt etiam ceciderint aliquando, tamen probabile est postea resipuisse, poenitentiam egisse, & conuersos denuò ad apprehendendum per fidem Dei misericordiam.
units.tr: We could indeed explain this whole history of Gideon's victory allegorically or morally, but there is no need at all. See Oecolampadius, also Primasius, and Augustine in volume 10, very fully. Yet the question which Chrysostom raises here must by no means be passed over: why does the Apostle praise these men, of whom it is clear that most fell shamefully? For example, Gideon sinned in asking for a sign so many times and tempting God, as he himself confessed, that he was tempting God (Judges 6); also in making an ephod, in which all Israel played the harlot (Judges 8); likewise the shoulder-cloth or girdle, whose use was in sacred things; likewise Samson, who killed himself. The answer is: first, he rightly lists them, because their faith was very remarkable and worthy to be set forth as an example, as is the faith of the other fathers. Second, although their life may somewhere seem blameworthy, the question here is about faith, not about life. Righteousness comes not from life or works but from faith. Examples are found in Mary Magdalene, Matthew, Zacchaeus, the thief, Peter, Paul, and others. And although the saints sometimes stumble for a time, yet again they are raised up through faith, as may be seen in David. Third, even if they sometimes fell, it is probable that afterwards they came to their senses, repented, and, converted once more, laid hold through faith on God's mercy.

units.la: Quod attinet ad factum Gedeonis, videndus illius animus: parauit is signum memoriale habitæ à Deo victoriæ. Quòd populus postea abusus fuerit, & cultum superstitiosum exhibendo peccarit, (sicut hodie colitur vestis Christi) certè non magis videtur Gedeoni imputandum, quàm Deo ipsi imputabitur, quòd populus etiam peccauerit in serpente æneo, temporibus Iosiæ. Sed Scriptura apertè dicit, factum ipsi & domui eius. Quare non est simile factum Gedeonis.
units.tr: As for the deed of Gideon, his intention must be considered: he prepared a memorial of the victory received from God. That the people afterwards abused it and sinned by offering superstitious worship (as Christ's garment is venerated today), this certainly seems no more to be imputed to Gideon than it will be imputed to God himself that the people also sinned with the bronze serpent in the times of Josiah. But Scripture plainly says that the thing became a snare to him and to his house. Therefore Gideon's deed is not similar.

units.la: De Barac) Hic antecesfsit tempore, Iudicum 4. Gedeon tamen prior est dignitate, propter factorum excellentiam. Hic Barac filius Abinoam obtinuit victoriam aduersus Siseram ducem exercitus Iabin regis Chanaan, qui tum per viginti annos grauiter oppresserat Israelitas. Ostendit autem hic fidem suam, quando credidit & obediuit voci Deboræ prophetissæ, quæ dicebat, ipsum à Deo designatū, per quē adiūctis sibi decem millibus pugnatorum, populus foret liberandus. Etiamsi ipse Sisera interfectus est à muliere Iahel vxor Heber Cenæi: quod factum, quia ipse noluit suscipere munus iniunctū à Deo per prophetissam, nisi ipsa quoque ad expeditionem sequeretur. Iterum hic exemplum tentationum, & effectus fidei.
units.tr: Concerning Barak: he came earlier in time (Judges 4), but Gideon is prior in dignity on account of the excellence of his deeds. This Barak, son of Abinoam, obtained the victory against Sisera, the commander of the army of Jabin king of Canaan, who had for twenty years heavily oppressed the Israelites. He showed his faith when he believed and obeyed the voice of Deborah the prophetess, who said that he had been designated by God, and that through him, with ten thousand fighting men joined to him, the people would be set free. Although Sisera himself was killed by the woman Jael, wife of Heber the Kenite, this happened because Barak was unwilling to accept the task enjoined on him by God through the prophetess unless she also followed him on the expedition. Here again is an example of temptations and of the effect of faith.

units.la: De Sampsone) Et in hoc liberatore Israelitarum è manu Philistinorum, licet conspicere præclaros effectus fidei, præsertim, quando etiam, antequam nasceretur, per angelum nunciatum est, futurum eum liberatorem Israelis, & Nazaræum, id est, dedicatum Domino: deinde, quando toties inculcatur, eum impulsu Domini & spiritus Sancti pleraque omnia fecisse. Mysterij erat & fidei, quòd peteret sibi dari vxorem Philistinam: diserte enim ait Scriptura, à Domino id factum, vt ita haberetur occasio agendi cōtra Philistinos: (Christus hoc mysterio significabatur adiuncturus sibi gentes) Mysterij item & fidei erat, quòd leonem aggrederetur & interficeret: interfectio leonis victoriam Christi contra Satanam, qui est leo rugiens (1. Petr. 5.) designat. Mysterij item & fidei erat, quòd portas cum postibus & seris Gazæ noctu abstulerit. Fidei erat, quòd traditus Philistæis, funes, quibus ligatus erat, ruperit, & arrepta mandibula asini mille Philistinos interfecerit.
units.tr: Concerning Samson: in this deliverer of the Israelites from the hand of the Philistines one may clearly see the effects of faith, especially when, even before he was born, it was announced by an angel that he would be the deliverer of Israel and a Nazirite, that is, dedicated to the Lord; and then when it is so often repeated that he did most things by the impulse of the Lord and the Holy Spirit. It was a mystery and an act of faith that he asked to be given a Philistine wife, for Scripture expressly says that this was done by the Lord, so that there would thus be an occasion for acting against the Philistines. (By this mystery Christ was signified as going to join the Gentiles to himself.) It was also a mystery and an act of faith that he attacked and killed the lion; the killing of the lion signifies Christ's victory over Satan, who is the roaring lion (1 Pet. 5). It was also a mystery and an act of faith that he carried off the gates of Gaza by night, with their posts and bars. It was an act of faith that, when he was handed over to the Philistines, he broke the cords with which he was bound and, seizing the jawbone of an ass, killed a thousand Philistines.

units.la: Postremò & insignis fidei erat, quòd, postquam captiuus & exæcatus esset per Philistinos, atque omnibus ludibrio expositus, in ædibus, ad quas conuenerant omnes principes, & ad tria fere millia hominum, implorata diuina ope domus columnas concussi fleris ferit,& ruina ędiu omnes occiderit,plures (vt Scriptura loquitur) interficiens moriens, quâ interfecerat viues.Quo, inquam,sperassset,se posse talia efficere,nisi fidem habuisset, Deum sibi vires additurum?quamobrem & præmisit inuocationem,quæ cùm exaudita est,certum est ex fide profectam.
units.tr: Lastly, it was also a remarkable act of faith that, after he had been taken captive and blinded by the Philistines and exposed to mockery by all, he, in the house to which all the princes and some three thousand people had gathered, implored divine help, shook the pillars of the house and struck them, and by the fall of the building killed all at once. In dying he slew more (as Scripture puts it) than he had slain while living. For what, I ask, would he have hoped, that he could accomplish such things, unless he had had faith that God would add strength to him? Therefore he also put forward an invocation, and when this was heard, it is certain that it proceeded from faith.

units.la: Neque est,quòd contendat quispiam,Samsonem vt interfectorem suiipsius damnâdum,& ex desperatione potius,quàm fide id fecisse. Palàm enim est ex ijs,quæ antecesserunt de vocatione ipsius à Deo ad liberandum populum:item ex inuocatione,quæ fa-ctum illud præcessit,ex fide id eum fecisse.Præterea, quando instinctu spiritus Sancti id fecit,sicut cætera quoque:mors illata ad peccatum ipsi non imputatur. Aliud enim est, se temerè & sine vocatione in periculum mortis conijcere:aliud vocationi diuinæ ad id per Spiritum impellenti obedire. Neque licet conferre mortem ipsius cum morte Catonis vel similiu. Qua de re vide Augustinum de ciuitate Dei,lib.1.cap.21. & 26.& contra epistolam Gaudentij lib.2.cap.23.
units.tr: Nor is there reason for anyone to contend that Samson should be condemned as the killer of himself, and that he did it from despair rather than from faith. For it is plain from what came before, concerning his calling by God to free the people, and also from the invocation which preceded that deed, that he did it from faith. Moreover, since he did it by the prompting of the Holy Spirit, as he did the other things, the death he brought on himself is not imputed to him as sin. For it is one thing to throw oneself rashly and without a calling into mortal danger, and another thing to obey a divine calling that impels one to this through the Spirit. Nor is it right to compare his death with the death of Cato or the like. On this matter see Augustine, On the City of God, book 1, chapters 21 and 26, and Against the Letter of Gaudentius, book 2, chapter 23.

units.la: Discimus in hisce: primò,quemadmodum Sancti periculis subinde exponantur,& tamen Dominus eos tandem liberet.
units.tr: From these things we learn, first, how the saints are sometimes exposed to dangers, and yet the Lord at last delivers them.

units.la: Deinde de faciendis ijs,quæ vocationi conueniunt, etiam cum vitæ discrimine, doctrina hic est propositá.
units.tr: Second, the teaching here is that what belongs to one's calling must be done, even at the risk of life.

units.la: De Iephte) Samson celebratus est ante Hiephthae,licet hic præcesserit tempore,& pro pter excellentiam emicuisse fidem Iephte, licet colligere, tum ex oratione , quam per legatos habere voluit ad regem Ammonitarum,tum ex eo,quòd Iudicum 10.dicitur Spiritus Domini in eum infilisse,& cum precatione ac voto aggressum oppugnare hostes, quorum occupauit viginti ciuitates.Cæterum de voto Iephte,& quòd filiam immolauerit, multa quidem Augustinus quæstionum super vetus testamentum lib.1. Item primo libro de ciuitate Dei cap.21.Sed non probatur mihi: magis arridet explanatio loci huius apud Lyranum:item apud Brentium in librum Iudicum. Hieronymus etiam in Hieremiae cap.7.scribens concedit,filiam oblatam & immolatam more pecudum,dicit; animum offerentis placuisse,licet non sacrificium. Ac votum Iephte ait inconsideratum, nec filiam debuisse in vitam obedire. Vide si placet. Lectu enim dignissimus est locus.
units.tr: On Jephthah) Samson is celebrated before Jephthah, although Jephthah came earlier in time. From the speech he wished to deliver through envoys to the king of the Ammonites, and from Judges 10, where it is said that the Spirit of the Lord came upon him, and that he attacked and assaulted the enemies with prayer and a vow, and took twenty of their cities, one can gather that the faith of Jephthah was outstanding. As for Jephthah's vow, and that he sacrificed his daughter, Augustine has many things in his Questions on the Old Testament, book 1, and likewise in book 1 of The City of God, chapter 21. But I do not approve of them. I prefer the explanation of this passage given by Lyra, and likewise by Brenz on the book of Judges. Jerome too, writing on Jeremiah chapter 7, concedes that the daughter was offered and slaughtered like cattle, and says that the mind of the one offering pleased God, though not the sacrifice. He calls Jephthah's vow ill-considered, and says the daughter ought not to have been made to obey it with her life. See it if you wish; the passage is well worth reading.

units.la: Dauid)De Dauide potest multa referri:sed illud inprimis memorabile,& fide clarissimum testimonium,quòd pugnauit & superauit Goliath.1 Sam.17. Certè verba ipsius Dauidis egregiam fidem exprimunt:Dominus, inquit,qui eripuit me de manu leonis,& de manu vrsi,ipse me liberabit de manu Philistæi huius: et verba eius ad Goliath, Tu venis ad me cum gladio,& lancea,& clypeo:ego verò venio ad te in nomine Domini exercituum Dei acierum Israelis,quem probris affecisti. Hodie tradet te Iehouah in manum meam, & percutiam te,atque auferam caput tuum à te, daboque cadauera castrorum Philisthim hodie volatilibus cœli,& bestijs terræ,& subijcit,& cognoscent omnes habitatores terræ,quòd est Deus Israeli. Scietque vniuersa congregatio ista,quòd non gladio & lancea saluum facit Iehoua,(Iehouae enim est bellum)& tradet vos in manum nostram,&c. Item fides Dauidis eluxit in liberatione Ceilæ oppidi, ab oppugnatione Philistinorum, primo Samuelis vicesimo tertio. Fidem ostendit,quàdo Saulem potuit occidere,& non occidit,sperans,se verè per Deum liberandum,primo Samuelis vicesimo quarto abscidit oram vestis,primo Samuelis vicesimo sexto abstulit scyphum aquæ & lanceam.Fide cõprehendit latrunculos Amalecythas,primo Samuelis tricesimo. Iterum fide percussit Philistæos,secundo Samuelis quinto.Sed & plures insignes victorias obtinuit,secundo Samuelis octauo. Ac tandem promisiones ad ipsum factæ sunt, quòd ex ipso nascetur Christus,quibus & credidit. Satis est hæc breuiter attigisse. Sunt multa, in quibus Dauidis fides potest celebrari:item in quibus Dauid etiam typum Christi gesisit: ex quibus etiam multiplex doctrina ad pietatem & mores conducens posset colligi.
units.tr: David) Much can be related about David, but the most memorable thing, and the clearest testimony to his faith, is that he fought and overcame Goliath (1 Samuel 17). Indeed David's own words express an outstanding faith: "The Lord who delivered me from the paw of the lion and from the paw of the bear, he will deliver me from the hand of this Philistine." And his words to Goliath: "You come to me with sword, spear and shield, but I come to you in the name of the Lord of hosts, the God of the armies of Israel, whom you have defied. Today Jehovah will deliver you into my hand, and I will strike you down and cut off your head from you, and I will give the corpses of the Philistine camp today to the birds of the sky and the beasts of the earth, and all the inhabitants of the earth will know that there is a God in Israel. And all this assembly will know that Jehovah saves not with sword and spear, for the battle is Jehovah's, and he will deliver you into our hand," and so on. Likewise David's faith shone in the rescue of the town of Keilah from the attack of the Philistines (1 Samuel 23). He showed his faith when he could have killed Saul and did not, hoping that he would truly be delivered by God (1 Samuel 24, where he cut off the corner of Saul's robe). In 1 Samuel 26 he took the cup of water and the spear. By faith he seized the Amalekite raiders (1 Samuel 30). Again by faith he struck the Philistines (2 Samuel 5). He also won several notable victories (2 Samuel 8). And finally the promises were made to him, that Christ would be born of him, and he believed them. It is enough to have touched on these briefly. There are many instances in which David's faith can be celebrated, and in which David also bore the type of Christ; from these a manifold teaching conducive to piety and morals could also be gathered.

units.la: Samuel)Huius fides ostenditur etiam diuersis locis, at clarissimè primo Regum duodecimo,vbi commemorat,quanta beneficia Dominus Israeli contulerit,simulque iubet eos à Domino expectare adhuc misericordiam.
units.tr: Samuel) His faith is shown in various places, but most clearly in 1 Samuel 12, where he recounts how many benefits the Lord conferred on Israel, and at the same time bids them to expect mercy still from the Lord.

units.la: Prophetis)Intelligit prophetas,qui temporibus Regum, & deinceps ita sunt appellati: qui omnes fidem suam multis modis declararunt:ut Nathan,Elias,Helisæus, Michæas, Esaias,Hieremias. Sequitur:
units.tr: Prophets) He means the prophets, who from the time of the kings onward were so called. All of them declared their faith in many ways: Nathan, Elijah, Elisha, Micah, Isaiah, Jeremiah. There follows:

units.la: Qui per fidem expugnauerunt regna, operati sunt iustitiam, assecuti sunt promissiones, obstruxerunt ora leonum, extinxerunt vim ignis, effugerunt acies gladij, va-lidi lidi facti sunt ex imbecillitate, effecti sunt robusti in bello, incursiones auerterunt, mulieres acceperunt ex resurrectione mortuos suos, &c.
units.tr: Who through faith subdued kingdoms, wrought righteousness, obtained promises, stopped the mouths of lions, quenched the power of fire, escaped the edge of the sword, out of weakness were made strong, became mighty in war, turned back invading armies, women received their dead raised to life again, etc.

units.la: Nolens lectorem onerare enumerandis pluribus nominibus, addit insignes aliquot & maxime memorabiles effectus fidei: quod his de causis prudentissime videtur facere. Primo enim proponit effectus fide adhuc alios & valde excellentes, quàm hactenus relatos, qui in ijsdem patribus, & proximè, & paulo etiam ante nominatis spectari adhuc potuerunt, non tamen omnes pluribus verbis exponi.
units.tr: Not wishing to burden the reader by listing many names, he adds some outstanding and most memorable effects of faith. He seems to do this most wisely, for these reasons. First, he sets forth further effects of faith, and very excellent ones, beyond those related so far, which could still be seen in the same fathers, both those recently and somewhat earlier named, yet not all of them can be expounded at length.

units.la: Secundò, tacitè suggerit omnium animis multorum aliorum patrum, qui hactenus non sunt nominati, memoriam, in quibus hi effectus, quos hic recensèt, maximè emicuerunt. Tertiò prodest, vt finem facturus Inductionis institutæ, vim omnem fidei alarius ponat ob oculos, necnon dignitatem eius amplificet, illustretq;.
units.tr: Secondly, he tacitly suggests to the minds of all the memory of many other fathers, not so far named, in whom these effects that he now recounts shone most brightly. Thirdly, as he is about to finish the induction he has undertaken, he serves to set before the eyes the whole force of faith, and also to amplify and illustrate its dignity.

units.la: Quartò, hac ratione omnes excitare vult ad fidem multò alacrius amplectendam & constantius tuendam. Quodq; hoc modo postremo loco dicitur, altius animis imprimitur, & inhaeret diutius. Etsi verò hi effectus admodum praeclari sint, & plane dignissimi, de quibus copiosè dicatur, tamen quia ex ijs, quae hactenus à nobis exposita sunt, plerique clarius possunt intelligi. & quiuis praeterea potest per se ratione quandam eodem modo exponendi eos accipere. Praeterea, quia opus est nos progredi ad huius partis finem faciendum: ideò nos nihil aliud, quàm breviter indicabimus, in quibus patribus primum suprà nominatis, deinde non nominatis hi effectus spectari debeant.
units.tr: Fourthly, by this method he wishes to stir everyone to embrace faith much more eagerly and to defend it more steadfastly. And what is said in this final place is impressed more deeply on the mind and cleaves to it longer. Although these effects are very distinguished and fully worthy of being discussed at length, nevertheless, since most of them can be understood more clearly from what we have already set out, and anyone can by his own reasoning grasp in the same way how to explain them, and since we must press on to finish this part, we will only briefly indicate in which of the fathers named above, and then in those not named, these effects ought to be looked for.

units.la: Expugnauerunt regna) Hic effectus fidei maximè eluxit in Iosue: ut videre est toto libro, quo res gestae ipsius perscribuntur, praecipueq; cap. 12. Item in Gedeone, Iephte, Dauide. Nam à Dauide superati sunt Syri, Moabitae, Ammonitae, &c.
units.tr: They subdued kingdoms) This effect of faith shone most clearly in Joshua, as is evident throughout the book that records his deeds, and especially in chapter 12. Likewise in Gideon, Jephthah and David; for the Syrians, Moabites, Ammonites, etc. were overcome by David.

units.la: Operati sunt iustitiam) Dupliciter intelligi id potest: vel, vt proximè sequitur expugnationem regnorum, & adiunctum est heroicæ fortitudini, ac tum erit sententia: eos expugnando regna iustè egisse, nimirum vlcisdendo iniurias illatas nomine Dei, & item populo Dei. Quomodo alias in Scripturis, qui ita egerunt aliquid, recte egisse dicuntur: quo modo & Pinehas imputatum est ad iustitiam, quòd occidisset concumbentem cum Madianitide, Num. 15. Vel certè in genere accipi potest, iustè operatos sanctos patres, quando nihil contra ius ac fas attentarunt, cōtra quenquam, sed in omni vita ea egerunt, quae bonos iustos viros decent. Atq; ita iustud conuenit omnibus sanctis patribus. Neq; hoc pacto ulli faciunt, nisi qui praeclara fide sunt praediti.
units.tr: They wrought righteousness) This can be understood in two ways. Either, as it immediately follows the subduing of kingdoms and is joined to heroic courage, the sense will be that in subduing kingdoms they acted justly, namely by avenging the injuries done in the name of God and likewise to the people of God. In this way in other places of Scripture those who acted so in some matter are said to have acted rightly; thus Phinehas was reckoned to him for righteousness because he slew the man who lay with the Midianite woman (Numbers 25). Or it may be taken in general: the holy fathers acted justly when they attempted nothing against right and law toward anyone, but in all their life did those things that befit good and upright men. And so this righteousness belongs to all the holy fathers. And they do not do this in any way except those who are endowed with outstanding faith.

units.la: Assecuti sunt promissiones) Et istud dupliciter potest intelligi: vno modo, q., qui excellenti fide fuerunt praediti, digni habiti sunt à Deo ad quos promissiones insignes faceret: vt Iuli Abrahamo, Dauidi, & similibus factę sunt egregiae promissiones de semine benedicto exipsis nascituro. Secundo modo, vt sit sententia, plurimos patres propter ingentem fidem etiam accepisse res promissas. Vt Iosue accepit terram promissam: item Abraham spiriualiter vidit adimpletas promissiones. Vidit diem meum, inquit Christus, Ioan. 8. & gauisus est. Item Dauid vidit sedentem super solium regni, &c.
units.tr: They obtained promises) This too can be understood in two ways. In one way, those who were endowed with excellent faith were deemed worthy by God to whom he would make notable promises, as to Abraham, David and similar men, to whom splendid promises were made concerning the blessed seed to be born from them. In the second way, the sense is that many of the fathers, on account of their great faith, also received the things promised, as Joshua received the promised land; likewise Abraham saw spiritually the promises fulfilled. "Abraham saw my day," says Christ, "and rejoiced" (John 8). Likewise David saw one sitting on the throne of the kingdom, etc.

units.la: Occluserunt ora leonum) Hoc inprimis de Daniele accipiendum, qui coniectus in lacum leonum famelicorum, tam hoc per fidem obtinuit, vt ora in ipsum nō aperirent: Daniel. 6. Etiamsi in Samsone Iudic. 14. & Dauide, 1. Samuel. 17. simile quiddam spectari posit, in quorum manibus leones vim omnem nocendi amiserunt, quasi illis occlusum effetos. Si autem de solo Daniele accipiamus, tropicam notabimus esse locutionem, qua, quod ab vno gestum est, sic refertur, tanquam si à pluribus gestum foret: quomodo & Matth. 27. latrones dicuntur conuiciati Christo: cum tamen Lucas referat, tātum vnū id fecisse.
units.tr: They stopped the mouths of lions) This must be understood chiefly of Daniel, who, cast into the den of hungry lions, obtained by faith so that they did not open their mouths against him (Daniel 6). Although something similar may be seen in Samson (Judges 14) and David (1 Samuel 17), in whose hands the lions lost all power to harm, as if their mouths had been shut and stopped up. But if we understand this of Daniel alone, we shall note that it is a figurative expression, by which what was done by one is related as if it had been done by several; so also in Matthew 27 the robbers are said to have reviled Christ, whereas Luke relates that only one did so.

units.la: Extinxerunt uim ignis) De Aarone Numer. 16. qui occurrit, & orauit pro populo, ut incendium, quod murmuratores inuadebat, restingueretur: quatuordecim millia & septingenti consumpti ab igne fuerant. Item de tribus illis coniectis in fornacem ardentem, Ananias, Azaria, Misaele, inquam, Daniel 3.
